Yopi hetu, yopi paccayo vedanāya uppādāya, sopi anicco. Aniccasambhūtā[V 2.0023], bhikkhave, vedanā kuto niccā bhavissati! Saññā aniccā… saṅkhārā aniccā. Yopi hetu yopi paccayo saṅkhārānaṃ uppādāya, sopi anicco. Aniccasambhūtā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā kuto niccā bhavissanti! Viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ. Yopi hetu yopi paccayo viññāṇassa uppādāya, sopi anicco. Aniccasambhūtaṃ, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ kuto niccaṃ bhavissati! Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

18. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, form is impermanent. Whatever cause and whatever condition there is for the arising of form, that too is impermanent. Bhikkhus, form having arisen from what is impermanent—how could it be permanent? Feeling is impermanent. Whatever cause and whatever condition there is for the arising of feeling, that too is impermanent. Bhikkhus, feeling having arisen from what is impermanent—how could it be permanent? Perception is impermanent… Formations are impermanent. Whatever cause and whatever condition there is for the arising of formations, that too is impermanent. Bhikkhus, formations having arisen from what is impermanent—how could they be permanent? Consciousness is impermanent. Whatever cause and whatever condition there is for the arising of consciousness, that too is impermanent. Bhikkhus, consciousness having arisen from what is impermanent—how could it be permanent? Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” Seventh.

8. Sahetudukkhasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Suffering with Cause

19. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ. Yopi hetu yopi paccayo rūpassa uppādāya, sopi dukkho. Dukkhasambhūtaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ kuto sukhaṃ bhavissati! Vedanā dukkhā… saññā dukkhā… saṅkhārā dukkhā… viññāṇaṃ [P 3.0024] dukkhaṃ. Yopi hetu yopi paccayo viññāṇassa uppādāya, sopi dukkho. Dukkhasambhūtaṃ, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ kuto sukhaṃ bhavissati! Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… [T 3.0030] nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

19. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, form is suffering. Whatever cause and condition there is for the arising of form, that too is suffering. Bhikkhus, since form has arisen from suffering, how could it become happiness? Feeling is suffering… perception is suffering… formations are suffering… consciousness is suffering. Whatever cause and condition there is for the arising of consciousness, that too is suffering. Bhikkhus, since consciousness has arisen from suffering, how could it become happiness? Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The eighth.

9. Sahetuanattasuttaṃ

9. With its Cause (Not-Self)

20. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, anattā. Yopi hetu yopi paccayo rūpassa uppādāya, sopi anattā. Anattasambhūtaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ kuto attā bhavissati! Vedanā anattā… saññā anattā… saṅkhārā anattā… viññāṇaṃ anattā. Yopi hetu yopi paccayo viññāṇassa uppādāya, sopi anattā. Anattasambhūtaṃ, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ kuto attā bhavissati! Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Navamaṃ.

20. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, form is not-self. Whatever cause and condition there is for the arising of form, that too is not-self. Bhikkhus, since form has arisen from what is not-self, how could it become self? Feeling is not-self… perception is not-self… formations are not-self… consciousness is not-self. Whatever cause and condition there is for the arising of consciousness, that too is not-self. Bhikkhus, since consciousness has arisen from what is not-self, how could it become self? Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The ninth.

10. Ānandasuttaṃ

10. Ānanda

21. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 2.0024][M 2.0021]… ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘nirodho nirodho’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamesānaṃ kho, bhante, dhammānaṃ nirodho nirodhā (sī. pī.) ‘nirodho’ti vuccatī”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, ānanda, aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammaṃ. Tassa nirodho nirodhā (sī. pī.) ‘nirodho’ti vuccati. Vedanā aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā. Tassā nirodho ‘nirodho’ti vuccati. Saññā… saṅkhārā aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā [P 3.0025] khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā. Tesaṃ nirodho ‘nirodho’ti vuccati. Viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammaṃ. Tassa [T 3.0031] nirodho ‘nirodho’ti vuccati. Imesaṃ kho, ānanda, dhammānaṃ nirodho ‘nirodho’ti vuccatī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

21. At Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove…. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “‘Cessation, cessation,’ it is said, venerable sir. Of which things, venerable sir, is the cessation called ‘cessation’?” “Ānanda, form is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, of a nature to be destroyed, of a nature to vanish, of a nature to fade away, and of a nature to cease. Its cessation is called ‘cessation.’ Feeling is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, of a nature to be destroyed, of a nature to vanish, of a nature to fade away, and of a nature to cease. Its cessation is called ‘cessation.’ Perception… Volitional formations are impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, of a nature to be destroyed, of a nature to vanish, of a nature to fade away, and of a nature to cease. Their cessation is called ‘cessation.’ Consciousness is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, of a nature to be destroyed, of a nature to vanish, of a nature to fade away, and of a nature to cease. Its cessation is called ‘cessation.’ Ānanda, the cessation of these things is called ‘cessation.’” The tenth.

Aniccavaggo dutiyo.

The second chapter on Impermanence.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā, yadaniccāpare tayo;

Hetunāpi tayo vuttā, ānandena ca te dasāti.

Impermanence, Suffering, and Not-Self; three others on ‘What is Impermanent’; three also taught with a Cause; and with the one by Ānanda, they are ten.

3. Bhāravaggo

3. The Chapter on the Burden

1. Bhārasuttaṃ

1. The Burden

22. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 3.0032]… tatra kho [V 2.0025]… “bhārañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi bhārahārañca bhārādānañca bhāranikkhepanañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, bhāro? Pañcupādānakkhandhā tissa vacanīyaṃ. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho; ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhāro”.

22. At Sāvatthī…. There the Blessed One said: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the burden, the bearer of the burden, the taking up of the burden, and the laying down of the burden. Listen to it. And what, bhikkhus, is the burden? ‘The five aggregates subject to clinging,’ it should be said. Which five? The form aggregate subject to clinging, the feeling aggregate subject to clinging, the perception aggregate subject to clinging, the formations aggregate subject to clinging, and the consciousness aggregate subject to clinging. This, bhikkhus, is called the burden.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, bhārahāro[M 2.0022]? Puggalo tissa vacanīyaṃ. Yvāyaṃ āyasmā evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto; ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhārahāro.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the bearer of the burden? ‘The person,’ it should be said. That venerable one of such a name and such a clan—this, bhikkhus, is called the bearer of the burden.

“Katamañca[P 3.0026], bhikkhave, bhārādānaṃ? Yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobhavikā ponobbhavikā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) nandīrāgasahagatā nandirāgasahagatā (sabbattha) tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhārādānaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the taking up of the burden? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting in this and that; that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence. This, bhikkhus, is called the taking up of the burden.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, bhāranikkhepanaṃ? Yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhāranikkhepana”nti.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the laying down of the burden? It is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving, its relinquishment, release, letting go, and non-reliance. This, bhikkhus, is called the laying down of the burden.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna vatvā (sī.) evamīdisesu ṭhānesu sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, further said this:

“Bhārā have pañcakkhandhā, bhārahāro ca puggalo;

Bhārādānaṃ dukhaṃ loke, bhāranikkhepanaṃ sukhaṃ.

“The five aggregates are indeed burdens,

and the person is the bearer of the burden.

Taking up the burden is suffering in the world;

laying down the burden is happiness.

“Nikkhipitvā [T 3.0033] garuṃ bhāraṃ, aññaṃ bhāraṃ anādiya;

Samūlaṃ taṇhamabbuyha taṇhamabbhuyha (pī. ka.), nicchāto parinibbuto”ti. paṭhamaṃ;

“Having laid down the heavy burden,

and not taking up another,

having pulled out craving along with its root,

one is without desire, fully extinguished.” The first.

2. Pariññasuttaṃ

2. Full Comprehension

23. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Pariññeyye ca, bhikkhave, dhamme desessāmi pariññañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katame ca, bhikkhave, pariññeyyā dhammā? Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, pariññeyyo dhammo, vedanā pariññeyyo dhammo, saññā pariññeyyo dhammo, saṅkhārā pariññeyyo dhammo, viññāṇaṃ pariññeyyo dhammo[V 2.0026]. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, pariññeyyā dhammā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, pariññā? Yo, bhikkhave, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, pariññā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

23. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the things to be fully comprehended and full comprehension itself. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, are the things to be fully comprehended? Form, bhikkhus, is a thing to be fully comprehended. Feeling is a thing to be fully comprehended. Perception is a thing to be fully comprehended. Formations are things to be fully comprehended. Consciousness is a thing to be fully comprehended. These, bhikkhus, are called the things to be fully comprehended. And what, bhikkhus, is full comprehension? It is the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion. This, bhikkhus, is called full comprehension.” The second.

3. Abhijānasuttaṃ

3. Directly Knowing

24. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpaṃ[P 3.0027], bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya; vedanaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya; saññaṃ anabhijānaṃ… saṅkhāre anabhijānaṃ [M 2.0023] aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya; viññāṇaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Rūpañca kho, bhikkhave, abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya; vedanaṃ abhijānaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāyā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

24. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, without directly knowing and fully understanding form, without dispassion for it and without abandoning it, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. Without directly knowing and fully understanding feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, without dispassion for it and without abandoning it, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. But, bhikkhus, by directly knowing and fully understanding form, by becoming dispassionate towards it and abandoning it, one is capable of the destruction of suffering. By directly knowing and fully understanding feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, by becoming dispassionate towards it and abandoning it, one is capable of the destruction of suffering.” The third.

4. Chandarāgasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Desire and Lust

25. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpasmiṃ chandarāgo taṃ [T 3.0034] pajahatha. Evaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ pahīnaṃ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ. Yo vedanāya chandarāgo taṃ pajahatha. Evaṃ sā vedanā pahīnā bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Yo saññāya chandarāgo taṃ pajahatha. Evaṃ sā saññā pahīnā bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Yo saṅkhāresu chandarāgo taṃ pajahatha. Evaṃ te saṅkhārā pahīnā bhavissanti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Yo viññāṇasmiṃ chandarāgo taṃ pajahatha. Evaṃ taṃ viññāṇaṃ pahīnaṃ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhamma”nti. Catutthaṃ.

25. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, abandon desire and lust for form. Thus, that form will be abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, obliterated, so that it is incapable of arising again in the future. Abandon desire and lust for feeling. Thus, that feeling will be abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, obliterated, so that it is incapable of arising again in the future. Abandon desire and lust for perception. Thus, that perception will be abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, obliterated, so that it is incapable of arising again in the future. Abandon desire and lust for formations. Thus, those formations will be abandoned, their roots cut off, made like a palm stump, obliterated, so that they are incapable of arising again in the future. Abandon desire and lust for consciousness. Thus, that consciousness will be abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, obliterated, so that it is incapable of arising again in the future.”

5. Assādasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Gratification

26. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0027]. “Pubbeva pubbe (pī. ka.) me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva bodhisattassa (pī. ka.) sato etadahosi – ‘ko nu kho rūpassa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko vedanāya assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko saññāya assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko saṅkhārānaṃ assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko viññāṇassa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇa’nti? Tassa [P 3.0028] mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘yaṃ kho rūpaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ rūpassa assādo. Yaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, ayaṃ rūpassa ādīnavo. Yo rūpasmiṃ chandarāgavinayo [T 3.0035] chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ[M 2.0024], ayaṃ vedanāya assādo yā (ka.). Yaṃ vedanā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṃ vedanāya ādīnavo. Yo vedanāya chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ vedanāya nissaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ saññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati…pe… yaṃ saṅkhāre paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ assādo. Yaṃ ye (sī. ka.) saṅkhārā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavo. Yo saṅkhāresu chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ viññāṇassa assādo. Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, ayaṃ viññāṇassa ādīnavo. Yo viññāṇasmiṃ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ’”.

26. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment, while I was still an unenlightened Bodhisatta, this thought occurred to me: ‘What is the gratification in form, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in feeling, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in perception, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in formations, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in consciousness, what is the danger, what is the escape?’ Then, Bhikkhus, this thought occurred to me: ‘The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on form—this is the gratification in form. That form is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in form. The dispelling of desire and lust for form, the abandonment of desire and lust—this is the escape from form. The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on feeling—this is the gratification in feeling. That feeling is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in feeling. The dispelling of desire and lust for feeling, the abandonment of desire and lust—this is the escape from feeling. The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on perception… and so on… The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on formations—this is the gratification in formations. That formations are impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in formations. The dispelling of desire and lust for formations, the abandonment of desire and lust—this is the escape from formations. The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on consciousness—this is the gratification in consciousness. That consciousness is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in consciousness. The dispelling of desire and lust for consciousness, the abandonment of desire and lust—this is the escape from consciousness.’”

“Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ, neva tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṃ abhisambuddho (sī.). Yato ca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ; athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake [T 3.0036] sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti cetovimutti (sī. pī. ka.); ayamantimā jāti; natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for as long as I did not fully understand, as it really is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape concerning these five aggregates of clinging, for that long, Bhikkhus, I did not claim to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. But when, Bhikkhus, I fully understood, as it really is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape concerning these five aggregates of clinging, then, Bhikkhus, I claimed to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘Unshakeable is my liberation; this is the last birth; now there is no further becoming.’”

6. Dutiyaassādasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Gratification

27. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0028][P 3.0029]. “Rūpassāhaṃ, bhikkhave, assādapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo rūpassa assādo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā rūpassa assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Rūpassāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādīnavapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo rūpassa ādīnavo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā rūpassa ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Rūpassāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nissaraṇapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yaṃ rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ paññāya me taṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ. Vedanāyāhaṃ, bhikkhave… saññāyāhaṃ, bhikkhave… saṅkhārānāhaṃ[M 2.0025], bhikkhave… viññāṇassāhaṃ, bhikkhave, assādapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo viññāṇassa assādo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā viññāṇassa assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Viññāṇassāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādīnavapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo viññāṇassa ādīnavo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā viññāṇassa ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Viññāṇassāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nissaraṇapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yaṃ viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ paññāya me taṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ. Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ assādañca [T 3.0037] assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ…pe… abbhaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti cetovimutti (sī. pī. ka.); ayamantimā jāti; natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

27. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I went in search of the gratification in form. I discovered the gratification in form. To whatever extent there is gratification in form, that I have clearly seen with wisdom. I went in search of the danger in form. I discovered the danger in form. To whatever extent there is danger in form, that I have clearly seen with wisdom. I went in search of the escape from form. I discovered the escape from form. To whatever extent there is an escape from form, that I have clearly seen with wisdom. I went in search of the gratification in feeling… in perception… in volitional formations… in consciousness. I discovered the gratification in consciousness. To whatever extent there is gratification in consciousness, that I have clearly seen with wisdom. I went in search of the danger in consciousness. I discovered the danger in consciousness. To whatever extent there is danger in consciousness, that I have clearly seen with wisdom. I went in search of the escape from consciousness. I discovered the escape from consciousness. To whatever extent there is an escape from consciousness, that I have clearly seen with wisdom. Bhikkhus, so long as I did not directly know as they really are the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape concerning these five aggregates subject to clinging… but when I did directly know them as they really are, knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘My liberation is unshakeable; this is my last birth; now there is no further becoming.’” The Sixth.

7. Tatiyaassādasuttaṃ

7. The Third Discourse on Gratification

28. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpassa assādo abhavissa nayidaṃ [P 3.0030] sattā rūpasmiṃ sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpassa assādo, tasmā sattā rūpasmiṃ sārajjanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpassa ādīnavo abhavissa nayidaṃ sattā rūpasmiṃ nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpassa ādīnavo, tasmā sattā rūpasmiṃ [V 2.0029] nibbindanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa nayidaṃ sattā rūpasmā nissareyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ, tasmā sattā rūpasmā nissaranti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, vedanāya…pe… no cedaṃ, bhikkhave, saññāya… no cedaṃ, bhikkhave, saṅkhārānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa[T 3.0038], nayidaṃ sattā saṅkhārehi nissareyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi saṅkhārānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ, tasmā sattā saṅkhārehi nissaranti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, viññāṇassa assādo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā viññāṇasmiṃ sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi viññāṇassa assādo, tasmā sattā viññāṇasmiṃ sārajjanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, viññāṇassa ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā viññāṇasmiṃ nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi viññāṇassa ādīnavo, tasmā sattā viññāṇasmiṃ nibbindanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā viññāṇasmā nissareyyuṃ[M 2.0026]. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ, tasmā sattā viññāṇasmā nissaranti.

28. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, if there were no gratification in form, beings would not be enamored with form. But because there is gratification in form, beings are enamored with form. If there were no danger in form, beings would not become disenchanted with form. But because there is danger in form, beings become disenchanted with form. If there were no escape from form, beings would not escape from form. But because there is an escape from form, beings escape from form. If there were no gratification in feeling… in perception… If there were no escape from volitional formations, beings would not escape from volitional formations. But because there is an escape from volitional formations, beings escape from volitional formations. If there were no gratification in consciousness, beings would not be enamored with consciousness. But because there is gratification in consciousness, beings are enamored with consciousness. If there were no danger in consciousness, beings would not become disenchanted with consciousness. But because there is danger in consciousness, beings become disenchanted with consciousness. If there were no escape from consciousness, beings would not escape from consciousness. But because there is an escape from consciousness, beings escape from consciousness.”

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññaṃsu nābbhaññiṃsu (sī.); neva tāva, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā [P 3.0031] sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaṃyuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā vihariṃsu. Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññaṃsu; atha, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya [T 3.0039] nissaṭā visaṃyuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharanti”. Sattamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for as long as beings had not directly known as it really is the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape of these five aggregates subject to clinging, for so long, bhikkhus, they had not dwelt escaped, disjoined, and liberated, with a mind free from boundaries, from the world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, from this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans. But when, bhikkhus, beings directly knew as it really is the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape of these five aggregates subject to clinging, then, bhikkhus, they dwell escaped, disjoined, and liberated, with a mind free from boundaries, from the world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, from this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans.” The Seventh.

8. Abhinandanasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Delighting

29. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0030]. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ abhinandati, dukkhaṃ so abhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ abhinandati, aparimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo vedanaṃ abhinandati… yo saññaṃ abhinandati… yo saṅkhāre abhinandati… yo viññāṇaṃ abhinandati, dukkhaṃ so abhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ abhinandati, aparimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ nābhinandati, dukkhaṃ so nābhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ nābhinandati, parimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo vedanaṃ nābhinandati… yo saññaṃ nābhinandati… yo saṅkhāre nābhinandati… yo viññāṇaṃ nābhinandati, dukkhaṃ so nābhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ nābhinandati, parimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

29. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whoever delights in form, delights in suffering. Whoever delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Whoever delights in feeling… whoever delights in perception… whoever delights in volitional formations… whoever delights in consciousness, delights in suffering. Whoever delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. But, bhikkhus, whoever does not delight in form, does not delight in suffering. Whoever does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. Whoever does not delight in feeling… whoever does not delight in perception… whoever does not delight in volitional formations… whoever does not delight in consciousness, does not delight in suffering. Whoever does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.” The Eighth.

9. Uppādasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Arising

30. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpassa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo[P 3.0032], dukkhasseso uppādo rogānaṃ ṭhiti jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo vedanāya…pe… yo saññāya…pe… yo saṅkhārānaṃ…pe… yo viññāṇassa [M 2.0027] uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo rogānaṃ ṭhiti jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho rogānaṃ vūpasamo jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo. Yo vedanāya [T 3.0040] …pe… yo saññāya… yo saṅkhārānaṃ… yo viññāṇassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho rogānaṃ vūpasamo jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Navamaṃ.

30. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, persistence, new generation, and manifestation of form, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. Whatever is the arising, persistence, new generation, and manifestation of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. But, Bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation, appeasement, and disappearance of form, that is the cessation of suffering, the appeasement of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death. Whatever is the cessation, appeasement, and disappearance of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness, that is the cessation of suffering, the appeasement of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death.”

10. Aghamūlasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Root of Misery

31. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Aghañca, bhikkhave, desessāmi aghamūlañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca [V 2.0031] bhikkhave aghaṃ? Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, aghaṃ, vedanā aghaṃ, saññā aghaṃ, saṅkhārā aghaṃ, viññāṇaṃ aghaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, aghaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, aghamūlaṃ? Yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobhavikā nandīrāgasahagatā nandirāgasahagatā (sabbattha) tatratatrābhinandinī; seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, aghamūla”nti. Dasamaṃ.

31. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you misery and the root of misery. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is misery? Form, Bhikkhus, is misery; feeling is misery; perception is misery; formations are misery; consciousness is misery. This, Bhikkhus, is called misery. And what, Bhikkhus, is the root of misery? It is this craving which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting greatly in this and that; that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence. This, Bhikkhus, is called the root of misery.”

11. Pabhaṅgusuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on the Perishable

32. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Pabhaṅguñca, bhikkhave, desessāmi appabhaṅguñca. Taṃ suṇātha. Kiñca, bhikkhave, pabhaṅgu, kiṃ appabhaṅgu? Rūpaṃ[P 3.0033], bhikkhave, pabhaṅgu. Yo tassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, idaṃ appabhaṅgu. Vedanā pabhaṅgu. Yo tassā nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, idaṃ appabhaṅgu. Saññā pabhaṅgu… saṅkhārā pabhaṅgu. Yo tesaṃ nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, idaṃ appabhaṅgu. Viññāṇaṃ pabhaṅgu. Yo tassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, idaṃ appabhaṅgū”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

32. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the perishable and the imperishable. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the perishable? What is the imperishable? Form, Bhikkhus, is perishable. Whatever is its cessation, appeasement, and disappearance, that is the imperishable. Feeling is perishable. Whatever is its cessation, appeasement, and disappearance, that is the imperishable. Perception is perishable… Formations are perishable. Whatever is their cessation, appeasement, and disappearance, that is the imperishable. Consciousness is perishable. Whatever is its cessation, appeasement, and disappearance, that is the imperishable.”

Bhāravaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on the Burden, the Third.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Bhāraṃ [T 3.0041] pariññaṃ abhijānaṃ, chandarāgaṃ catutthakaṃ;

Assādā ca tayo vuttā, abhinandanamaṭṭhamaṃ;

Uppādaṃ aghamūlañca, ekādasamo pabhaṅgūti.

The Bhāra, the Pariññā, the Abhijāna, the Chandarāga as the fourth; and three on Gratification are stated; the Abhinandana as the eighth; the Uppāda and the Aghamūla, and the Pabhaṅgu as the eleventh.

4. Natumhākaṃvaggo

4. The Chapter on 'What is Not Yours'

1. Natumhākaṃsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on 'What is Not Yours'

33. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0042][M 2.0028]. “Yaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Taṃ vo pahīnaṃ hitāya [V 2.0032] sukhāya bhavissati. Kiñca, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ? Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Taṃ vo pahīnaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Vedanā na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Sā vo pahīnā hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Saññā na tumhākaṃ… saṅkhārā [P 3.0034] na tumhākaṃ, te pajahatha. Te vo pahīnā hitāya sukhāya bhavissanti. Viññāṇaṃ na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Taṃ vo pahīnaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati”.

33. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever is not yours, abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness. And what, Bhikkhus, is not yours? Form, Bhikkhus, is not yours; abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness. Feeling is not yours; abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness. Perception is not yours… Formations are not yours; abandon them. They, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness. Consciousness is not yours; abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yaṃ imasmiṃ jetavane tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṃ taṃ jano hareyya vā ḍaheyya vā yathāpaccayaṃ vā kareyya. Api nu tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘amhe jano harati vā ḍahati vā yathāpaccayaṃ vā karotī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Taṃ kissa hetu”? “Na hi no etaṃ, bhante, attā vā attaniyaṃ vā”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Taṃ vo pahīnaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Vedanā na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Sā vo pahīnā hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Saññā na tumhākaṃ… saṅkhārā na tumhākaṃ… viññāṇaṃ na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Taṃ vo pahīnaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissatī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Suppose, Bhikkhus, a person were to carry off, burn, or do as they please with whatever grass, sticks, branches, and leaves are in this Jeta's Grove. Would it occur to you thus: ‘A person is carrying us off, burning us, or doing with us as they please’?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.” “For what reason?” “Because, venerable sir, this is not our self, nor what belongs to our self.” “Even so, Bhikkhus, form is not yours; abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness. Feeling is not yours; abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness. Perception is not yours… Formations are not yours… Consciousness is not yours; abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness.”

2. Dutiyanatumhākaṃsuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on 'What is Not Yours'

34. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0043]. “Yaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Taṃ vo pahīnaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Kiñca, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ? Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Taṃ vo pahīnaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Vedanā na tumhākaṃ… saññā na tumhākaṃ… saṅkhārā na tumhākaṃ… viññāṇaṃ na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha. Taṃ vo pahīnaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ taṃ pajahatha. Taṃ vo pahīnaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

34. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever is not yours, abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness. And what, Bhikkhus, is not yours? Form, Bhikkhus, is not yours; abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness. Feeling is not yours… perception is not yours… formations are not yours… Consciousness is not yours; abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness. Bhikkhus, whatever is not yours, abandon it. That, having been abandoned by you, will be for your welfare and happiness.”

3. Aññatarabhikkhusuttaṃ

3. The Sutta on a Certain Bhikkhu

35. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha [P 3.0035] kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [M 2.0029] nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ [V 2.0033] etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu; yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho, appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, anuseti, tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati; yaṃ nānuseti, na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchatī”ti. “Aññātaṃ, bhagavā; aññātaṃ, sugatā”ti.

35. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. As he sat there, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute.” “Bhikkhu, that which one has a latent tendency towards, by that one is designated; that which one does not have a latent tendency towards, by that one is not designated.” “It is understood, Blessed One; it is understood, Well-Farer!”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti? “Rūpaṃ ce, bhante, anuseti tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Vedanaṃ ce anuseti tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Saññaṃ ce anuseti tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Saṅkhāre ce anuseti tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Viññāṇaṃ ce anuseti tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Rūpaṃ ce, bhante, nānuseti na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Vedanaṃ ce… saññaṃ ce… saṅkhāre ce… viññāṇaṃ ce nānuseti [T 3.0044] na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“But how, bhikkhu, do you understand in detail the meaning of what I have stated in brief?” “Venerable sir, if a latent tendency lies latent in regard to form, by that one is designated. If a latent tendency lies latent in regard to feeling, by that one is designated. If a latent tendency lies latent in regard to perception, by that one is designated. If latent tendencies lie latent in regard to formations, by that one is designated. If a latent tendency lies latent in regard to consciousness, by that one is designated. Venerable sir, if a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to form, by that one is not designated. If… in regard to feeling… in regard to perception… in regard to formations… if a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to consciousness, by that one is not designated. It is in this way, venerable sir, that I understand in detail the meaning of what the Blessed One has stated in brief.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ ce, bhikkhu, anuseti tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Vedanaṃ ce… saññaṃ ce… saṅkhāre ce… viññāṇaṃ ce anuseti tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Rūpaṃ ce, bhikkhu, nānuseti na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Vedanaṃ ce… saññaṃ ce… saṅkhāre ce… viññāṇaṃ ce nānuseti na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena, bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.

“Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good, bhikkhu, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief. If, bhikkhu, a latent tendency lies latent in regard to form, by that one is designated. If… in regard to feeling… if… in regard to perception… if… in regard to formations… if a latent tendency lies latent in regard to consciousness, by that one is designated. If, bhikkhu, a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to form, by that one is not designated. If… in regard to feeling… if… in regard to perception… if… in regard to formations… if a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to consciousness, by that one is not designated. Thus, bhikkhu, the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief is to be understood in detail in this way.”

Atha kho so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā [P 3.0036] anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Then that bhikkhu, delighting and rejoicing in the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed.

Atha kho so bhikkhu eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Tatiyaṃ.

Then that bhikkhu, dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, before long, with his own direct knowledge, realized in this very life and dwelt in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness. He understood: “Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.” And that bhikkhu became one of the arahants. The Third.

4. Dutiyaaññatarabhikkhusuttaṃ

4. The Second Discourse concerning a Certain Bhikkhu

36. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0034]. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante[T 3.0045], bhagavā [M 2.0030] saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, anuseti taṃ anumīyati; yaṃ anumīyati tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Yaṃ nānuseti na taṃ anumīyati; yaṃ nānumīyati na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchatī”ti. “Aññātaṃ, bhagavā; aññātaṃ, sugatā”ti.

36. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One… and sat down to one side. Seated there, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute.” “Bhikkhu, that in which a latent tendency lies latent is subject to repeated death; by that which is subject to repeated death, one is designated. That in which a latent tendency does not lie latent is not subject to repeated death; by that which is not subject to repeated death, one is not designated.” “It is understood, Blessed One! It is understood, Well-farer!”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti? “Rūpaṃ ce, bhante, anuseti taṃ anumīyati; yaṃ anumīyati tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Vedanaṃ ce anuseti… saññaṃ ce anuseti… saṅkhāre ce anuseti… viññāṇaṃ ce anuseti taṃ anumīyati; yaṃ anumīyati tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Rūpaṃ ce, bhante, nānuseti na taṃ anumīyati; yaṃ nānumīyati [P 3.0037] na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Vedanaṃ ce nānuseti… saññaṃ ce nānuseti… saṅkhāre ce nānuseti… viññāṇaṃ ce nānuseti na taṃ anumīyati; yaṃ nānumīyati na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“But how, bhikkhu, do you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief?” “Venerable sir, if a latent tendency lies latent in regard to form, that form is subject to repeated death; by that which is subject to repeated death, one is designated. If a latent tendency lies latent in regard to feeling… in regard to perception… in regard to formations… if a latent tendency lies latent in regard to consciousness, that consciousness is subject to repeated death; by that which is subject to repeated death, one is designated. Venerable sir, if a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to form, that form is not subject to repeated death; by that which is not subject to repeated death, one is not designated. If a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to feeling… in regard to perception… in regard to formations… if a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to consciousness, that consciousness is not subject to repeated death; by that which is not subject to repeated death, one is not designated. It is in this way, venerable sir, that I understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ ce, bhikkhu, anuseti taṃ anumīyati; yaṃ anumīyati tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Vedanaṃ ce, bhikkhu… saññaṃ ce, bhikkhu… saṅkhāre ce, bhikkhu… viññāṇaṃ ce, bhikkhu, anuseti taṃ anumīyati; yaṃ anumīyati tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Rūpaṃ ce, bhikkhu, nānuseti na taṃ [T 3.0046] anumīyati; yaṃ nānumīyati na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Vedanaṃ ce nānuseti… saññaṃ ce nānuseti… saṅkhāre ce nānuseti… viññāṇaṃ ce nānuseti na taṃ anumīyati; yaṃ nānumīyati na tena saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā [V 2.0035] saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti…pe… aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Catutthaṃ.

“Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good, bhikkhu, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief. Bhikkhu, if a latent tendency lies latent in regard to form, that form is subject to repeated death; by that which is subject to repeated death, one is designated. If… in regard to feeling, bhikkhu… in regard to perception, bhikkhu… in regard to formations, bhikkhu… if a latent tendency lies latent in regard to consciousness, bhikkhu, that consciousness is subject to repeated death; by that which is subject to repeated death, one is designated. Bhikkhu, if a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to form, that form is not subject to repeated death; by that which is not subject to repeated death, one is not designated. If a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to feeling… in regard to perception… in regard to formations… if a latent tendency does not lie latent in regard to consciousness, that consciousness is not subject to repeated death; by that which is not subject to repeated death, one is not designated. Indeed, bhikkhu, the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief should be understood in detail in this way.” …And that bhikkhu became one of the arahants. The Fourth.

5. Ānandasuttaṃ

5. Discourse to Ānanda

37. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

37. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. After an exchange of friendly, courteous talk, he sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Ānanda, who was sitting to one side:

“Sace [M 2.0031] taṃ, ānanda, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘katamesaṃ, āvuso ānanda, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa ṭhitānaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) aññathattaṃ paññāyatī’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, ānanda, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti? “Sace [P 3.0038] maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘katamesaṃ, āvuso ānanda, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyatī’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘rūpassa kho, āvuso, uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. Vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhārānaṃ… viññāṇassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. Imesaṃ kho, āvuso, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa [T 3.0047] aññathattaṃ paññāyatī’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyya”nti.

“Ānanda, if they were to ask you thus: ‘Friend Ānanda, of what phenomena is the arising discerned, the passing away discerned, and the alteration of that which is present discerned?’—being asked thus, Ānanda, how would you answer?” “Venerable sir, if they were to ask me thus: ‘Friend Ānanda, of what phenomena is the arising discerned, the passing away discerned, and the alteration of that which is present discerned?’—being asked thus, venerable sir, I would answer thus: ‘Friend, the arising of form is discerned, its passing away is discerned, and the alteration of it while it is present is discerned. Of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness, the arising is discerned, its passing away is discerned, and the alteration of it while it is present is discerned. Of these phenomena, friend, the arising is discerned, their passing away is discerned, and the alteration of them while they are present is discerned.’ Being asked thus, venerable sir, I would answer in this way.”

“Sādhu sādhu, ānanda! Rūpassa kho, ānanda, uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. Vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhārānaṃ… viññāṇassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. Imesaṃ kho, ānanda, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyatīti. Evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ byākareyyāsī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Good, good, Ānanda! Ānanda, the arising of form is indeed discerned, its passing away is discerned, and the alteration of it while it is present is discerned. The arising of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness is discerned, its passing away is discerned, and the alteration of it while it is present is discerned. Ānanda, of these phenomena, the arising is indeed discerned, their passing away is discerned, and the alteration of them while they are present is discerned. Being asked thus, Ānanda, you should answer in this way.” The fifth.

6. Dutiyaānandasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse to Ānanda

38. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0036]. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

38. At Sāvatthī. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Ānanda, who was sitting to one side:

“Sace taṃ, ānanda, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘katamesaṃ, āvuso ānanda, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyittha? Katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyissati, vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyissati? Katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyatī’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, ānanda, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti? “Sace maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘katamesaṃ, āvuso ānanda, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyittha? Katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyissati[M 2.0032], vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitassa [P 3.0039] aññathattaṃ paññāyissati[T 3.0048]? Katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyatī’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘yaṃ kho, āvuso, rūpaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vipariṇataṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyittha. Yā vedanā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā; tassā uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitāya aññathattaṃ paññāyittha. Yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā; tesaṃ uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyittha. Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vipariṇataṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyittha. Imesaṃ kho, āvuso, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyittha’”.

“If, Ānanda, they were to ask you thus: ‘Friend Ānanda, of what phenomena was the arising discerned, the passing away discerned, and the alteration of that which was present discerned? Of what phenomena will the arising be discerned, the passing away be discerned, and the alteration of that which will be present discerned? Of what phenomena is the arising discerned, the passing away discerned, and the alteration of that which is present discerned?’—being asked thus, Ānanda, how would you answer?” “If, venerable sir, they were to ask me thus: ‘Friend Ānanda, of what phenomena was the arising discerned, the passing away discerned, and the alteration of that which was present discerned? Of what phenomena will the arising be discerned, the passing away be discerned, and the alteration of that which will be present discerned? Of what phenomena is the arising discerned, the passing away discerned, and the alteration of that which is present discerned?’—being asked thus, venerable sir, I would answer thus: ‘Indeed, friends, whatever form was past, ceased, and altered, of that form the arising was discerned, the passing away was discerned, and the alteration of it while it was present was discerned. Whatever feeling was past, ceased, and altered, of that feeling the arising was discerned, the passing away was discerned, and the alteration of it while it was present was discerned. Whatever perception… Whatever volitional formations were past, ceased, and altered, of those volitional formations the arising was discerned, the passing away was discerned, and the alteration of them while they were present was discerned. Whatever consciousness was past, ceased, and altered, of that consciousness the arising was discerned, the passing away was discerned, and the alteration of it while it was present was discerned. Indeed, friends, of these phenomena the arising was discerned, the passing away was discerned, and the alteration of them while they were present was discerned.’

“Yaṃ kho, āvuso, rūpaṃ ajātaṃ apātubhūtaṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyissati, vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyissati. Yā vedanā ajātā apātubhūtā; tassā uppādo paññāyissati, vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitāya aññathattaṃ paññāyissati. Yā saññā…pe… ye saṅkhārā ajātā apātubhūtā; tesaṃ uppādo paññāyissati, vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyissati. Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ apātubhūtaṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyissati, vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyissati. Imesaṃ kho, āvuso[T 3.0049][V 2.0037], dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyissati, vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyissati.

‘Indeed, friends, as for form that is unborn and unmanifest: its arising will be discerned, its passing away will be discerned, and the alteration of it while it is present will be discerned. As for feeling that is unborn and unmanifest: its arising will be discerned, its passing away will be discerned, and the alteration of it while it is present will be discerned. As for perception… as for volitional formations that are unborn and unmanifest: their arising will be discerned, their passing away will be discerned, and the alteration of them while they are present will be discerned. As for consciousness that is unborn and unmanifest: its arising will be discerned, its passing away will be discerned, and the alteration of it while it is present will be discerned. Indeed, friends, of these phenomena the arising will be discerned, their passing away will be discerned, and the alteration of them while they are present will be discerned.

“Yaṃ kho, āvuso, rūpaṃ jātaṃ pātubhūtaṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. Yā vedanā jātā pātubhūtā…pe… yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā jātā pātubhūtā; tesaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ jātaṃ pātubhūtaṃ tassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. Imesaṃ kho, āvuso, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyatī’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyya”nti.

‘Indeed, friends, as for form that has arisen and appeared: its arising is discerned, its passing away is discerned, and the alteration of it while it is present is discerned. As for feeling that has arisen and appeared… as for perception… as for volitional formations that have arisen and appeared: their arising is discerned, their passing away is discerned, and the alteration of them while they are present is discerned. As for consciousness that has arisen and appeared: its arising is discerned, its passing away is discerned, and the alteration of it while it is present is discerned. Indeed, friends, of these phenomena the arising is discerned, their passing away is discerned, and the alteration of them while they are present is discerned.’ Being asked thus, venerable sir, I would answer in this way.”

“Sādhu[M 2.0033], sādhu, ānanda! Yaṃ kho, ānanda, rūpaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vipariṇataṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyittha. Yā vedanā [P 3.0040]… yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā… yaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vipariṇataṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyittha. Imesaṃ kho, ānanda, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyittha, vayo paññāyittha, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyittha.

“Good, good, Ānanda! Indeed, Ānanda, whatever form was past, ceased, and changed: its arising was discerned, its passing away was discerned, and the alteration of its persistence was discerned. Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness was past, ceased, and changed: its arising was discerned, its passing away was discerned, and the alteration of its persistence was discerned. Indeed, Ānanda, of these phenomena the arising was discerned, the passing away was discerned, and the alteration of their persistence was discerned.

“Yaṃ kho, ānanda, rūpaṃ ajātaṃ apātubhūtaṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyissati, vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyissati. Yā vedanā… yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā… yaṃ viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ apātubhūtaṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyissati[T 3.0050], vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyissati. Imesaṃ kho, ānanda, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyissati, vayo paññāyissati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyissati.

“Indeed, Ānanda, whatever form is unborn and unmanifested: its arising will be discerned, its passing away will be discerned, and the alteration of its persistence will be discerned. Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness is unborn and unmanifested: its arising will be discerned, its passing away will be discerned, and the alteration of its persistence will be discerned. Indeed, Ānanda, the arising of these phenomena will be discerned, their passing away will be discerned, and the alteration of their persistence will be discerned.

“Yaṃ kho, ānanda, rūpaṃ jātaṃ pātubhūtaṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. Yā vedanā jātā pātubhūtā… yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā… yaṃ viññāṇaṃ jātaṃ pātubhūtaṃ; tassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. Imesaṃ kho, ānanda, dhammānaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyatīti. Evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ byākareyyāsī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Indeed, Ānanda, whatever form has been born and has manifested: its arising is discerned, its passing away is discerned, and the alteration of its persistence is discerned. Whatever feeling has been born and has manifested… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness has been born and has manifested: its arising is discerned, its passing away is discerned, and the alteration of its persistence is discerned. Indeed, Ānanda, the arising of these phenomena is discerned, their passing away is discerned, and the alteration of their persistence is discerned. Being asked thus, Ānanda, you should answer thus.” The Sixth.

7. Anudhammasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse in Accordance with the Dhamma

39. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0038]. “Dhammānudhammappaṭipannassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ayamanudhammo hoti yaṃ rūpe nibbidābahulo nibbidābahulaṃ (pī. ka.) vihareyya, vedanāya nibbidābahulo vihareyya, saññā nibbidābahulo vihareyya, saṅkhāresu nibbidābahulo vihareyya, viññāṇe nibbidābahulo vihareyya. Yo rūpe nibbidābahulo viharanto, vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhāresu nibbidābahulo viharanto, viññāṇe nibbidābahulo viharanto rūpaṃ parijānāti, vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ parijānāti, so rūpaṃ parijānaṃ, vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ parijānaṃ parimuccati rūpamhā, parimuccati vedanā[P 3.0041], parimuccati saññāya[M 2.0034], parimuccati saṅkhārehi, parimuccati viññāṇamhā, parimuccati [T 3.0051] jātiyā jarāmaraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, parimuccati dukkhasmāti vadāmī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

39. At Sāvatthī. “For a bhikkhu, bhikkhus, who practices in accordance with the Dhamma, this is the practice in accordance with the Dhamma: that he should dwell with much revulsion towards form, dwell with much revulsion towards feeling, dwell with much revulsion towards perception, dwell with much revulsion towards volitional formations, dwell with much revulsion towards consciousness. One who, dwelling with much revulsion towards form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, fully understands form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness. That one, fully understanding form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, is liberated from form, liberated from feeling, liberated from perception, liberated from volitional formations, liberated from consciousness; he is liberated from birth, aging, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair. He is liberated from suffering, I say.” The Seventh.

8. Dutiyaanudhammasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse in Accordance with the Dhamma

40. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Dhammānudhammappaṭipannassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ayamanudhammo hoti yaṃ rūpe aniccānupassī vihareyya…pe… parimuccati dukkhasmāti vadāmī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

40. At Sāvatthī. “For a bhikkhu, bhikkhus, who practices in accordance with the Dhamma, this is the practice in accordance with the Dhamma: that he should dwell contemplating impermanence in form… he is liberated from suffering, I say.” The Eighth.

9. Tatiyaanudhammasuttaṃ

9. The Third Discourse in Accordance with the Dhamma

41. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Dhammānudhammappaṭipannassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ayamanudhammo hoti yaṃ rūpe dukkhānupassī vihareyya…pe… [T 3.0052] parimuccati dukkhasmāti vadāmī”ti. Navamaṃ.

41. At Sāvatthī. “For a bhikkhu, bhikkhus, who practices in accordance with the Dhamma, this is the practice in accordance with the Dhamma: that he should dwell contemplating suffering in form… he is liberated from suffering, I say.” The Ninth.

10. Catutthaanudhammasuttaṃ

10. The Fourth Discourse in Accordance with the Dhamma

42. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0039]. “Dhammānudhammappaṭipannassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ayamanudhammo hoti yaṃ rūpe anattānupassī vihareyya, vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhāresu… viññāṇe anattānupassī vihareyya. Yo rūpe anattānupassī viharanto…pe… rūpaṃ parijānāti, vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ parijānāti, so rūpaṃ parijānaṃ, vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ parijānaṃ parimuccati rūpamhā, parimuccati vedanāya, parimuccati saññāya, parimuccati saṅkhārehi, parimuccati viññāṇamhā, parimuccati jātiyā jarāmaraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, parimuccati dukkhasmāti vadāmī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

42. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who practices in accordance with the Dhamma, this is the practice in accordance with the Dhamma: that he should dwell contemplating not-self in form, in feeling, in perception, in volitional formations, and in consciousness. As he dwells contemplating not-self in form… he fully understands form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness. Fully understanding form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, he is liberated from form, liberated from feeling, liberated from perception, liberated from volitional formations, liberated from consciousness; he is liberated from birth, aging, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair. He is liberated from suffering, I say.” The Tenth.

Natumhākaṃvaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter: Not Yours.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Natumhākena [P 3.0042] dve vuttā, bhikkhūhi apare duve;

Ānandena ca dve vuttā, anudhammehi dve dukāti.

Two were spoken on ‘Not Yours,’ two others on the bhikkhus; and two were spoken on Ānanda, and two pairs on the practice in accordance with the Dhamma.

5. Attadīpavaggo

5. The Chapter on Self as an Island

1. Attadīpasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Self as an Island

43. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0053][M 2.0035]. “Attadīpā, bhikkhave, viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā. Attadīpānaṃ, bhikkhave, viharataṃ attasaraṇānaṃ anaññasaraṇānaṃ, dhammadīpānaṃ dhammasaraṇānaṃ anaññasaraṇānaṃ yoni upaparikkhitabbā. Kiṃjātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, kiṃpahotikā”ti?

43. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, dwell with yourselves as an island, with yourselves as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge. For those, bhikkhus, who dwell with themselves as an island, with themselves as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge, the origin should be investigated: ‘What is the origin of sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair? What is their cause?’”

“Kiṃjātikā [V 2.0040] ca, bhikkhave, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, kiṃpahotikā? Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto, rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ; attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Tassa taṃ rūpaṃ vipariṇamati, aññathā ca hoti. Tassa rūpavipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā. Vedanaṃ attato samanupassati, vedanāvantaṃ vā attānaṃ; attani vā vedanaṃ, vedanāya vā attānaṃ. Tassa sā vedanā vipariṇamati, aññathā ca hoti. Tassa vedanāvipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā. Saññaṃ attato samanupassati… saṅkhāre attato samanupassati… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ; attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Tassa [P 3.0043] taṃ viññāṇaṃ vipariṇamati, aññathā ca hoti[T 3.0054]. Tassa viññāṇavipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā.

“What, Bhikkhus, is the nature of sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair, and what is their origin? Here, Bhikkhus, an uninstructed ordinary person, who has not seen the noble ones, is unskilled in the noble Dhamma, and untrained in the noble Dhamma; who has not seen good persons, is unskilled in the Dhamma of good persons, and untrained in the Dhamma of good persons, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. When that form of his changes and becomes otherwise, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair arise. He regards feeling as self, or self as possessing feeling, or feeling as in self, or self as in feeling. When that feeling of his changes and becomes otherwise, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair arise. He regards perception as self… he regards volitional formations as self… he regards consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. When that consciousness of his changes and becomes otherwise, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair arise.”

“Rūpassa tveva, bhikkhave, aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmaṃ virāgaṃ nirodhaṃ vipariṇāma virāga nirodhaṃ (sī.), pubbe ceva rūpaṃ etarahi ca sabbaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti, evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato ye sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā te pahīyanti. Tesaṃ pahānā na paritassati, aparitassaṃ sukhaṃ viharati, sukhavihārī bhikkhu ‘tadaṅganibbuto’ti vuccati. Vedanāya tveva, bhikkhave, aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmaṃ virāgaṃ nirodhaṃ, pubbe ceva vedanā etarahi ca sabbā vedanā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammāti, evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ [M 2.0036] sammappaññāya passato ye sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā te pahīyanti. Tesaṃ pahānā na paritassati, aparitassaṃ sukhaṃ viharati, sukhavihārī bhikkhu ‘tadaṅganibbuto’ti vuccati. Saññāya… saṅkhārānaṃ tveva, bhikkhave, aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmaṃ virāgaṃ nirodhaṃ, pubbe ceva saṅkhārā etarahi ca sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammāti, evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato ye sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā te pahīyanti. Tesaṃ pahānā na paritassati, aparitassaṃ sukhaṃ viharati, sukhavihārī bhikkhu ‘tadaṅganibbuto’ti vuccati. Viññāṇassa tveva, bhikkhave, aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmaṃ virāgaṃ nirodhaṃ, pubbe ceva viññāṇaṃ etarahi ca sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti, evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya [T 3.0055] passato ye sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā [V 2.0041] te pahīyanti. Tesaṃ pahānā na paritassati, aparitassaṃ sukhaṃ viharati, sukhavihārī bhikkhu ‘tadaṅganibbuto’ti vuccatī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for one who, having known the impermanence of form itself, its alteration, fading away, and cessation, sees with right wisdom as it really is that ‘both form in the past and all form at present is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change,’ those states of sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair are abandoned. With their abandonment, he is not anxious. Being unanxious, he dwells happily. A bhikkhu who dwells happily is said to be ‘extinguished by that factor.’ Bhikkhus, for one who, having known the impermanence of feeling itself, its alteration, fading away, and cessation, sees with right wisdom as it really is that ‘both feeling in the past and all feeling at present is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change,’ those states of sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair are abandoned. With their abandonment, he is not anxious. Being unanxious, he dwells happily. A bhikkhu who dwells happily is said to be ‘extinguished by that factor.’ …of perception… Bhikkhus, for one who, having known the impermanence of volitional formations themselves, their alteration, fading away, and cessation, sees with right wisdom as it really is that ‘both volitional formations in the past and all volitional formations at present are impermanent, suffering, and subject to change,’ those states of sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair are abandoned. With their abandonment, he is not anxious. Being unanxious, he dwells happily. A bhikkhu who dwells happily is said to be ‘extinguished by that factor.’ Bhikkhus, for one who, having known the impermanence of consciousness itself, its alteration, fading away, and cessation, sees with right wisdom as it really is that ‘both consciousness in the past and all consciousness at present is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change,’ those states of sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair are abandoned. With their abandonment, he is not anxious. Being unanxious, he dwells happily. A bhikkhu who dwells happily is said to be ‘extinguished by that factor.’” The First.

2. Paṭipadāsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Practice

44. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Sakkāyasamudayagāminiñca [P 3.0044] vo, bhikkhave, paṭipadaṃ desessāmi, sakkāyanirodhagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sakkāyasamudayagāminī paṭipadā? Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto, rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ; attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ attato… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ; attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘sakkāyasamudayagāminī paṭipadā, sakkāyasamudayagāminī paṭipadā’ti. Iti hidaṃ, bhikkhave, vuccati ‘dukkhasamudayagāminī samanupassanā’ti. Ayamevettha attho”.

44. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the practice leading to the origin of identity and the practice leading to the cessation of identity. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the practice leading to the origin of identity? Here, Bhikkhus, an uninstructed ordinary person, who has not seen the noble ones, is unskilled in the noble Dhamma, and untrained in the noble Dhamma; who has not seen good persons, is unskilled in the Dhamma of good persons, and untrained in the Dhamma of good persons, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. He regards feeling as self… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. This, Bhikkhus, is called ‘the practice leading to the origin of identity.’ Thus, Bhikkhus, this is called ‘the contemplation leading to the origin of suffering.’ This is the meaning here.”

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā? Idha, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto, sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto, na rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ[M 2.0037]; na attani vā rūpaṃ, na rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Na vedanaṃ [T 3.0056] attato… na saññaṃ… na saṅkhāre… na viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ; na attani vā viññāṇaṃ, na viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti. Iti hidaṃ, bhikkhave, vuccati ‘dukkhanirodhagāminī samanupassanā’ti. Ayamevettha attho”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“And what, Bhikkhus, is the practice leading to the cessation of identity? Here, Bhikkhus, an instructed noble disciple, who has seen the noble ones, is skilled in the noble Dhamma, and well-trained in the noble Dhamma; who has seen good persons, is skilled in the Dhamma of good persons, and well-trained in the Dhamma of good persons, does not regard form as self, nor self as possessing form, nor form as in self, nor self as in form. He does not regard feeling as self… nor perception… nor volitional formations… he does not regard consciousness as self, nor self as possessing consciousness, nor consciousness as in self, nor self as in consciousness. This, Bhikkhus, is called ‘the practice leading to the cessation of identity.’ Thus, Bhikkhus, this is called ‘the contemplation leading to the cessation of suffering.’ This is the meaning here.” The Second.

3. Aniccasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Impermanence

45. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ[P 3.0045]; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā[V 2.0042]; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato cittaṃ virajjati vimuccati anupādāya āsavehi. Vedanā aniccā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato cittaṃ virajjati vimuccati anupādāya āsavehi. Rūpadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cittaṃ virattaṃ vimuttaṃ hoti anupādāya āsavehi, vedanādhātuyā…pe… saññādhātuyā… saṅkhāradhātuyā… viññāṇadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cittaṃ virattaṃ vimuttaṃ hoti anupādāya āsavehi. Vimuttattā ṭhitaṃ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṃ santussitaṃ (ka. sī. pī. ka.). Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ [T 3.0057] karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

45. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, form is impermanent. Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering; whatever is suffering, that is not-self; whatever is not-self, that should be seen with right wisdom as it truly is: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ For one who sees this with right wisdom as it truly is, the mind becomes dispassionate and is liberated from the taints without grasping. Feeling is impermanent… perception… volitional formations… consciousness is impermanent. Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering; whatever is suffering, that is not-self; whatever is not-self, that should be seen with right wisdom as it truly is: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ For one who sees this with right wisdom as it truly is, the mind becomes dispassionate and is liberated from the taints without grasping. If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu’s mind is dispassionate and liberated from the taints without grasping regarding the form element… the feeling element… the perception element… the volitional formations element… the consciousness element, then, because of being liberated, it is steady. Because of being steady, it is content. Because of being content, he is not agitated. Not being agitated, he personally attains Parinibbāna. He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Third.

4. Dutiyaaniccasuttaṃ

4. The Second Sutta on Impermanence

46. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vedanā aniccā… saññā aniccā… saṅkhārā aniccā… viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ”.

46. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, form is impermanent. Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering; whatever is suffering, that is not-self; whatever is not-self, that should be seen with right wisdom as it truly is: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Feeling is impermanent… perception is impermanent… volitional formations are impermanent… consciousness is impermanent. Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering; whatever is suffering, that is not-self; whatever is not-self, that should be seen with right wisdom as it truly is: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Evametaṃ [M 2.0038] yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato pubbantānudiṭṭhiyo na honti. Pubbantānudiṭṭhīnaṃ asati, aparantānudiṭṭhiyo [P 3.0046] na honti. Aparantānudiṭṭhīnaṃ asati, thāmaso thāmasā (sī. syā. kaṃ.) parāmāso na hoti. Thāmase thāmasā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), thāmaso (ka.) parāmāse asati rūpasmiṃ… vedanāya [V 2.0043]… saññāya… saṅkhāresu… viññāṇasmiṃ cittaṃ virajjati vimuccati anupādāya āsavehi. Vimuttattā ṭhitaṃ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṃ. Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“For one who sees this as it truly is with right wisdom, speculative views about the past do not arise. When there are no speculative views about the past, speculative views about the future do not arise. When there are no speculative views about the future, there is no tenacious grasping. When there is no tenacious grasping, the mind becomes dispassionate towards form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, and is liberated from the taints without grasping. Being liberated, it is steady. Being steady, it is content. Being content, one is not agitated. Not being agitated, one personally attains Parinibbāna. One understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Fourth.

5. Samanupassanāsuttaṃ

5. The Sutta on Viewing

47. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ attānaṃ samanupassamānā samanupassanti, sabbete pañcupādānakkhandhe samanupassanti, etesaṃ vā aññataraṃ. Katame pañca? Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ [T 3.0058] vā attānaṃ; attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ; attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ”.

47. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins view the self in its many different ways, all of them view the five aggregates subject to clinging, or one or another of them. Which five? Here, bhikkhus, an uninstructed worldling—who has not seen the noble ones, is not skilled in the Dhamma of the noble ones, and is not trained in the Dhamma of the noble ones; who has not seen good persons, is not skilled in the Dhamma of good persons, and is not trained in the Dhamma of good persons—views form as self, or the self as possessing form, or form as in the self, or the self as in form. One views feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or the self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in the self, or the self as in consciousness.”

“Iti ayañceva samanupassanā ‘asmī’ti cassa avigataṃ adhigataṃ (bahūsu) hoti. ‘Asmī’ti kho pana, bhikkhave, avigate pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ avakkanti hoti – cakkhundriyassa sotindriyassa ghānindriyassa jivhindriyassa kāyindriyassa.
