Atthi, bhikkhave, mano, atthi dhammā, atthi avijjādhātu. Avijjāsamphassajena, bhikkhave, vedayitena phuṭṭhassa assutavato puthujjanassa ‘asmī’tipissa hoti; ‘ayamahamasmī’tipissa hoti; ‘bhavissa’ntipissa hoti; ‘na bhavissa’ntipissa hoti; ‘rūpī bhavissa’ntipissa hoti; ‘arūpī bhavissa’ntipissa hoti; ‘saññī bhavissa’ntipissa hoti; ‘asaññī bhavissa’ntipissa hoti; ‘nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissa’ntipissa hoti”.

“Thus, this very viewing occurs, and for him the conceit ‘I am’ is not eliminated. Bhikkhus, when the conceit ‘I am’ is not eliminated, the manifestation of the five faculties occurs—the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, and the body faculty. There is, bhikkhus, the mind, there are mental phenomena, and there is the element of ignorance. Bhikkhus, for an uninstructed worldling, when touched by a feeling born of contact associated with ignorance, there arises for him ‘I am’; there arises for him ‘this I am’; there arises for him ‘I will be’; there arises for him ‘I will not be’; there arises for him ‘I will be possessed of form’; there arises for him ‘I will be formless’; there arises for him ‘I will be percipient’; there arises for him ‘I will be non-percipient’; there arises for him ‘I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient’.”

“Tiṭṭhanteva [M 2.0039][P 3.0047] kho tiṭṭhanti kho pana (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), bhikkhave, tattheva tatheva (katthaci) pañcindriyāni. Athettha sutavato ariyasāvakassa avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati. Tassa avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā ‘asmī’tipissa na hoti; ‘ayamahamasmī’tipissa na hoti; ‘bhavissa’nti… ‘na bhavissa’nti… rūpī… arūpī [V 2.0044]… saññī… asaññī… ‘nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissa’ntipissa na hotī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, the five faculties remain right there. Then, for the instructed noble disciple, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Due to the fading away of ignorance and the arising of true knowledge, the conceit ‘I am’ does not arise for him; ‘this I am’ does not arise for him; ‘I will be’ does not arise for him; ‘I will not be’ does not arise for him; ‘I will be possessed of form’ does not arise for him; ‘I will be formless’ does not arise for him; ‘I will be percipient’ does not arise for him; ‘I will be non-percipient’ does not arise for him; nor does ‘I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient’ arise for him.” The Fifth.

6. Khandhasuttaṃ

6. The Sutta on the Aggregates

48. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Pañca, bhikkhave, khandhe desessāmi[T 3.0059], pañcupādānakkhandhe ca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katame ca, bhikkhave, pañcakkhandhā? Yaṃ kiñci, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, ayaṃ vuccati rūpakkhandho. Yā kāci vedanā…pe… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā…pe… ayaṃ vuccati saṅkhārakkhandho. Yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, ayaṃ vuccati viññāṇakkhandho. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, pañcakkhandhā”.

48. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach the five aggregates and the five aggregates subject to clinging. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, are the five aggregates? Whatever form there is, bhikkhus—whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—this is called the form aggregate. Whatever feeling there is… whatever perception there is… whatever formations there are—whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle… this is called the formations aggregate. Whatever consciousness there is—whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—this is called the consciousness aggregate. These, bhikkhus, are called the five aggregates.”

“Katame ca, bhikkhave, pañcupādānakkhandhā? Yaṃ kiñci, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… yaṃ dūre santike vā sāsavaṃ upādāniyaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati rūpupādānakkhandho. Yā kāci vedanā…pe… yā dūre santike vā sāsavā upādāniyā, ayaṃ vuccati vedanupādānakkhandho. Yā kāci saññā…pe… yā dūre santike vā sāsavā upādāniyā, ayaṃ vuccati saññupādānakkhandho. Ye keci saṅkhārā…pe… sāsavā upādāniyā, ayaṃ vuccati saṅkhārupādānakkhandho. Yaṃ [P 3.0048] kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… [T 3.0060] yaṃ dūre santike vā sāsavaṃ upādāniyaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, pañcupādānakkhandhā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, are the five aggregates subject to clinging? Whatever form there is, bhikkhus—whether past, future, or present… far or near—that is tainted and subject to clinging, this is called the form aggregate subject to clinging. Whatever feeling there is… that is far or near, tainted and subject to clinging, this is called the feeling aggregate subject to clinging. Whatever perception there is… that is far or near, tainted and subject to clinging, this is called the perception aggregate subject to clinging. Whatever formations there are… that are tainted and subject to clinging, this is called the formations aggregate subject to clinging. Whatever consciousness there is—whether past, future, or present… far or near—that is tainted and subject to clinging, this is called the consciousness aggregate subject to clinging. These, bhikkhus, are called the five aggregates subject to clinging.” The sixth.

7. Soṇasuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on Soṇa

49. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha [V 2.0045] kho soṇo gahapatiputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami [M 2.0040] …pe… ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho soṇaṃ gahapatiputtaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

49. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary. Then Soṇa the householder’s son approached the Blessed One… Seated to one side, the Blessed One said this to Soṇa the householder’s son:

“Ye hi keci, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā aniccena rūpena dukkhena vipariṇāmadhammena ‘seyyohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; ‘sadisohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; ‘hīnohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; kimaññatra yathābhūtassa adassanā? Aniccāya vedanāya dukkhāya vipariṇāmadhammāya ‘seyyohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; ‘sadisohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; ‘hīnohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; kimaññatra yathābhūtassa adassanā? Aniccāya saññāya… aniccehi saṅkhārehi dukkhehi vipariṇāmadhammehi ‘seyyohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; ‘sadisohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; ‘hīnohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; kimaññatra yathābhūtassa adassanā? Aniccena viññāṇena dukkhena vipariṇāmadhammena ‘seyyohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; ‘sadisohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; ‘hīnohamasmī’ti vā samanupassanti; kimaññatra yathābhūtassa adassanā?

“Soṇa, whatever ascetics or brahmins, with respect to impermanent, painful, and perishable form, repeatedly contemplate, ‘I am superior,’ or ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior’—what else could this be, other than not seeing it as it really is? With respect to impermanent, painful, and perishable feeling, they repeatedly contemplate, ‘I am superior,’ or ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior’—what else could this be, other than not seeing it as it really is? With respect to impermanent perception… with respect to impermanent, painful, and perishable formations, they repeatedly contemplate, ‘I am superior,’ or ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior’—what else could this be, other than not seeing them as they really are? With respect to impermanent, painful, and perishable consciousness, they repeatedly contemplate, ‘I am superior,’ or ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior’—what else could this be, other than not seeing it as it really is?

“Ye ca kho keci, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā aniccena rūpena dukkhena vipariṇāmadhammena ‘seyyohamasmī’tipi na samanupassanti[T 3.0061]; ‘sadisohamasmī’tipi na samanupassanti[P 3.0049]; ‘hīnohamasmī’tipi na samanupassanti; kimaññatra yathābhūtassa dassanā? Aniccāya vedanāya… aniccāya saññāya… aniccehi saṅkhārehi… aniccena viññāṇena dukkhena vipariṇāmadhammena ‘seyyohamasmī’tipi na samanupassanti; ‘sadisohamasmī’tipi na samanupassanti; ‘hīnohamasmī’tipi na samanupassanti; kimaññatra yathābhūtassa dassanā?

“And indeed, Soṇa, whatever ascetics or brahmins, with respect to impermanent, painful, and perishable form, do not repeatedly contemplate, ‘I am superior,’ nor ‘I am equal,’ nor ‘I am inferior’—what else could this be, other than seeing it as it really is? With respect to impermanent feeling… with respect to impermanent perception… with respect to impermanent formations… with respect to impermanent, painful, and perishable consciousness, they do not repeatedly contemplate, ‘I am superior,’ nor ‘I am equal,’ nor ‘I am inferior’—what else could this be, other than seeing it as it really is?

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, soṇa, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti? “Aniccā, bhante”… “saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ [V 2.0046] vipariṇāmadhammaṃ kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, Soṇa, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fit to be regarded thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.”… “Perception… volitional formations… is consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fit to be regarded thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Tasmātiha[M 2.0041], soṇa, yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ.

“Therefore, Soṇa, whatever form there is—whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—all form should be seen with right wisdom as it actually is: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ [T 3.0062] kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ [P 3.0050] vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ.

“Whatever feeling there is… whatever perception there is… whatever volitional formations there are… whatever consciousness there is—whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—all consciousness should be seen with right wisdom as it actually is: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Evaṃ passaṃ, soṇa, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Seeing thus, Soṇa, the well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, they become dispassionate. Through dispassion, they are liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises, ‘Liberated.’ They understand: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’” The seventh.

8. Dutiyasoṇasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse to Soṇa

50. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho soṇo gahapatiputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho soṇaṃ gahapatiputtaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

50. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary. Then the householder’s son Soṇa approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to the householder’s son Soṇa as he was sitting to one side:

“Ye hi keci, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā rūpaṃ nappajānanti, rūpasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, rūpanirodhaṃ nappajānanti, rūpanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti; vedanaṃ nappajānanti, vedanāsamudayaṃ nappajānanti, vedanānirodhaṃ nappajānanti, vedanānirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ [V 2.0047] nappajānanti; saññaṃ nappajānanti…pe… saṅkhāre nappajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti; viññāṇaṃ nappajānanti, viññāṇasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, viññāṇanirodhaṃ [T 3.0063] nappajānanti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti. Na me te, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.

“Soṇa, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not distinctly understand form, the origin of form, the cessation of form, and the path leading to the cessation of form; who do not distinctly understand feeling, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation; who do not distinctly understand perception…; who do not distinctly understand formations, their origin, their cessation, and the path leading to their cessation; who do not distinctly understand consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation—those, Soṇa, are not considered by me to be ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones do not, having realized it for themselves with higher knowledge in this very life, attain and dwell in the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood.

“Ye [M 2.0042] ca kho keci, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā rūpaṃ pajānanti[P 3.0051], rūpasamudayaṃ pajānanti, rūpanirodhaṃ pajānanti, rūpanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti; vedanaṃ pajānanti…pe… saññaṃ pajānanti… saṅkhāre pajānanti… viññāṇaṃ pajānanti, viññāṇasamudayaṃ pajānanti, viññāṇanirodhaṃ pajānanti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti. Te ca kho me, soṇa, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“But whatever ascetics or brahmins, Soṇa, who distinctly understand form, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation; who distinctly understand feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation—those, Soṇa, are considered by me to be ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones, having realized it for themselves with higher knowledge in this very life, attain and dwell in the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.” The eighth.

9. Nandikkhayasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Destruction of Delight

51. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Aniccaññeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaṃ aniccanti passati. Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Sammā passaṃ nibbindati. Nandikkhayā rāgakkhayo, rāgakkhayā nandikkhayo. Nandirāgakkhayā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ suvimuttanti vuccati. Aniccaññeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vedanaṃ aniccanti passati. Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Sammā passaṃ nibbindati. Nandikkhayā rāgakkhayo, rāgakkhayā [T 3.0064] nandikkhayo. Nandirāgakkhayā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ suvimuttanti vuccati. Anicceyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saññaṃ aniccanti passati…pe… anicceyeva bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅkhāre aniccāti passati. Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Sammā passaṃ nibbindati. Nandikkhayā rāgakkhayo, rāgakkhayā nandikkhayo. Nandirāgakkhayā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ suvimuttanti vuccati. Aniccaññeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu viññāṇaṃ aniccanti passati. Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Sammā passaṃ nibbindati. Nandikkhayā rāgakkhayo, rāgakkhayā nandikkhayo. Nandirāgakkhayā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ suvimuttanti vuccatī”ti. Navamaṃ.

51. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu sees form that is indeed impermanent as ‘impermanent.’ This is his right view. Seeing rightly, he becomes disenchanted. From the destruction of delight comes the destruction of lust; from the destruction of lust comes the destruction of delight. Through the destruction of delight and lust, the mind is liberated; it is called ‘well-liberated.’ Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu sees feeling that is indeed impermanent as ‘impermanent.’ This is his right view. Seeing rightly, he becomes disenchanted. From the destruction of delight comes the destruction of lust; from the destruction of lust comes the destruction of delight. Through the destruction of delight and lust, the mind is liberated; it is called ‘well-liberated.’ Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu sees perception that is indeed impermanent as ‘impermanent’… Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu sees formations that are indeed impermanent as ‘impermanent.’ This is his right view. Seeing rightly, he becomes disenchanted. From the destruction of delight comes the destruction of lust; from the destruction of lust comes the destruction of delight. Through the destruction of delight and lust, the mind is liberated; it is called ‘well-liberated.’ Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu sees consciousness that is indeed impermanent as ‘impermanent.’ This is his right view. Seeing rightly, he becomes disenchanted. From the destruction of delight comes the destruction of lust; from the destruction of lust comes the destruction of delight. Through the destruction of delight and lust, the mind is liberated; it is called ‘well-liberated.’” The ninth.

10. Dutiyanandikkhayasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on the Destruction of Delight

52. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0048]. “Rūpaṃ[P 3.0052], bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karotha, rūpāniccatañca yathābhūtaṃ samanupassatha. Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yoniso manasi karonto, rūpāniccatañca yathābhūtaṃ samanupassanto rūpasmiṃ nibbindati. Nandikkhayā rāgakkhayo, rāgakkhayā nandikkhayo. Nandirāgakkhayā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ suvimuttanti vuccati. Vedanaṃ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karotha, vedanāniccatañca yathābhūtaṃ samanupassatha. Vedanaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yoniso manasi [M 2.0043] karonto, vedanāniccatañca yathābhūtaṃ samanupassanto vedanāya nibbindati. Nandikkhayā rāgakkhayo, rāgakkhayā nandikkhayo. Nandirāgakkhayā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ suvimuttanti vuccati. Saññaṃ bhikkhave… saṅkhāre, bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karotha, saṅkhārāniccatañca yathābhūtaṃ samanupassatha. Saṅkhāre, bhikkhave[T 3.0065], bhikkhu yoniso manasi karonto, saṅkhārāniccataṃ yathābhūtaṃ samanupassanto saṅkhāresu nibbindati. Nandikkhayā rāgakkhayo, rāgakkhayā nandikkhayo. Nandirāgakkhayā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ suvimuttanti vuccati. Viññāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karotha, viññāṇāniccatañca yathābhūtaṃ samanupassatha. Viññāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yoniso manasi karonto, viññāṇāniccatañca yathābhūtaṃ samanupassanto viññāṇasmiṃ nibbindati. Nandikkhayā rāgakkhayo, rāgakkhayā nandikkhayo. Nandirāgakkhayā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ suvimuttanti vuccatī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

52. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, attend carefully to form, and truly see the impermanence of form. A bhikkhu who attends carefully to form and truly sees the impermanence of form becomes disenchanted with form. With the destruction of delight comes the destruction of lust; with the destruction of lust comes the destruction of delight. Through the destruction of delight and lust, the mind is liberated and is called well-liberated. Bhikkhus, attend carefully to feeling, and truly see the impermanence of feeling. A bhikkhu who attends carefully to feeling and truly sees the impermanence of feeling becomes disenchanted with feeling. With the destruction of delight comes the destruction of lust; with the destruction of lust comes the destruction of delight. Through the destruction of delight and lust, the mind is liberated and is called well-liberated. Bhikkhus, attend carefully to perception… Bhikkhus, attend carefully to volitional formations, and truly see the impermanence of volitional formations. A bhikkhu who attends carefully to volitional formations and truly sees the impermanence of volitional formations becomes disenchanted with volitional formations. With the destruction of delight comes the destruction of lust; with the destruction of lust comes the destruction of delight. Through the destruction of delight and lust, the mind is liberated and is called well-liberated. Bhikkhus, attend carefully to consciousness, and truly see the impermanence of consciousness. A bhikkhu who attends carefully to consciousness and truly sees the impermanence of consciousness becomes disenchanted with consciousness. With the destruction of delight comes the destruction of lust; with the destruction of lust comes the destruction of delight. Through the destruction of delight and lust, the mind is liberated and is called well-liberated.” The tenth.

Attadīpavaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter on Oneself as an Island is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that is:

Attadīpā paṭipadā, dve ca honti aniccatā;

Samanupassanā khandhā, dve soṇā dve nandikkhayena cāti.

Oneself as an Island, two on the Way of Practice, Impermanence, Contemplation, Aggregates, two Soṇas, and two on the Destruction of Delight.

Mūlapaṇṇāsako samatto.

The Root Fifty is completed.

Tassa mūlapaṇṇāsakassa vagguddānaṃ –

The summary of the chapters of that Root Fifty is:

Nakulapitā [P 3.0053] anicco ca, bhāro natumhākena ca;

Attadīpena paññāso, paṭhamo tena pavuccatīti.

The Nakulapitā, the Anicca, the Bhāra, the Natumhāka, and the Attadīpa: with these it is the first fifty, and therefore it is called the First Fifty.

6. Upayavaggo

6. The Section on Clinging

1. Upayasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Clinging

53. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0066][V 2.0049]. “Upayo upāyo (bahūsu), bhikkhave, avimutto, anupayo vimutto. Rūpupayaṃ rūpūpāyaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.), rūpupāyaṃ (pī. ka.) vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭheyya, rūpārammaṇaṃ rūpappatiṭṭhaṃ [M 2.0044] nandūpasecanaṃ vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyya. Vedanupayaṃ vā…pe… saññupayaṃ vā…pe… saṅkhārupayaṃ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭheyya, saṅkhārārammaṇaṃ saṅkhārappatiṭṭhaṃ nandūpasecanaṃ vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyya”.

53. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, one who clings is not liberated; one who does not cling is liberated. If, bhikkhus, consciousness were to stand clinging to form, it would stand having form as its object, established in form; being watered by delight, it would attain growth, increase, and expansion. If consciousness were to stand clinging to feeling… If consciousness were to stand clinging to perception… If, bhikkhus, consciousness were to stand clinging to volitional formations, it would stand having volitional formations as its object, established in volitional formations; being watered by delight, it would attain growth, increase, and expansion.”

“Yo, bhikkhave, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahamaññatra rūpā aññatra vedanāya aññatra saññāya aññatra saṅkhārehi viññāṇassa āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā cutiṃ vā upapattiṃ vā vuddhiṃ vā virūḷhiṃ vā vepullaṃ vā paññāpessāmī’ti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Bhikkhus, if anyone should say: ‘I shall make known a coming, a going, a passing away, a rebirth, a growth, an increase, or an expansion of consciousness apart from form, apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from volitional formations’—that is not possible.”

“Rūpadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti. Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṃ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti. Vedanādhātuyā ce, bhikkhave… saññādhātuyā ce bhikkhave… saṅkhāradhātuyā ce bhikkhave… viññāṇadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti. Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṃ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti. Tadappatiṭṭhitaṃ viññāṇaṃ avirūḷhaṃ anabhisaṅkhaccavimuttaṃ[P 3.0054]. Vimuttattā ṭhitaṃ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṃ. Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu has abandoned lust for the form element, then with the abandoning of lust the object is cut off, and there is no establishment for consciousness. If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has abandoned lust for the feeling element… for the perception element… for the volitional formations element… If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has abandoned lust for the consciousness element, then with the abandoning of lust the object is cut off, and there is no establishment for consciousness. That consciousness, being unestablished, not growing, and not fashioning anything further, is liberated. Being liberated, it is steady; being steady, it is content; being content, it is not agitated. Not being agitated, he personally attains parinibbāna. He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’” The first.

2. Bījasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Seeds

54. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0067]. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, bījajātāni. Katamāni pañca? Mūlabījaṃ, khandhabījaṃ, aggabījaṃ, phalubījaṃ, bījabījaññeva pañcamaṃ. Imāni cassu, bhikkhave[V 2.0050], pañca bījajātāni akhaṇḍāni apūtikāni avātātapahatāni sārādāni sārādāyīni (katthaci) sukhasayitāni, pathavī paṭhavī (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ca nāssa, āpo ca nāssa; api numāni api nu imāni (sī. pī.), bhikkhave, pañca bījajātāni vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyyu”nti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Imāni cassu, bhikkhave, pañca bījajātāni akhaṇḍāni…pe… sukhasayitāni, pathavī ca assa, āpo ca assa; api numāni, bhikkhave, pañca bījajātāni vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyyu”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātu, evaṃ catasso viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo daṭṭhabbā. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, āpodhātu, evaṃ nandirāgo daṭṭhabbo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pañca bījajātāni, evaṃ viññāṇaṃ sāhāraṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ”.

54. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of seeds. Which five? Root-seed, stem-seed, bud-seed, joint-seed, and seed-seed as the fifth. If, bhikkhus, these five kinds of seeds were unbroken, unspoiled, unharmed by wind and sun, possessing an essence, and well-kept, but there were no earth and no water, would these five kinds of seeds come to growth, increase, and expansion?” “No, venerable sir.” “If, bhikkhus, these five kinds of seeds were unbroken... well-kept, and there were earth and water, would these five kinds of seeds come to growth, increase, and expansion?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Just as, bhikkhus, the earth element, so should the four stations of consciousness be seen. Just as, bhikkhus, the water element, so should delight and lust be seen. Just as, bhikkhus, the five kinds of seeds, so should consciousness with its nutriment be seen.”

“Rūpupayaṃ[M 2.0045], bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭheyya[P 3.0055], rūpārammaṇaṃ rūpappatiṭṭhaṃ nandūpasecanaṃ vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyya. Vedanupayaṃ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭheyya…pe… saññupayaṃ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭheyya…pe… saṅkhārupayaṃ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭheyya, saṅkhārārammaṇaṃ saṅkhārappatiṭṭhaṃ nandūpasecanaṃ vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyya.

“Monks, consciousness, while standing, might stand resorting to form; taking form as its object, established in form, watered by delight, it would attain growth, increase, and expansion. Or, monks, consciousness, while standing, might stand resorting to feeling... to perception... or, monks, consciousness, while standing, might stand resorting to volitional formations; taking volitional formations as its object, established in volitional formations, watered by delight, it would attain growth, increase, and expansion.”

“Yo, bhikkhave, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahamaññatra rūpā aññatra vedanāya aññatra saññāya [T 3.0068] aññatra saṅkhārehi viññāṇassa āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā cutiṃ vā upapattiṃ vā vuddhiṃ vā virūḷhiṃ vā vepullaṃ vā paññāpessāmī’ti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Monks, if anyone should say: ‘Apart from form, apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from volitional formations, I will declare the coming or going, the passing away or arising, the growth, increase, or expansion of consciousness,’ that would be impossible.”

“Rūpadhātuyā ceva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti. Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṃ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti. Vedanādhātuyā ce… saññādhātuyā ce… saṅkhāradhātuyā ce… viññāṇadhātuyā ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti. Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṃ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti. Tadappatiṭṭhitaṃ viññāṇaṃ avirūḷhaṃ anabhisaṅkhaccavimuttaṃ. Vimuttattā ṭhitaṃ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṃ. Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Monks, when a monk’s lust for the form element is abandoned, due to the abandoning of lust the object is cut off, and there is no support for consciousness. When it is so for the feeling element… for the perception element… for the formations element… Monks, when a monk’s lust for the consciousness element is abandoned, due to the abandoning of lust the object is cut off, and there is no support for consciousness. That consciousness, being unsupported and unproliferating, is unconditioned and liberated. Being liberated, it is steady. Being steady, it is content. Being content, it is not agitated. Not being agitated, one personally attains Nibbāna. One understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the spiritual life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’” The Second.

3. Udānasuttaṃ

3. Discourse on the Inspired Utterance

55. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0051]. Tatra kho bhagavā udānaṃ udānesi – “‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti – evaṃ adhimuccamāno [P 3.0056] bhikkhu chindeyya orambhāgiyāni saṃyojanānī”ti. Evaṃ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yathā kathaṃ pana, bhante, ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti – evaṃ adhimuccamāno bhikkhu chindeyya orambhāgiyāni saṃyojanānī”ti?

55. At Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One uttered this inspired utterance: ‘“If it were not, it would not be for me; if it had not come to be, it will not come to be for me.” A monk who is thus resolved would cut off the lower fetters.’ When this was said, a certain monk said to the Blessed One: ‘But how, venerable sir, for a monk who is thus resolved: “If it were not, it would not be for me; if it had not come to be, it will not come to be for me,” would he cut off the lower fetters?’”

“Idha, bhikkhu, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī…pe… sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā [T 3.0069] attānaṃ; attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ; attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ.

“Here, monk, an uninstructed worldling, who does not see the noble ones… undisciplined in the Dhamma of true persons, regards form as self, or the self as possessing form, or form as in the self, or the self as in form. He regards feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or the self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in the self, or the self as in consciousness.”

“So [M 2.0046] aniccaṃ rūpaṃ ‘aniccaṃ rūpa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, aniccaṃ vedanaṃ ‘aniccā vedanā’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, aniccaṃ saññaṃ ‘aniccā saññā’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, anicce saṅkhāre ‘aniccā saṅkhārā’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, aniccaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘aniccaṃ viññāṇa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti.

“He does not understand impermanent form as it really is, as ‘impermanent form.’ He does not understand impermanent feeling as it really is, as ‘impermanent feeling.’ He does not understand impermanent perception as it really is, as ‘impermanent perception.’ He does not understand impermanent formations as they really are, as ‘impermanent formations.’ He does not understand impermanent consciousness as it really is, as ‘impermanent consciousness.’”

“Dukkhaṃ rūpaṃ ‘dukkhaṃ rūpa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ… dukkhaṃ saññaṃ… dukkhe saṅkhāre… dukkhaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘dukkhaṃ viññāṇa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti.

“He does not understand suffering form as it really is, as ‘suffering form.’ He does not understand suffering feeling… suffering perception… suffering formations… suffering consciousness as it really is, as ‘suffering consciousness.’”

“Anattaṃ rūpaṃ ‘anattā rūpa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, anattaṃ vedanaṃ ‘anattā vedanā’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, anattaṃ saññaṃ ‘anattā saññā’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, anatte saṅkhāre ‘anattā saṅkhārā’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, anattaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘anattā viññāṇa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti.

“He does not understand form that is not-self as it really is, as ‘form is not-self.’ He does not understand feeling that is not-self as it really is, as ‘feeling is not-self.’ He does not understand perception that is not-self as it really is, as ‘perception is not-self.’ He does not understand formations that are not-self as they really are, as ‘formations are not-self.’ He does not understand consciousness that is not-self as it really is, as ‘consciousness is not-self.’”

“Saṅkhataṃ rūpaṃ ‘saṅkhataṃ rūpa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, saṅkhataṃ vedanaṃ… saṅkhataṃ saññaṃ… saṅkhate saṅkhāre… saṅkhataṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘saṅkhataṃ viññāṇa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Rūpaṃ vibhavissatīti [V 2.0052] yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Vedanā vibhavissati… saññā vibhavissati… saṅkhārā vibhavissanti… viññāṇaṃ vibhavissatīti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti.

“He does not understand conditioned form as it really is, as ‘conditioned form.’ He does not understand conditioned feeling… conditioned perception… conditioned formations… conditioned consciousness as it really is, as ‘conditioned consciousness.’ He does not understand as it really is that ‘form will cease.’ He does not understand as it really is that ‘feeling will cease… perception will cease… formations will cease… consciousness will cease.’”

“Sutavā [P 3.0057] ca kho, bhikkhu, ariyasāvako ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa [T 3.0070] kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto na rūpaṃ attato samanupassati…pe… na vedanaṃ… na saññaṃ… na saṅkhāre… na viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati.

“But, monk, the instructed noble disciple, who sees the noble ones, is skilled in the noble Dhamma, is well-trained in the noble Dhamma; who sees true persons, is skilled in the Dhamma of true persons, is well-trained in the Dhamma of true persons, does not regard form as self… nor feeling… nor perception… nor formations… nor consciousness as self.”

“So aniccaṃ rūpaṃ ‘aniccaṃ rūpa’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Aniccaṃ vedanaṃ… aniccaṃ saññaṃ… anicce saṅkhāre… aniccaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘aniccaṃ viññāṇa’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Dukkhaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dukkhaṃ viññāṇaṃ… anattaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… anattaṃ viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhataṃ rūpaṃ…pe… saṅkhataṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘saṅkhataṃ viññāṇa’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Rūpaṃ vibhavissatīti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ vibhavissatīti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti.

“He understands impermanent form as it really is, as ‘impermanent form.’ He understands impermanent feeling… impermanent perception… impermanent formations… impermanent consciousness as it really is, as ‘impermanent consciousness.’ He understands suffering form… suffering consciousness… He understands form that is not-self… consciousness that is not-self… He understands conditioned form… conditioned consciousness as it really is, as ‘conditioned consciousness.’ He understands as it really is that ‘form will perish.’ He understands as it really is that ‘feeling… perception… formations… consciousness will perish.’”

“So [M 2.0047] rūpassa vibhavā, vedanāya vibhavā, saññā vibhavā, saṅkhārānaṃ vibhavā, viññāṇassa vibhavā, evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti – evaṃ adhimuccamāno bhikkhu chindeyya orambhāgiyāni saṃyojanānī”ti. “Evaṃ adhimuccamāno, bhante, bhikkhu chindeyya orambhāgiyāni saṃyojanānī”ti.

“Through the cessation of form, the cessation of feeling, the cessation of perception, the cessation of formations, and the cessation of consciousness, thus, bhikkhu, a bhikkhu who is resolved in this way: ‘It might not be, it might not be for me; it will not be, it will not be for me,’ would sever the lower fetters.” “Venerable sir, a bhikkhu who is resolved in this way would sever the lower fetters.”

“Kathaṃ pana, bhante, jānato kathaṃ passato anantarā āsavānaṃ khayo hotī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, assutavā puthujjano atasitāye ṭhāne tāsaṃ āpajjati. Tāso heso hesā (ka.) bhikkhu assutavato puthujjanassa – ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’”ti.

“Venerable sir, for one knowing in what way, for one seeing in what way, does the immediate destruction of the taints occur?” “Here, bhikkhu, an uninstructed worldling falls into terror in a situation that is not a cause for terror. This, bhikkhu, is the terror for the uninstructed worldling: ‘It might not be, it might not be for me; it will not be, it will not be for me.’”

“Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhu, ariyasāvako atasitāye ṭhāne [T 3.0071] na tāsaṃ āpajjati. Na heso na hesā (ka.), bhikkhu, tāso sutavato ariyasāvakassa – ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti. Rūpupayaṃ [P 3.0058] vā, bhikkhu, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭheyya, rūpārammaṇaṃ rūpappatiṭṭhaṃ [V 2.0053] nandūpasecanaṃ vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyya. Vedanupayaṃ vā, bhikkhu… saññupayaṃ vā, bhikkhu… saṅkhārupayaṃ vā, bhikkhu, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭheyya, saṅkhārārammaṇaṃ saṅkhārappatiṭṭhaṃ nandūpasecanaṃ vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyya.

“But a learned noble disciple, bhikkhu, does not fall into terror in a situation that is not a cause for terror. This is not a terror for the learned noble disciple: ‘It might not be, it might not be for me; it will not be, it will not be for me.’ If, bhikkhu, consciousness, while established, were to be established by resorting to form, with form as its object, with form as its support, and nurtured by delight, it would attain growth, increase, and expansion. Or if, bhikkhu, by resorting to feeling… or if, bhikkhu, by resorting to perception… or if, bhikkhu, consciousness, while established, were to be established by resorting to formations, with formations as its object, with formations as its support, and nurtured by delight, it would attain growth, increase, and expansion.

“Yo so (sabbattha) bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahamaññatra rūpā, aññatra vedanāya, aññatra saññāya, aññatra saṅkhārehi viññāṇassa āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā cutiṃ vā upapattiṃ vā vuddhiṃ vā virūḷhiṃ vā vepullaṃ vā paññāpessāmī’ti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“If a bhikkhu were to say, ‘Apart from form, apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from formations, I shall make known the coming or going, the passing away or reappearance, the growth, increase, or expansion of consciousness,’ that situation does not exist.

“Rūpadhātuyā ce, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti. Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṃ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti. Vedanādhātuyā ce, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno… saññādhātuyā ce, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno… saṅkhāradhātuyā ce, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno… viññāṇadhātuyā ce, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno rāgo pahīno hoti. Rāgassa pahānā vocchijjatārammaṇaṃ patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti. Tadappatiṭṭhitaṃ viññāṇaṃ avirūḷhaṃ anabhisaṅkhārañca vimuttaṃ. Vimuttattā ṭhitaṃ. Ṭhitattā santusitaṃ. Santusitattā na paritassati. Aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati. ‘Khīṇā jāti…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti [M 2.0048] pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, jānato evaṃ passato anantarā āsavānaṃ khayo hotī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“If, bhikkhu, a bhikkhu’s passion for the form element is abandoned, with the abandoning of passion the object is cut off, and there is no establishment for consciousness. If, bhikkhu, for the feeling element… If, bhikkhu, for the perception element… If, bhikkhu, for the formations element… If, bhikkhu, a bhikkhu’s passion for the consciousness element is abandoned, with the abandoning of passion the object is cut off, and there is no establishment for consciousness. That consciousness, being unestablished, not growing, and unconstructed, is liberated. Being liberated, it is steady. Being steady, it is satisfied. Being satisfied, it is not agitated. Not being agitated, one personally attains Parinibbāna. One understands: ‘Destroyed is birth… there is no more for this state of being.’ Thus, bhikkhu, for one who knows thus and sees thus, there is the immediate destruction of the taints.” The Third.

4. Upādānaparipavattasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Cycle of Clinging

56. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0072]. “Pañcime, bhikkhave, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho[P 3.0059], saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ime pañcupādānakkhandhe catuparivaṭṭaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ, neva tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṃ. Yato ca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ime pañcupādānakkhandhe catuparivaṭṭaṃ yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ[V 2.0054], athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke…pe… sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṃ”.

56. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these five aggregates of clinging. What are the five? The aggregate of clinging to form, the aggregate of clinging to feeling, the aggregate of clinging to perception, the aggregate of clinging to formations, and the aggregate of clinging to consciousness. For as long, bhikkhus, as I did not directly know these five aggregates of clinging in their four aspects as they really are, for so long, bhikkhus, I did not claim to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. But when, bhikkhus, I directly knew these five aggregates of clinging in their four aspects as they really are, then I claimed to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas… with its devas and humans.”

“Kathañca catuparivaṭṭaṃ? Rūpaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, rūpasamudayaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, rūpanirodhaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, rūpanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ; vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, viññāṇasamudayaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, viññāṇanirodhaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ.

“And how is it fourfold? I directly knew form, I directly knew the origin of form, I directly knew the cessation of form, I directly knew the path leading to the cessation of form. I directly knew feeling… perception… formations… I directly knew consciousness, I directly knew the origin of consciousness, I directly knew the cessation of consciousness, I directly knew the path leading to the cessation of consciousness.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ? Cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ. Āhārasamudayā rūpasamudayo; āhāranirodhā rūpanirodho. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo rūpanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“And what, bhikkhus, is form? The four great elements and form derived from the four great elements. This, bhikkhus, is called form. From the arising of nutriment, there is the arising of form; from the cessation of nutriment, there is the cessation of form. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice that leads to the cessation of form, that is: right view … right concentration.”

“Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā [T 3.0073] vā evaṃ rūpaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpasamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpanirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya rūpassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā. Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṃ dhammavinaye gādhanti.

“Whatever ascetics or brahmins, bhikkhus, who, having directly known form in this way, having directly known the origin of form, having directly known the cessation of form, having directly known the path leading to the cessation of form, are practicing for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form—they are practicing well. Those who are practicing well gain a foothold in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

“Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ rūpaṃ abhiññāya…pe… evaṃ rūpanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya, rūpassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā te suvimuttā. Ye suvimuttā te kevalino. Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya.

“And whatever ascetics or brahmins, bhikkhus, who, having thus directly known form… and having thus directly known the path leading to the cessation of form, are, through disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, and non-clinging with regard to form, liberated—they are well-liberated. Those who are well-liberated are consummate. For those who are consummate, there is no round of existence to be designated for them.”

“Katamā [M 2.0049] ca, bhikkhave, vedanā? Chayime, bhikkhave, vedanākāyā [P 3.0060] – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, vedanā. Phassasamudayā vedanāsamudayo; phassanirodhā vedanānirodho. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“And what, bhikkhus, is feeling? These are the six classes of feeling: feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-contact. This, bhikkhus, is called feeling. With the arising of contact, there is the arising of feeling; with the cessation of contact, there is the cessation of feeling. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice that leads to the cessation of feeling, namely: right view… right concentration.”

“Ye [V 2.0055] hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ vedanaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ vedanāsamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ vedanānirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ vedanānirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya vedanāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā. Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṃ dhammavinaye gādhanti.

“Indeed, bhikkhus, whatever contemplatives or brahmins who, having thus directly comprehended feeling, having thus directly comprehended the origin of feeling, having thus directly comprehended the cessation of feeling, and having thus directly comprehended the path leading to the cessation of feeling, are practicing for disenchantment with, dispassion toward, and cessation of feeling—they are practicing well. Those who are practicing well are well-established in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

“Ye ca kho keci[T 3.0074], bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ vedanaṃ abhiññāya…pe… evaṃ vedanānirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya…pe… vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya.

“And indeed, bhikkhus, whatever contemplatives or brahmins who, having thus directly comprehended feeling… and having thus directly comprehended the path leading to the cessation of feeling… are, through disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, and non-clinging, liberated—they are well-liberated. Those who are well-liberated are consummate. For those who are consummate, there is no cycle to be designated.”

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, saññā? Chayime, bhikkhave, saññākāyā – rūpasaññā, saddasaññā, gandhasaññā, rasasaññā, phoṭṭhabbasaññā, dhammasaññā. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, saññā. Phassasamudayā saññāsamudayo; phassanirodhā saññānirodho. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saññānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi…pe… vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya.

“And what, bhikkhus, is perception? These are the six classes of perception: perception of forms, perception of sounds, perception of smells, perception of tastes, perception of tangibles, perception of mental objects. This, bhikkhus, is called perception. With the arising of contact, there is the arising of perception; with the cessation of contact, there is the cessation of perception. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice that leads to the cessation of perception, namely: right view… right concentration… For them, there is no cycle to be designated.”

“Katame ca, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā? Chayime, bhikkhave, cetanākāyā – rūpasañcetanā, saddasañcetanā, gandhasañcetanā, rasasañcetanā, phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā, dhammasañcetanā. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā. Phassasamudayā saṅkhārasamudayo; phassanirodhā saṅkhāranirodho. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅkhāranirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“And what, bhikkhus, are formations? These six, bhikkhus, are the bodies of volition: volition directed at forms, volition directed at sounds, volition directed at odors, volition directed at tastes, volition directed at tangible objects, and volition directed at mental phenomena. These, bhikkhus, are called formations. From the arising of contact, there is the arising of formations; from the cessation of contact, there is the cessation of formations. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice leading to the cessation of formations, that is: Right View… Right Concentration.”

“Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ saṅkhāre abhiññāya, evaṃ saṅkhārasamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ saṅkhāranirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ [T 3.0075] paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya saṅkhārānaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya [P 3.0061] nirodhāya [M 2.0050] paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā. Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṃ dhammavinaye gādhanti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins, having thus directly known formations, having thus directly known the origin of formations, having thus directly known the cessation of formations, and having thus directly known the practice leading to the cessation of formations, are practicing for disenchantment with, for dispassion toward, and for the cessation of formations—they are practicing well. Those who are practicing well gain a foothold in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

“Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ saṅkhāre abhiññāya, evaṃ saṅkhārasamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ saṅkhāranirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ [V 2.0056] abhiññāya saṅkhārānaṃ nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā, te suvimuttā. Ye suvimuttā, te kevalino. Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya.

“And furthermore, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins, having thus directly known formations, having thus directly known the origin of formations, having thus directly known the cessation of formations, and having thus directly known the practice leading to the cessation of formations, are, through disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, and non-clinging, liberated—they are well-liberated. Those who are well-liberated are consummate. For those who are consummate, there is no cycle for their designation.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ? Chayime, bhikkhave, viññāṇakāyā – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ. Nāmarūpasamudayā viññāṇasamudayo; nāmarūpanirodhā viññāṇanirodho. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo viññāṇanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“And what, bhikkhus, is consciousness? These six, bhikkhus, are the bodies of consciousness: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. This, bhikkhus, is called consciousness. From the arising of name-and-form, there is the arising of consciousness; from the cessation of name-and-form, there is the cessation of consciousness. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice leading to the cessation of consciousness, that is: Right View… Right Concentration.”

“Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ viññāṇaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇasamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇanirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya viññāṇassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā. Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṃ dhammavinaye gādhanti.

“Bhikkhus, whatsoever ascetics or brahmins, having directly known consciousness thus, having directly known the origin of consciousness thus, having directly known the cessation of consciousness thus, having directly known the practice leading to the cessation of consciousness thus, are practicing for disenchantment with consciousness, for dispassion, for cessation—they are practicing well. Those who are practicing well gain a firm footing in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

“Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ viññāṇaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇasamudayaṃ [T 3.0076] abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇanirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya viññāṇassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā, te suvimuttā. Ye suvimuttā, te kevalino. Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāyā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, whatsoever ascetics or brahmins, having directly known consciousness thus, having directly known the origin of consciousness thus, having directly known the cessation of consciousness thus, having directly known the practice leading to the cessation of consciousness thus, are liberated without clinging through disenchantment with, dispassion toward, and cessation of consciousness—they are well-liberated. Those who are well-liberated are accomplished. For those who are accomplished, there is no cycle to be designated.”

5. Sattaṭṭhānasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Seven Grounds

57. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Sattaṭṭhānakusalo, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tividhūpaparikkhī imasmiṃ dhammavinaye kevalī vusitavā uttamapurisoti vuccati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sattaṭṭhānakusalo hoti? Idha[P 3.0062], bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaṃ pajānāti, rūpasamudayaṃ pajānāti, rūpanirodhaṃ pajānāti, rūpanirodhagāminiṃ [M 2.0051] paṭipadaṃ pajānāti; rūpassa assādaṃ pajānāti, rūpassa ādīnavaṃ pajānāti, rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ pajānāti; vedanaṃ pajānāti [V 2.0057]… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ pajānāti, viññāṇasamudayaṃ pajānāti, viññāṇanirodhaṃ pajānāti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānāti; viññāṇassa assādaṃ pajānāti, viññāṇassa ādīnavaṃ pajānāti, viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ pajānāti.

57. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who is skilled in the seven grounds and who investigates in three ways is called, in this Dhamma and Discipline, an accomplished one, one who has lived the holy life, a supreme person. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu skilled in the seven grounds? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu understands form, understands the origin of form, understands the cessation of form, and understands the practice leading to the cessation of form; he understands the gratification in form, the danger in form, and the escape from form. He understands feeling… perception… volitional formations… he understands consciousness, understands the origin of consciousness, understands the cessation of consciousness, and understands the practice leading to the cessation of consciousness; he understands the gratification in consciousness, the danger in consciousness, and the escape from consciousness.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ? Cattāro ca mahābhūtā, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ. Āhārasamudayā rūpasamudayo; āhāranirodhā rūpanirodho. Ayameva ariyo [T 3.0077] aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo rūpanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“And what, bhikkhus, is form? The four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements. This, bhikkhus, is called form. From the origination of nutriment is the origination of form; from the cessation of nutriment is the cessation of form. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice leading to the cessation of form, that is: Right View… Right Concentration.”

“Yaṃ rūpaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ – ayaṃ rūpassa assādo. Yaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ – ayaṃ rūpassa ādīnavo. Yo rūpasmiṃ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ – idaṃ rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ.

“Whatever pleasure and mental joy arise in dependence on form—this is the gratification of form. That form is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger of form. The removal of desire and lust, the abandoning of desire and lust for form—this is the escape from form.”

“Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ rūpaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpasamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpanirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya; evaṃ rūpassa assādaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpassa ādīnavaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ abhiññāya rūpassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā. Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṃ dhammavinaye gādhanti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins, having directly known form thus, having directly known the origination of form thus, having directly known the cessation of form thus, having directly known the practice leading to the cessation of form thus; having directly known the gratification of form thus, having directly known the danger of form thus, having directly known the escape from form thus, are practicing for disenchantment with, dispassion toward, and cessation of form—they are practicing well. Those who are practicing well gain a footing in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

“Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ rūpaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpasamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpanirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya; evaṃ rūpassa assādaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpassa ādīnavaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ [P 3.0063] abhiññāya rūpassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā, te suvimuttā. Ye suvimuttā, te kevalino. Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya.

“Moreover, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins who, having directly known form thus, having directly known the origination of form thus, having directly known the cessation of form thus, having directly known the practice leading to the cessation of form thus; having directly known the gratification of form thus, having directly known the danger of form thus, having directly known the escape from form thus, are, through disenchantment with, dispassion toward, and the cessation of form, liberated without clinging—they are well-liberated. Those who are well-liberated are consummate. For those who are consummate, there is no round for designation.”

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, vedanā? Chayime, bhikkhave, vedanākāyā – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā…pe… [V 2.0058] manosamphassajā vedanā. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, vedanā. Phassasamudayā vedanāsamudayo; phassanirodhā [T 3.0078] vedanānirodho. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“And what, bhikkhus, is feeling? These six are the classes of feeling, bhikkhus: feeling born of eye-contact… feeling born of mind-contact. This, bhikkhus, is called feeling. From the origination of contact is the origination of feeling; from the cessation of contact is the cessation of feeling. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice leading to the cessation of feeling, that is: Right View… Right Concentration.”

“Yaṃ [M 2.0052] vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ – ayaṃ vedanāya assādo. Yā vedanā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā – ayaṃ vedanāya ādīnavo. Yo vedanāya chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ – idaṃ vedanāya nissaraṇaṃ.

“Whatever pleasure and mental joy arise in dependence on feeling—this is the gratification of feeling. That feeling is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger of feeling. The removal of desire and lust, the abandoning of desire and lust for feeling—this is the escape from feeling.”

“Ye hi, keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ vedanaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ vedanāsamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ vedanānirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ vedanānirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya; evaṃ vedanāya assādaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ vedanāya ādīnavaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ vedanāya nissaraṇaṃ abhiññāya vedanāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā. Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṃ dhammavinaye gādhanti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins, having directly known feeling thus, having directly known the origination of feeling thus, having directly known the cessation of feeling thus, having directly known the practice leading to the cessation of feeling thus; having directly known the gratification of feeling thus, having directly known the danger of feeling thus, having directly known the escape from feeling thus, are practicing for disenchantment with, dispassion toward, and cessation of feeling—they are practicing well. Those who are practicing well gain a footing in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

“Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ vedanaṃ abhiññāya…pe… vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya.

“And indeed, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins, having directly known feeling thus… there is no round for them to be designated.”

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, saññā? Chayime, bhikkhave, saññākāyā – rūpasaññā, saddasaññā, gandhasaññā, rasasaññā, phoṭṭhabbasaññā, dhammasaññā. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, saññā. Phassasamudayā saññāsamudayo; phassanirodhā saññānirodho. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saññānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi…pe… vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya.

“And what, bhikkhus, is perception? These six are the classes of perception, bhikkhus: perception of forms, perception of sounds, perception of odors, perception of tastes, perception of tactile objects, and perception of mental phenomena. This, bhikkhus, is called perception. From the origination of contact is the origination of perception; from the cessation of contact is the cessation of perception. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice leading to the cessation of perception, that is: Right View… Right Concentration… there is no round for them to be designated.”

“Katame [T 3.0079] ca, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā? Chayime, bhikkhave, cetanākāyā – rūpasañcetanā, saddasañcetanā, gandhasañcetanā, rasasañcetanā, phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā, dhammasañcetanā. Ime vuccanti bhikkhave[V 2.0059], saṅkhārā. Phassasamudayā saṅkhārasamudayo; phassanirodhā saṅkhāranirodho[P 3.0064]. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅkhāranirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“And what, bhikkhus, are formations? These six, bhikkhus, are classes of volition: volition regarding forms, volition regarding sounds, volition regarding odors, volition regarding tastes, volition regarding tactile objects, and volition regarding mental phenomena. These, bhikkhus, are called formations. From the origination of contact is the origination of formations; from the cessation of contact is the cessation of formations. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice leading to the cessation of formations, that is: Right View… Right Concentration.”

“Yaṃ saṅkhāre paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ – ayaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ assādo. Ye saṅkhārā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā – ayaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavo. Yo saṅkhāresu chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ – idaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ.

“Whatever pleasure and mental joy arise in dependence on formations—this is the gratification of formations. That formations are impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger of formations. The removal of desire and lust, the abandoning of desire and lust for formations—this is the escape from formations.”

“Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ saṅkhāre abhiññāya, evaṃ saṅkhārasamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ saṅkhāranirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya…pe… saṅkhārānaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya [M 2.0053] paṭipannā te suppaṭipannā. Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṃ dhammavinaye gādhanti…pe… vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya.

“Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins, having thus directly known formations, having thus directly known the origination of formations, having thus directly known the cessation of formations, having thus directly known the practice leading to the cessation of formations… are practicing for disenchantment with, dispassion toward, and cessation of formations—they are practicing well. Those who are practicing well gain a footing in this Dhamma and Discipline… There is no round for them to be designated.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ? Chayime, bhikkhave, viññāṇakāyā – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ. Nāmarūpasamudayā viññāṇasamudayo; nāmarūpanirodhā viññāṇanirodho. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo viññāṇanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“And what, bhikkhus, is consciousness? These six, bhikkhus, are classes of consciousness: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. This, bhikkhus, is called consciousness. From the arising of name-and-form, there is the arising of consciousness; from the cessation of name-and-form, there is the cessation of consciousness. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice leading to the cessation of consciousness, that is: right view… right concentration.”

“Yaṃ [T 3.0080] viññāṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ – ayaṃ viññāṇassa assādo. Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ – ayaṃ viññāṇassa ādīnavo. Yo viññāṇasmiṃ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ – idaṃ viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ.

“Whatever pleasure and joy arise in dependence on consciousness: this is the gratification of consciousness. That consciousness is impermanent, suffering, and of a nature to change: this is the danger of consciousness. Whatever is the removal of desire and lust, the abandoning of desire and lust for consciousness: this is the escape from consciousness.”

“Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ viññāṇaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇasamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇanirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya; evaṃ viññāṇassa assādaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇassa ādīnavaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ abhiññāya viññāṇassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipannā, te suppaṭipannā. Ye suppaṭipannā, te imasmiṃ dhammavinaye gādhanti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins who, having directly known consciousness in this way, having directly known the origin of consciousness, having directly known the cessation of consciousness, having directly known the way leading to the cessation of consciousness; having directly known the gratification of consciousness, having directly known the danger of consciousness, having directly known the escape from consciousness, are practicing for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness—they are practicing well. Those who practice well gain a firm footing in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

“Ye [V 2.0060][P 3.0065] ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā evaṃ viññāṇaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇasamudayaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇanirodhaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhiññāya; evaṃ viññāṇassa assādaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇassa ādīnavaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ abhiññāya viññāṇassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā, te suvimuttā. Ye suvimuttā, te kevalino. Ye kevalino vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sattaṭṭhānakusalo hoti.

“And indeed, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins who, having directly known consciousness in this way, having directly known the origin of consciousness, having directly known the cessation of consciousness, having directly known the way leading to the cessation of consciousness; having directly known the gratification of consciousness, having directly known the danger of consciousness, having directly known the escape from consciousness, through disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness, are liberated without clinging—they are well liberated. Those who are well liberated are consummate. For those who are consummate, there is no round for designation. Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is skilled in seven points.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tividhūpaparikkhī hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhātuso upaparikkhati, āyatanaso upaparikkhati, paṭiccasamuppādaso upaparikkhati[T 3.0081][M 2.0054]. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tividhūpaparikkhī hoti. Sattaṭṭhānakusalo, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tividhūpaparikkhī, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye kevalī vusitavā ‘uttamapuriso’ti vuccatī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu an investigator in three ways? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu investigates in terms of elements, investigates in terms of sense bases, and investigates in terms of dependent origination. Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is an investigator in three ways. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who is skilled in seven points and an investigator in three ways is called in this Dhamma and Discipline a consummate one, one who has lived the holy life, a supreme person.” The Fifth.

6. Sammāsambuddhasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One

58. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Tathāgato, bhikkhave, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho rūpassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto sammāsambuddhoti vuccati. Bhikkhupi, bhikkhave, paññāvimutto rūpassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto paññāvimuttoti vuccati.

58. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, being liberated through disenchantment with form, dispassion, cessation, and non-clinging, is called a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu liberated by wisdom, being liberated through disenchantment with form, dispassion, cessation, and non-clinging, is also called one liberated by wisdom.”

“Tathāgato, bhikkhave, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vedanāya nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto sammāsambuddhoti vuccati. Bhikkhupi, bhikkhave, paññāvimutto vedanāya nibbidā…pe… paññāvimuttoti vuccati.

“Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, being liberated through disenchantment with feeling, dispassion, cessation, and non-clinging, is called a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu liberated by wisdom, being liberated through disenchantment with feeling… is also called one liberated by wisdom.”

“Tathāgato, bhikkhave, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho saññāya… saṅkhārānaṃ… viññāṇassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā [P 3.0066] anupādā vimutto sammāsambuddhoti vuccati. Bhikkhupi, bhikkhave, paññāvimutto viññāṇassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto paññāvimuttoti vuccati.

“Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, being liberated through disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, and non-clinging with regard to perception… formations… and consciousness, is called a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu liberated by wisdom, being liberated through disenchantment with consciousness, dispassion, cessation, and non-clinging, is also called one liberated by wisdom.”

“Tatra [V 2.0061] kho, bhikkhave, ko viseso, ko adhippayāso adhippāyo (sī.), adhippāyaso (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ, tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa paññāvimuttena bhikkhunā”ti? “Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaññeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti. “Tena hi, bhikkhave[T 3.0082], suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“In this regard, bhikkhus, what is the distinction, what is the superiority, what is the difference between the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, and a bhikkhu liberated by wisdom?” “Venerable sir, our teachings have the Blessed One as their root, their guide, and their refuge. It would be good if the Blessed One himself would clarify the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will remember it.” “Then listen, bhikkhus, and pay close attention; I will speak.” “So be it, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Tathāgato, bhikkhave, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā, asañjātassa maggassa sañjanetā sañjānetā (syā. kaṃ.), anakkhātassa maggassa akkhātā maggaññū, maggavidū, maggakovido; maggānugā ca, bhikkhave, etarahi sāvakā viharanti pacchāsamannāgatā. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, viseso, ayaṃ adhippayāso, idaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa paññāvimuttena bhikkhunā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is the producer of the unarisen path, the generator of the unknown path, the declarer of the undeclared path. He is the knower of the path, the discoverer of the path, the expert on the path. And now, bhikkhus, his disciples dwell following the path, having come after him. This, bhikkhus, is the distinction, this is the superiority, this is the difference between the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, and a bhikkhu liberated by wisdom.” The Sixth.

7. Anattalakkhaṇasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Characteristic of Non-self

59. Ekaṃ [M 2.0055] samayaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye. Tatra kho bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

59. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana. There the Blessed One addressed the group of five bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus.” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, anattā. Rūpañca hidaṃ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṃ rūpaṃ ābādhāya saṃvatteyya, labbhetha ca rūpe – ‘evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotu, evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī’ti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ anattā, tasmā rūpaṃ ābādhāya saṃvattati, na ca labbhati rūpe – ‘evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotu, evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, form is not-self. If, bhikkhus, form were self, this form would not lead to affliction, and one could exercise mastery over form, thinking: ‘Let my form be thus; let my form not be thus.’ But because, bhikkhus, form is not-self, therefore form leads to affliction, and one cannot exercise mastery over form, thinking: ‘Let my form be thus; let my form not be thus.’”

“Vedanā anattā. Vedanā ca hidaṃ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṃ vedanā ābādhāya saṃvatteyya, labbhetha [P 3.0067] ca vedanāya – ‘evaṃ me vedanā hotu, evaṃ me vedanā mā ahosī’ti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, vedanā anattā, tasmā vedanā ābādhāya saṃvattati[T 3.0083], na ca labbhati vedanāya – ‘evaṃ me vedanā hotu, evaṃ me vedanā mā ahosī’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, feeling is not-self. If, bhikkhus, feeling were self, this feeling would not lead to affliction, and it would be possible to have one's way with feeling: ‘Let my feeling be thus; let my feeling not be thus.’ But because, bhikkhus, feeling is not-self, therefore feeling leads to affliction, and it is not possible to have one's way with feeling: ‘Let my feeling be thus; let my feeling not be thus.’”

“Saññā [V 2.0062] anattā…pe… saṅkhārā anattā. Saṅkhārā ca hidaṃ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissaṃsu, nayidaṃ saṅkhārā ābādhāya saṃvatteyyuṃ, labbhetha ca saṅkhāresu – ‘evaṃ me saṅkhārā hontu, evaṃ me saṅkhārā mā ahesu’nti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā anattā, tasmā saṅkhārā ābādhāya saṃvattanti, na ca labbhati saṅkhāresu – ‘evaṃ me saṅkhārā hontu, evaṃ me saṅkhārā mā ahesu’”nti.

“Perception is not-self… Volitional formations are not-self. If, bhikkhus, volitional formations were self, they would not lead to affliction, and it would be possible to have one's way with volitional formations: ‘Let my volitional formations be thus; let my volitional formations not be thus.’ But because, bhikkhus, volitional formations are not-self, they lead to affliction, and it is not possible to have one's way with volitional formations: ‘Let my volitional formations be thus; let my volitional formations not be thus.’”

“Viññāṇaṃ anattā. Viññāṇañca hidaṃ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṃ viññāṇaṃ ābādhāya saṃvatteyya, labbhetha ca viññāṇe – ‘evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ hotu, evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ mā ahosī’ti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ anattā, tasmā viññāṇaṃ ābādhāya saṃvattati, na ca labbhati viññāṇe – ‘evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ hotu, evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ mā ahosī’”ti.

“Consciousness is not-self. If, bhikkhus, consciousness were self, it would not lead to affliction, and it would be possible to have one's way with consciousness: ‘Let my consciousness be thus; let my consciousness not be thus.’ But because, bhikkhus, consciousness is not-self, it leads to affliction, and it is not possible to have one's way with consciousness: ‘Let my consciousness be thus; let my consciousness not be thus.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me [M 2.0056] attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ [T 3.0084] sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ[P 3.0068], bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And is that which is impermanent suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And is it fitting to regard that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And is that which is impermanent suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And is it fitting to regard that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yā kāci vedanā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā…pe… yā dūre santike vā, sabbā [V 2.0063] vedanā – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, whatever form there is—whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—all form should be seen as it actually is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling there is—whether past, future, or present; internal or external… far or near—all feeling should be seen as it actually is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Yā kāci saññā…pe… ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā…pe… ye dūre santike vā, sabbe saṅkhārā – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ.
