“Whatever perception there is… Whatever volitional formations there are—whether past, future, or present; internal or external… far or near—all volitional formations should be seen as they actually are with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ.

“Whatever consciousness there is—whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—all consciousness should be seen as it actually is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā [T 3.0085] vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.

“Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with volitional formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When he is liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanduṃ abhinandunti (ka.).

The Blessed One said this. The monks of the group of five, delighted, rejoiced in the Blessed One's speech.

Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne pañcavaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsūti. Sattamaṃ.

And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of the monks of the group of five were liberated from the taints through non-clinging. The Seventh.

8. Mahālisuttaṃ

8. The Mahāli Sutta

60. Evaṃ [M 2.0057] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Atha kho mahāli licchavi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami [P 3.0069] …pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahāli licchavi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

60. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Then Mahāli the Licchavi approached the Blessed One and, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One:

“Pūraṇo, bhante, kassapo evamāha – ‘natthi hetu natthi paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya; ahetū [V 2.0064] appaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti. Natthi hetu natthi paccayo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā; ahetū appaccayā sattā visujjhantī’ti. Idha, bhagavā kimāhā”ti?

“Venerable sir, Pūraṇa Kassapa says this: ‘There is no cause, no condition for the defilement of beings; without cause and without condition, beings are defiled. There is no cause, no condition for the purification of beings; without cause and without condition, beings are purified.’ In this regard, what does the Blessed One say?”

“Atthi, mahāli, hetu atthi paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya; sahetū sappaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti. Atthi, mahāli, hetu, atthi paccayo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā; sahetū sappaccayā sattā visujjhantī”ti.

“There is, Mahāli, a cause and a condition for the defilement of beings; with cause and with condition, beings are defiled. There is, Mahāli, a cause and a condition for the purification of beings; with cause and with condition, beings are purified.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, hetu katamo paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya; kathaṃ sahetū sappaccayā sattā saṃkilissantī”ti?

“But what, venerable sir, is the cause and what is the condition for the defilement of beings? How is it that with cause and with condition, beings are defiled?”

“Rūpañca hidaṃ, mahāli, ekantadukkhaṃ abhavissa dukkhānupatitaṃ dukkhāvakkantaṃ anavakkantaṃ sukhena, nayidaṃ sattā rūpasmiṃ [T 3.0086] sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, rūpaṃ sukhaṃ sukhānupatitaṃ sukhāvakkantaṃ anavakkantaṃ dukkhena, tasmā sattā rūpasmiṃ sārajjanti; sārāgā saṃyujjanti; saṃyogā saṃkilissanti. Ayaṃ kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya; evaṃ sahetū sappaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti.

“If, Mahāli, this form were exclusively painful, followed by pain, pervaded by pain, and unpervaded by pleasure, beings would not be passionately attached to form. But because, Mahāli, form is pleasant, followed by pleasure, pervaded by pleasure, and unpervaded by pain, beings are passionately attached to form. Being passionately attached, they are fettered; being fettered, they are defiled. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the defilement of beings; thus, with cause and with condition, beings are defiled.”

“Vedanā ca hidaṃ, mahāli, ekantadukkhā abhavissa dukkhānupatitā dukkhāvakkantā anavakkantā sukhena, nayidaṃ sattā vedanāya sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, vedanā sukhā sukhānupatitā sukhāvakkantā anavakkantā dukkhena, tasmā sattā vedanāya sārajjanti; sārāgā saṃyujjanti; saṃyogā saṃkilissanti. Ayampi kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya. Evampi sahetū sappaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti.

“Indeed, Mahāli, if this feeling were exclusively suffering, followed by suffering, pervaded by suffering, and not pervaded by pleasure, these beings would not be intensely attached to feeling. And because, Mahāli, feeling is pleasure, followed by pleasure, pervaded by pleasure, and not pervaded by suffering, therefore beings are intensely attached to feeling. Due to intense attachment, they are yoked; due to being yoked, they are defiled. This indeed, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the defilement of beings. Thus, with cause and with condition, beings are defiled.”

“Saññā ca hidaṃ, mahāli…pe… saṅkhārā ca hidaṃ, mahāli, ekantadukkhā abhavissaṃsu dukkhānupatitā dukkhāvakkantā anavakkantā sukhena, nayidaṃ sattā [M 2.0058] saṅkhāresu sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, saṅkhārā sukhā sukhānupatitā sukhāvakkantā [P 3.0070] anavakkantā dukkhena, tasmā sattā saṅkhāresu sārajjanti; sārāgā saṃyujjanti; saṃyogā saṃkilissanti. Ayampi kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya. Evampi sahetū sappaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti.

“And this perception, Mahāli… and these volitional formations, Mahāli, if they were exclusively suffering, followed by suffering, pervaded by suffering, and not pervaded by pleasure, these beings would not be intensely attached to volitional formations. And because, Mahāli, volitional formations are pleasure, followed by pleasure, pervaded by pleasure, and not pervaded by suffering, therefore beings are intensely attached to volitional formations. Due to intense attachment, they are yoked; due to being yoked, they are defiled. This indeed, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the defilement of beings. Thus, with cause and with condition, beings are defiled.”

“Viññāṇañca [V 2.0065] hidaṃ, mahāli, ekantadukkhaṃ abhavissa dukkhānupatitaṃ dukkhāvakkantaṃ anavakkantaṃ sukhena, nayidaṃ sattā viññāṇasmiṃ sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho[T 3.0087], mahāli, viññāṇaṃ sukhaṃ sukhānupatitaṃ sukhāvakkantaṃ anavakkantaṃ dukkhena, tasmā sattā viññāṇasmiṃ sārajjanti; sārāgā saṃyujjanti; saṃyogā saṃkilissanti. Ayampi kho, mahāli, hetu ayaṃ paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya. Evampi sahetū sappaccayā sattā saṃkilissantī”ti.

“And this consciousness, Mahāli, if it were exclusively suffering, followed by suffering, pervaded by suffering, and not pervaded by pleasure, these beings would not be intensely attached to consciousness. And because, Mahāli, consciousness is pleasure, followed by pleasure, pervaded by pleasure, and not pervaded by suffering, therefore beings are intensely attached to consciousness. Due to intense attachment, they are yoked; due to being yoked, they are defiled. This indeed, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the defilement of beings. Thus, with cause and with condition, beings are defiled.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, hetu katamo paccayo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā; kathaṃ sahetū sappaccayā sattā visujjhantī”ti? “Rūpañca hidaṃ, mahāli, ekantasukhaṃ abhavissa sukhānupatitaṃ sukhāvakkantaṃ anavakkantaṃ dukkhena, nayidaṃ sattā rūpasmiṃ nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, rūpaṃ dukkhaṃ dukkhānupatitaṃ dukkhāvakkantaṃ anavakkantaṃ sukhena, tasmā sattā rūpasmiṃ nibbindanti; nibbindaṃ virajjanti; virāgā visujjhanti. Ayaṃ kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, sattānaṃ visuddhiyā. Evaṃ sahetū sappaccayā sattā visujjhanti”.

“Furthermore, venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition for the purification of beings? How is it that with cause and with condition, beings are purified?” “If, Mahāli, this form were exclusively pleasant, followed by pleasure, pervaded by pleasure, and not pervaded by suffering, these beings would not become disenchanted with form. But because, Mahāli, form is suffering, followed by suffering, pervaded by suffering, and not pervaded by pleasure, beings become disenchanted with form. Becoming disenchanted, they become dispassionate; through dispassion, they are purified. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the purification of beings. Thus, with cause and with condition, beings are purified.”

“Vedanā ca hidaṃ, mahāli, ekantasukhā abhavissa…pe… saññā ca hidaṃ, mahāli…pe… saṅkhārā ca hidaṃ, mahāli, ekantasukhā abhavissaṃsu…pe… viññāṇañca hidaṃ, mahāli, ekantasukhaṃ abhavissa sukhānupatitaṃ sukhāvakkantaṃ anavakkantaṃ dukkhena, nayidaṃ sattā viññāṇasmiṃ nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, viññāṇaṃ dukkhaṃ dukkhānupatitaṃ dukkhāvakkantaṃ anavakkantaṃ sukhena, tasmā sattā viññāṇasmiṃ nibbindanti; nibbindaṃ virajjanti; virāgā visujjhanti. Ayaṃ [P 3.0071] kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, sattānaṃ visuddhiyā[T 3.0088]. Evampi sahetū sappaccayā sattā visujjhantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“And if feeling, Mahāli, were exclusively pleasant… perception… formations… and if consciousness, Mahāli, were exclusively pleasant, followed by pleasure, pervaded by pleasure, and not pervaded by suffering, beings would not become disenchanted with consciousness. But because, Mahāli, consciousness is suffering, followed by suffering, pervaded by suffering, and not pervaded by pleasure, beings become disenchanted with consciousness. Becoming disenchanted, they become dispassionate; through dispassion, they are purified. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the purification of beings. In this way also, with cause and with condition, beings are purified.” The Eighth.

9. Ādittasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Burning

61. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, ādittaṃ, vedanā ādittā, saññā ādittā, saṅkhārā [V 2.0066] ādittā, viññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi… saññāyapi… saṅkhāresupi… viññāṇasmimpi [M 2.0059] nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Navamaṃ.

61. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, form is burning, feeling is burning, perception is burning, volitional formations are burning, consciousness is burning. Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the well-instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with volitional formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate; through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’” The Ninth.

10. Niruttipathasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Paths of Language

62. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Tayome, bhikkhave, niruttipathā adhivacanapathā paññattipathā asaṅkiṇṇā asaṅkiṇṇapubbā, na saṅkīyanti, na saṅkīyissanti, appaṭikuṭṭhā samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhi. Katame tayo? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vipariṇataṃ ‘ahosī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘ahosī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘ahosī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’”ti.

62. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these three paths of language, paths of designation, and paths of description that are unconfused, were not confused in the past, are not being confused, and will not be confused, and are not repudiated by wise ascetics and brahmins. What three? Bhikkhus, that form which is past, ceased, and changed: it is reckoned as ‘it was,’ designated as ‘it was,’ and described as ‘it was.’ It is not reckoned as ‘it is,’ nor is it reckoned as ‘it will be.’”

“Yā vedanā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā ‘ahosī’ti tassā saṅkhā, ‘ahosī’ti tassā samaññā, ‘ahosī’ti tassā paññatti; na tassā saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tassā saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’”ti.

“Whatever feeling is past, ceased, and changed: it is reckoned as ‘it was,’ designated as ‘it was,’ and described as ‘it was.’ It is not reckoned as ‘it is,’ nor is it reckoned as ‘it will be.’”

“Yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā ‘ahesu’nti tesaṃ saṅkhā, ‘ahesu’nti tesaṃ samaññā, ‘ahesu’nti tesaṃ paññatti; na tesaṃ saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tesaṃ saṅkhā ‘bhavissantī’”ti.

“Whatever perception… whatever volitional formations are past, ceased, and changed: they are reckoned as ‘they were,’ designated as ‘they were,’ and described as ‘they were.’ They are not reckoned as ‘they are,’ nor are they reckoned as ‘they will be.’”

“Yaṃ [P 3.0072] viññāṇaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vipariṇataṃ, ‘ahosī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘ahosī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘ahosī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na [T 3.0089] tassa saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’”ti.

“Whatever consciousness is past, ceased, and has undergone change, for that there is the reckoning ‘it was,’ for that there is the designation ‘it was,’ for that there is the concept ‘it was.’ For that there is no reckoning ‘it is,’ nor is there the reckoning ‘it will be.’”

“Yaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ ajātaṃ apātubhūtaṃ, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘ahosī’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever form is unborn, unmanifested, for that there is the reckoning ‘it will be,’ for that there is the designation ‘it will be,’ for that there is the concept ‘it will be.’ For that there is no reckoning ‘it is,’ nor is there the reckoning ‘it was.’”

“Yā [V 2.0067] vedanā ajātā apātubhūtā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassā saṅkhā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassā samaññā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassā paññatti; na tassā saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tassā saṅkhā ‘ahosī’”ti.

“Whatever feeling is unborn, unmanifested, for that there is the reckoning ‘it will be,’ for that there is the designation ‘it will be,’ for that there is the concept ‘it will be.’ For that there is no reckoning ‘it is,’ nor is there the reckoning ‘it was.’”

“Yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā ajātā apātubhūtā, ‘bhavissantī’ti tesaṃ saṅkhā, ‘bhavissantī’ti tesaṃ samaññā, ‘bhavissantī’ti tesaṃ paññatti; na tesaṃ saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tesaṃ saṅkhā ‘ahesu’”nti.

“Whatever perception… whatever formations are unborn, unmanifested, for them there is the reckoning ‘they will be,’ for them there is the designation ‘they will be,’ for them there is the concept ‘they will be.’ For them there is no reckoning ‘they are,’ nor is there the reckoning ‘they were.’”

“Yaṃ [M 2.0060] viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ apātubhūtaṃ, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘ahosī’”ti.

“Whatever consciousness is unborn, unmanifested, for that there is the reckoning ‘it will be,’ for that there is the designation ‘it will be,’ for that there is the concept ‘it will be.’ For that there is no reckoning ‘it is,’ nor is there the reckoning ‘it was.’”

“Yaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ jātaṃ pātubhūtaṃ, ‘atthī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘atthī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘atthī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘ahosī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever form is born, manifested, for that there is the reckoning ‘it is,’ for that there is the designation ‘it is,’ for that there is the concept ‘it is.’ For that there is no reckoning ‘it was,’ nor is there the reckoning ‘it will be.’”

“Yā vedanā jātā pātubhūtā, ‘atthī’ti tassā saṅkhā, ‘atthī’ti tassā samaññā, ‘atthī’ti tassā paññatti; na tassā saṅkhā ‘ahosī’ti, na tassā saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’”ti.

“Whatever feeling is born, manifested, for that there is the reckoning ‘it is,’ for that there is the designation ‘it is,’ for that there is the concept ‘it is.’ For that there is no reckoning ‘it was,’ nor is there the reckoning ‘it will be.’”

“Yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā jātā pātubhūtā, ‘atthī’ti tesaṃ saṅkhā, ‘atthī’ti tesaṃ samaññā, ‘atthī’ti tesaṃ paññatti; na tesaṃ saṅkhā ‘ahesu’nti, na tesaṃ [T 3.0090] saṅkhā, ‘bhavissantī’”ti.

“Whatever perception… whatever formations are born, manifested, for them there is the reckoning ‘they are,’ for them there is the designation ‘they are,’ for them there is the concept ‘they are.’ For them there is no reckoning ‘they were,’ nor is there the reckoning ‘they will be.’”

“Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ jātaṃ pātubhūtaṃ, ‘atthī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘atthī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘atthī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘ahosī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’”ti.

“Whatever consciousness is born, manifested, for that there is the reckoning ‘it is,’ for that there is the designation ‘it is,’ for that there is the concept ‘it is.’ For that there is no reckoning ‘it was,’ nor is there the reckoning ‘it will be.’”

“Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo niruttipathā adhivacanapathā paññattipathā asaṅkiṇṇā asaṅkiṇṇapubbā, na saṅkīyanti, na [P 3.0073] saṅkīyissanti, appaṭikuṭṭhā samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhi[V 2.0068]. Yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṃ ukkalā vassabhaññā okkalā vayabhiññā (ma. ni. 3.343) ahetukavādā akiriyavādā natthikavādā, tepime tayo niruttipathe adhivacanapathe paññattipathe na garahitabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ amaññiṃsu. Taṃ kissa hetu? Nindāghaṭṭanabyārosaupārambhabhayā”ti nindābyārosaupārambhabhayāti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ma. ni. 3.343.

“Bhikkhus, these three paths of expression, paths of designation, and paths of concepts are unconfused, were unconfused in the past, are not being confused, and will not be confused. They are not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins. Even those, bhikkhus, who were the Ukkalā and Vassabhaññā—proponents of no-cause, proponents of no-action, and proponents of nihilism—they too considered these three paths of expression, paths of designation, and paths of concepts as not to be disparaged and not to be rejected. For what reason? Out of fear of blame, attack, hostility, and reproach.”

Upayavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Chapter on Means, the Sixth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of its contents:

Upayo bījaṃ udānaṃ, upādānaparivattaṃ;

Sattaṭṭhānañca sambuddho, pañcamahāli ādittā.

Vaggo niruttipathena cāti.

Upāya, Bīja, Udāna, Upādāna, and Parivatta; Sattaṭṭhāna and Sambuddha, Sacca, Mahāli, and Āditta. The chapter with the Niruttipatha Sutta.

7. Arahantavaggo

7. The Chapter on the Arahant

1. Upādiyamānasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Clinging

63. Evaṃ [T 3.0091][M 2.0061] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Upādiyamāno kho, bhikkhu, baddho mārassa; anupādiyamāno mutto pāpimato”ti. “Aññātaṃ [P 3.0074] bhagavā, aññātaṃ sugatā”ti.

63. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute.’ ‘Bhikkhu, one who clings is bound by Māra; one who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.’ ‘I have understood, Blessed One! I have understood, Well-Gone One!’

“Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, bhante, upādiyamāno baddho mārassa; anupādiyamāno mutto pāpimato. Vedanaṃ upādiyamāno baddho mārassa; anupādiyamāno mutto pāpimato. Saññaṃ… saṅkhāre [V 2.0069]… viññāṇaṃ upādiyamāno baddho mārassa; anupādiyamāno mutto pāpimato. Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“In what way, then, bhikkhu, do you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief?” “Venerable sir, by clinging to form, one is bound by Māra; by not clinging, one is freed from the Evil One. By clinging to feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one is bound by Māra; by not clinging, one is freed from the Evil One. This, venerable sir, is how I understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ kho, bhikkhu, upādiyamāno baddho mārassa; anupādiyamāno mutto pāpimato. Vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ upādiyamāno baddho mārassa[T 3.0092]; anupādiyamāno mutto pāpimato. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.

“Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good, bhikkhu, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief. By clinging to form, one is bound by Māra; by not clinging, one is freed from the Evil One. By clinging to feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one is bound by Māra; by not clinging, one is freed from the Evil One. The meaning of what was spoken by me in brief should be understood in detail in this way, bhikkhu.”

Atha kho so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho so bhikkhu eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ [M 2.0062] karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Paṭhamaṃ.

Then that monk, having delighted in and rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed. Then that monk, dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute, before long realized for himself with higher knowledge in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, he dwelled therein. He understood: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state.” And that monk became one of the arahants. The first.

2. Maññamānasuttaṃ

2. The Sutta on Conceiving

64. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [P 3.0075] – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu…pe… ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Maññamāno kho, bhikkhu, baddho mārassa; amaññamāno mutto pāpimato”ti. “Aññātaṃ bhagavā, aññātaṃ sugatā”ti.

64. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain bhikkhu... and so on... That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief... and so on... so that I may dwell, ardent and resolute.' 'Bhikkhu, one who conceives with craving, conceit, and views is bound by Māra; one who does not conceive is freed from the Evil One.' 'I have understood it in detail, Blessed One! I have understood it in detail, Sugata!'

“Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, bhante, maññamāno baddho mārassa; amaññamāno mutto pāpimato. Vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ maññamāno baddho mārassa; amaññamāno mutto pāpimato. Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

'But how, bhikkhu, do you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief?' 'Venerable sir, one who conceives form with craving, conceit, and views is bound by Māra; one who does not conceive form is freed from the Evil One. One who conceives feeling... perception... volitional formations... consciousness with craving, conceit, and views is bound by Māra; one who does not conceive consciousness is freed from the Evil One. Venerable sir, this is how I understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by the Blessed One.'

“Sādhu [V 2.0070] sādhu[T 3.0093], bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ kho, bhikkhu, maññamāno baddho mārassa; amaññamāno mutto pāpimato. Vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ maññamāno baddho mārassa; amaññamāno mutto pāpimato. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti…pe… aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Dutiyaṃ.

'Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good, bhikkhu, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief. Bhikkhu, one who conceives form with craving, conceit, and views is bound by Māra; one who does not conceive form is freed from the Evil One. One who conceives feeling... perception... volitional formations... consciousness with craving, conceit, and views is bound by Māra; one who does not conceive consciousness is freed from the Evil One. Bhikkhu, indeed, the meaning of this teaching spoken by me in brief should be regarded in detail in this way.' ...and so on... And that bhikkhu became one of the arahants. The Second.

3. Abhinandamānasuttaṃ

3. The Sutta on Rejoicing

65. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena…pe… pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Abhinandamāno kho, bhikkhu, baddho mārassa; anabhinandamāno mutto pāpimato”ti. “Aññātaṃ bhagavā, aññātaṃ sugatā”ti.

65. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain bhikkhu... and so on... That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief... and so on... so that I may dwell resolute.' 'Bhikkhu, one who rejoices is bound by Māra; one who does not rejoice is freed from the Evil One.' 'I have understood it in detail, Blessed One! I have understood it in detail, Sugata!'

“Yathā [M 2.0063] kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, bhante, abhinandamāno baddho mārassa; anabhinandamāno mutto pāpimato. Vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ abhinandamāno baddho mārassa; anabhinandamāno mutto pāpimato. Imassa [P 3.0076] khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“But how, bhikkhu, do you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief?” “Venerable sir, by delighting in form, one is bound by Māra; by not delighting in it, one is freed from the Evil One. By delighting in feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one is bound by Māra; by not delighting in it, one is freed from the Evil One. Venerable sir, it is in this way that I understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ kho, bhikkhu, abhinandamāno baddho mārassa; anabhinandamāno mutto pāpimato. Vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre [T 3.0094]… viññāṇaṃ abhinandamāno baddho mārassa; anabhinandamāno mutto pāpimato. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti…pe… aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good, bhikkhu, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief. Bhikkhu, by delighting in form, one is bound by Māra; by not delighting in it, one is freed from the Evil One. By delighting in feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one is bound by Māra; by not delighting in it, one is freed from the Evil One. Bhikkhu, indeed, the meaning of this teaching spoken by me in brief should be regarded in detail in this way.” … And that bhikkhu became one of the arahants. The Third.

4. Aniccasuttaṃ

4. The Sutta on Impermanence

66. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0071]. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu…pe… ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, aniccaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti. “Aññātaṃ bhagavā; aññātaṃ sugatā”ti.

66. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain bhikkhu… Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief… so that I may dwell ardent and resolute.” “Bhikkhu, whatever is impermanent, there your desire should be abandoned.” “I have understood it in detail, Blessed One! I have understood it in detail, Sugata!”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, bhante, aniccaṃ; tatra me chando pahātabbo. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ; tatra me chando pahātabbo. Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“But how, bhikkhu, do you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief?” “Venerable sir, form is impermanent; there my desire should be abandoned. Feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent; there my desire should be abandoned. Venerable sir, it is in this way that I understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ kho, bhikkhu, aniccaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo. Vedanā aniccā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ; tatra kho te chando pahātabbo. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti…pe… [P 3.0077] aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Catutthaṃ.

“Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good, bhikkhu, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief. Form, bhikkhu, is impermanent; in that, desire should be abandoned by you. Feeling is impermanent… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent; in that, desire should be abandoned by you. Bhikkhu, indeed, the meaning of this teaching spoken by me in brief should be regarded in detail in this way.” … And that bhikkhu became one of the arahants. The Fourth.

5. Dukkhasuttaṃ

5. The Sutta on Suffering

67. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0064]. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [T 3.0095] – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu…pe… ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, dukkhaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti. “Aññātaṃ bhagavā; aññātaṃ sugatā”ti.

67. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain monk… seated to one side, that monk said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief… so that I might dwell ardent, with a mind dispatched to Nibbāna.” “Monk, whatever is suffering, therein your desire should be abandoned.” “It is understood, Blessed One; it is understood, Sugata.”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti[V 2.0072]? “Rūpaṃ kho, bhante, dukkhaṃ; tatra me chando pahātabbo. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ dukkhaṃ; tatra me chando pahātabbo. Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“But in what way, monk, do you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief?” “Venerable sir, form is suffering; therein my desire should be abandoned. Feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is suffering; therein my desire should be abandoned. Venerable sir, it is in this way that I understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ kho bhikkhu, dukkhaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ dukkhaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti…pe… aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Good, good, monk! It is good, monk, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief. Form, monk, is suffering; therein your desire should be abandoned. Feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is suffering; therein your desire should be abandoned. Indeed, monk, the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief should be regarded thus in detail.” … And that monk became one of the Arahants. The Fifth.

6. Anattasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Not-Self

68. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu…pe… ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Yo kho, bhikkhu, anattā; tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti. “Aññātaṃ, bhagavā; aññātaṃ, sugatā”ti.

68. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain monk… seated to one side, that monk said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief… so that I might dwell ardent, with a mind dispatched to Nibbāna.” “Monk, whatever is not-self, therein your desire should be abandoned.” “It is understood, Blessed One; it is understood, Sugata.”

“Yathā [P 3.0078] kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, bhante, anattā; tatra me [T 3.0096] chando pahātabbo. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ anattā; tatra me chando pahātabbo. Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“But in what way, monk, do you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief?” “Venerable sir, form is not-self; therein my desire should be abandoned. Feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is not-self; therein my desire should be abandoned. Venerable sir, it is in this way that I understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ kho, bhikkhu, anattā; tatra te chando pahātabbo[M 2.0065]. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ anattā; tatra te chando pahātabbo. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti…pe… [V 2.0073] aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Good, good, monk! It is good, monk, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief. Form, monk, is not-self; therein your desire should be abandoned. Feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is not-self; therein your desire should be abandoned. Indeed, monk, the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief should be regarded thus in detail.” … And that monk became one of the Arahants. The Sixth.

7. Anattaniyasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on What Is Not One's Own

69. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu…pe… vihareyya”nti. “Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, anattaniyaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti. “Aññātaṃ, bhagavā; aññātaṃ, sugatā”ti.

69. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain monk… seated to one side, that monk said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief… so that I might dwell.” “Monk, whatever is not one's own, therein your desire should be abandoned.” “It is understood, Blessed One; it is understood, Sugata.”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, bhante, anattaniyaṃ; tatra me chando pahātabbo. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ anattaniyaṃ; tatra me chando pahātabbo. Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“But in what way, monk, do you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief?” “Venerable sir, form is not one's own; therein my desire should be abandoned. Feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is not one's own; therein my desire should be abandoned. Venerable sir, it is in this way that I understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ kho, bhikkhu[T 3.0097], anattaniyaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo. Vedanā [P 3.0079] … saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ anattaniyaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti…pe… aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Sattamaṃ.

“Good, good, monk! It is good, monk, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief. Form, monk, is not one's own; therein your desire should be abandoned. Feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is not one's own; therein your desire should be abandoned. Indeed, monk, the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief should be regarded thus in detail.” … And that monk became one of the Arahants. The Seventh.

8. Rajanīyasaṇṭhitasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on What Is Established in Passion

70. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā…pe… vihareyya”nti. “Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, rajanīyasaṇṭhitaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti. “Aññātaṃ, bhagavā; aññātaṃ, sugatā”ti.

70. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain monk… seated to one side, that monk said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell…’. ‘Monk, whatever is established in passion, therein your desire should be abandoned.’ ‘It is understood, Blessed One; it is understood, Sugata.’

“Yathā [V 2.0074] kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsī”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, bhante, rajanīyasaṇṭhitaṃ; tatra me chando pahātabbo. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ rajanīyasaṇṭhitaṃ; tatra me chando pahātabbo. Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“But in what way, monk, do you understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken by me in brief?” “Venerable sir, form is established in passion; therein my desire should be abandoned. Feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is established in passion; therein my desire should be abandoned. Venerable sir, it is in this way that I understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu [M 2.0066] sādhu bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāsi. Rūpaṃ kho, bhikkhu, rajanīyasaṇṭhitaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ rajanīyasaṇṭhitaṃ; tatra te chando pahātabbo. Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti…pe… aññataro ca [T 3.0098] pana so bhikkhu arahataṃ ahosīti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good, bhikkhu, that you understand in detail the meaning of what was stated by me in brief. Form, bhikkhu, is established as a basis for passion; there your desire is to be abandoned. Feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is established as a basis for passion; there your desire is to be abandoned. Bhikkhu, the meaning of what was stated by me in brief is to be seen in detail in this way.” … And that bhikkhu became one of the Arahants. The Eighth.

9. Rādhasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Rādha

71. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā rādho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[P 3.0080]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kathaṃ nu kho, bhante, jānato, kathaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā na hontī”ti? “Yaṃ kiñci, rādha, rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Evaṃ kho, rādha, jānato evaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā na hontī”ti…pe… [V 2.0075] aññataro ca panāyasmā rādho arahataṃ ahosīti. Navamaṃ.

71. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Rādha approached the Blessed One and said to him: “Venerable sir, for one who knows how, for one who sees how, do the underlying tendencies of I-making, mine-making, and conceit not occur in regard to this conscious body and all external signs?” “Whatever form, Rādha, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—one sees all form as it really is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever formations… whatever consciousness, whether past, future, or present… far or near—one sees all consciousness as it really is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ It is for one who knows thus, Rādha, for one who sees thus, that the underlying tendencies of I-making, mine-making, and conceit do not occur in regard to this conscious body and all external signs.” … And the Venerable Rādha became one of the Arahants. The Ninth.

10. Surādhasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Surādha

72. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā surādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kathaṃ nu kho, bhante, jānato kathaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānāpagataṃ mānasaṃ hoti, vidhā samatikkantaṃ santaṃ suvimutta”nti? “Yaṃ [T 3.0099] kiñci, surādha, rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā anupādāvimutto hoti. Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ [P 3.0081] kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā [M 2.0067] sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā anupādāvimutto hoti. Evaṃ kho, surādha, jānato evaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye, bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānāpagataṃ mānasaṃ hoti vidhā samatikkantaṃ santaṃ suvimutta”nti…pe… aññataro ca panāyasmā surādho arahataṃ ahosīti. Dasamaṃ.

72. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Surādha said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, for one who knows how, for one who sees how, is the mind—in regard to this body with consciousness and externally in regard to all signs—devoid of I-making, mine-making, and conceit, having transcended the threefold classification, peaceful, and well liberated?” “Whatever form, Surādha, is past, future, or present... far or near, all that form—having seen it as it really is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’—one is liberated without clinging. Whatever feeling... whatever perception... whatever formations... whatever consciousness is past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, all that consciousness—having seen it as it really is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’—one is liberated without clinging. It is in this way, Surādha, that for one who knows thus, for one who sees thus, the mind—in regard to this body with consciousness and externally in regard to all signs—is devoid of I-making, mine-making, and conceit, having transcended the threefold classification, peaceful, and well liberated.” … And the Venerable Surādha became one of the arahants. The Tenth.

Arahantavaggo sattamo.

The Seventh Chapter on the Arahants.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Upādiyamaññamānā, athābhinandamāno ca;

Aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā ca, anattanīyaṃ rajanīyasaṇṭhitaṃ;

Rādhasurādhena te dasāti.

Clinging and Conceiving, and then Delighting; Impermanent, Suffering, and Not-Self; Not Belonging to Self and Established as a Basis for Passion; With Rādha and Surādha, these are the ten.

8. Khajjanīyavaggo

8. The Chapter on Being Devoured

1. Assādasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Gratification

73. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0100][V 2.0076]. “Assutavā, bhikkhave, puthujjano rūpassa assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhārānaṃ… viññāṇassa assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako rūpassa assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Vedanā [P 3.0082]… saññāya… saṅkhārānaṃ… viññāṇassa assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

73. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, the uninstructed ordinary person does not understand as it actually is the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of form. They do not understand as it actually is the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness. But, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple understands as it actually is the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of form. They understand as it actually is the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness.” The First.

2. Samudayasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Origin

74. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Assutavā, bhikkhave, puthujjano rūpassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhārānaṃ… viññāṇassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca [M 2.0068] nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako rūpassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhārānaṃ… viññāṇassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

74. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, the uninstructed ordinary person does not understand as it actually is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of form. They do not understand as it actually is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness. But, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple understands as it actually is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of form. They understand as it actually is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness.” The Second.

3. Dutiyasamudayasuttaṃ

3. The Second Discourse on Origin

75. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Sutavā, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako rūpassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca [V 2.0077] assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ [T 3.0101] pajānāti. Vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhārānaṃ… viññāṇassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

75. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple understands as it actually is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of form. They understand as it actually is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness.” The Third.

4. Arahantasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Arahants

76. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama[P 3.0083], nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ”.

76. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, form is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen with right wisdom as it really is: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen with right wisdom as it really is: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi… saññāyapi… saṅkhāresupi… viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Yāvatā, bhikkhave, sattāvāsā, yāvatā bhavaggaṃ, ete aggā, ete seṭṭhā lokasmiṃ yadidaṃ arahanto”ti.

“Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with volitional formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, one becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, one is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises, ‘I am liberated.’ One understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’ As far as there are abodes of beings, bhikkhus, as far as the summit of existence, these—the arahants—are the foremost, these are the best in the world.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:

“Sukhino vata arahanto, taṇhā tesaṃ na vijjati;

Asmimāno samucchinno, mohajālaṃ padālitaṃ.

“Happy indeed are the arahants; for them, craving is not found. The conceit ‘I am’ is eradicated, the net of delusion is rent asunder.

“Anejaṃ [T 3.0102][M 2.0069] te anuppattā, cittaṃ tesaṃ anāvilaṃ;

Loke anupalittā te, brahmabhūtā anāsavā.

“They have attained the unshakable, their mind is unperturbed; unstained in the world, they have become supreme, without taints.

“Pañcakkhandhe [V 2.0078] pariññāya, satta saddhammagocarā;

Pasaṃsiyā sappurisā, puttā buddhassa orasā.

“Having fully understood the five aggregates, they whose domain is the seven true Dhammas are the praiseworthy good persons, the Buddha's own offspring.

“Sattaratanasampannā, tīsu sikkhāsu sikkhitā;

Anuvicaranti mahāvīrā, pahīnabhayabheravā.

“Endowed with the seven jewels, trained in the three trainings, the great heroes wander about, having abandoned fear and dread.

“Dasahaṅgehi sampannā, mahānāgā samāhitā;

Ete kho seṭṭhā lokasmiṃ, taṇhā tesaṃ na vijjati.

“Endowed with ten factors, the great nāgas are composed; these indeed are the best in the world, for them, craving is not found.

“Asekhañāṇamuppannaṃ, antimoyaṃ antimassa (ka.) samussayo;

Yo sāro brahmacariyassa, tasmiṃ aparapaccayā.

“The knowledge of the adept has arisen; this is the final embodiment. In that which is the essence of the holy life, they are not dependent on another.

“Vidhāsu [P 3.0084] na vikampanti, vippamuttā punabbhavā;

Dantabhūmimanuppattā, te loke vijitāvino.

“They do not tremble amidst distinctions, being fully freed from renewed existence; having attained the ground of the tamed, they are victorious in the world.

“Uddhaṃ tiriyaṃ apācīnaṃ, nandī tesaṃ na vijjati;

Nadanti te sīhanādaṃ, buddhā loke anuttarā”ti. catutthaṃ;

“Upwards, across, and downwards—for them, delight is not found. They roar this lion’s roar: ‘The Buddhas are unsurpassed in the world!’” The fourth.

5. Dutiyaarahantasuttaṃ

5. The Second Arahant Discourse

77. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti…pe… evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ”.

77. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, form is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ … In this way, this should be seen with right wisdom as it really is.”

“Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi… saññāyapi… saṅkhāresupi… viññāṇasmimpi [T 3.0103] nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā [V 2.0079] vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Yāvatā, bhikkhave, sattāvāsā, yāvatā bhavaggaṃ, ete aggā, ete seṭṭhā lokasmiṃ yadidaṃ arahanto”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with volitional formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises, ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’ Bhikkhus, to the extent that there are abodes of beings, as far as the peak of existence, these are the foremost, these are the best in the world—that is, the arahants.” Fifth.

6. Sīhasuttaṃ

6. The Lion Discourse

78. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0070]. “Sīho, bhikkhave, migarājā sāyanhasamayaṃ āsayā nikkhamati; āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambhati; vijambhitvā samantā catuddisā anuviloketi; samantā catuddisā anuviloketvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadati; tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkamati. Ye [P 3.0085] hi keci, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā sīhassa migarañño nadato saddaṃ suṇanti; yebhuyyena bhayaṃ saṃvegaṃ santāsaṃ āpajjanti; bilaṃ bilāsayā pavisanti; dakaṃ dakāsayā pavisanti; vanaṃ vanāsayā pavisanti; ākāsaṃ pakkhino bhajanti. Yepi te, bhikkhave, rañño nāgā gāmanigamarājadhānīsu, daḷhehi varattehi baddhā, tepi tāni bandhanāni sañchinditvā sampadāletvā bhītā muttakarīsaṃ cajamānā mocantā (pī. ka.), yena vā tena vā palāyanti. Evaṃ mahiddhiko kho, bhikkhave, sīho migarājā tiracchānagatānaṃ pāṇānaṃ, evaṃ mahesakkho, evaṃ mahānubhāvo”.

78. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, the lion, the king of beasts, comes out from his lair in the evening. Having come out from his lair, he stretches. Having stretched, he surveys the four directions all around. Having surveyed the four directions all around, he roars a lion’s roar three times. Having roared a lion’s roar three times, he sets out for food. Now, bhikkhus, whatever animals hear the sound of the roaring lion, the king of beasts, for the most part they are overcome by fear, terror, and dread. Creatures dwelling in holes enter holes; creatures dwelling in water enter the water; creatures dwelling in the forest enter the forest; birds resort to the sky. Even those royal elephants, bhikkhus, in villages, towns, and royal capitals, bound by strong straps, break and tear apart those bonds and, terrified, voiding urine and dung, flee wherever they can. So mighty, bhikkhus, is the lion, the king of beasts, among animals, so powerful, so majestic.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yadā tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ [T 3.0104] sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So dhammaṃ deseti – ‘iti rūpaṃ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo; iti vedanā… iti saññā… iti saṅkhārā… iti viññāṇaṃ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti. Yepi te, bhikkhave, devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā uccesu vimānesu ciraṭṭhitikā tepi tathāgatassa dhammadesanaṃ sutvā yebhuyyena bhayaṃ saṃvegaṃ santāsaṃ āpajjanti – ‘aniccāva kira, bho, mayaṃ samānā niccamhāti amaññimha. Addhuvāva kira, bho, mayaṃ samānā dhuvamhāti amaññimha. Asassatāva kira, bho, mayaṃ samānā sassatamhāti amaññimha. Mayampi kira, bho, aniccā addhuvā asassatā sakkāyapariyāpannā’ti. Evaṃ mahiddhiko kho, bhikkhave, tathāgato [V 2.0080] sadevakassa lokassa, evaṃ mahesakkho, evaṃ mahānubhāvo”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā…pe… etadavoca satthā –

“Just so, bhikkhus, when a Tathāgata arises in the world—an Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One—he teaches the Dhamma: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the cessation of form; such is feeling; such is perception; such are volitional formations; such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the cessation of consciousness.’ Bhikkhus, even those devas who are long-lived, beautiful, abounding in happiness, dwelling in lofty palaces, enduring for a long time—when they hear the Tathāgata’s teaching of the Dhamma, for the most part they are struck with fear, trepidation, and terror, thinking: ‘It seems, friends, that we are impermanent, though we considered ourselves permanent. It seems, friends, that we are unstable, though we considered ourselves stable. It seems, friends, that we are non-eternal, though we considered ourselves eternal. It seems, friends, that we too are impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, included within a manifest body.’ So mighty, bhikkhus, is the Tathāgata in the world with its devas, so powerful, so majestic.” This is what the Blessed One said… The Teacher said further:

“Yadā [P 3.0086] buddho abhiññāya, dhammacakkaṃ pavattayi;

Sadevakassa lokassa, satthā appaṭipuggalo.

“When the Buddha—the Teacher, the incomparable person—set in motion the Wheel of Dhamma for the world with its devas, having directly known:

“Sakkāyañca [M 2.0071] nirodhañca, sakkāyassa ca sambhavaṃ;

Ariyañcaṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ, dukkhūpasamagāminaṃ.

“Identity, its cessation, and the origin of identity, and the noble eightfold path that leads to the stilling of suffering.”

“Yepi dīghāyukā devā, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Bhītā santāsamāpāduṃ, sīhassevitare migā.

Even those devas who are long-lived, beautiful, and glorious were seized with terror, frightened like other beasts before a lion,

Avītivattā [T 3.0105] sakkāyaṃ, aniccā kira bho mayaṃ;

Sutvā arahato vākyaṃ, vippamuttassa tādino”ti. chaṭṭhaṃ;

“‘We have not transcended identity; it seems, friends, we are impermanent!’ after hearing the word of the Arahant—the liberated, the imperturbable one. Sixth.”

7. Khajjanīyasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on What is to be Consumed

79. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaramānā anussaranti sabbete pañcupādānakkhandhe anussaranti etesaṃ vā aññataraṃ. Katame pañca? ‘Evaṃrūpo ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti – iti vā hi, bhikkhave, anussaramāno rūpaṃyeva anussarati. ‘Evaṃvedano ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti – iti vā hi, bhikkhave, anussaramāno vedanaṃyeva anussarati. ‘Evaṃsañño ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti… ‘evaṃsaṅkhāro ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti… ‘evaṃviññāṇo ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti – iti vā hi, bhikkhave, anussaramāno viññāṇameva anussarati”.

79. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins recall their manifold past lives, all of them recall these five aggregates subject to clinging, or one among them. Which five? ‘I was of such a form in the past’—thus, bhikkhus, in recalling, one recalls only form. ‘I was of such a feeling in the past’—thus, bhikkhus, in recalling, one recalls only feeling. ‘I was of such a perception in the past’… ‘I was of such formations in the past’… ‘I was of such a consciousness in the past’—thus, bhikkhus, in recalling, one recalls only consciousness.”

“Kiñca, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ vadetha? Ruppatīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā ‘rūpa’nti vuccati. Kena ruppati? Sītenapi ruppati, uṇhenapi ruppati, jighacchāyapi ruppati, pipāsāyapi [V 2.0081] ruppati, ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassenapi … siriṃsapasamphassenapi (sī. pī.) ruppati. Ruppatīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā ‘rūpa’nti vuccati.

“And what, bhikkhus, do you call form? It is afflicted, bhikkhus, therefore it is called ‘form.’ By what is it afflicted? It is afflicted by cold, it is afflicted by heat, it is afflicted by hunger, it is afflicted by thirst, it is afflicted by the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things. It is afflicted, bhikkhus, therefore it is called ‘form.’”

“Kiñca, bhikkhave, vedanaṃ vadetha? Vedayatīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā ‘vedanā’ti vuccati. Kiñca vedayati? Sukhampi vedayati, dukkhampi vedayati, adukkhamasukhampi [P 3.0087] vedayati. Vedayatīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā ‘vedanā’ti vuccati.

“And what, bhikkhus, do you call feeling? It feels, bhikkhus, therefore it is called ‘feeling.’ And what does it feel? It feels pleasure, it feels pain, and it feels neither-pain-nor-pleasure. It feels, bhikkhus, therefore it is called ‘feeling.’”

“Kiñca, bhikkhave, saññaṃ vadetha? Sañjānātīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā [T 3.0106] ‘saññā’ti vuccati. Kiñca sañjānāti? Nīlampi sañjānāti, pītakampi sañjānāti, lohitakampi sañjānāti, odātampi sañjānāti. Sañjānātīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā ‘saññā’ti vuccati.

“And what, bhikkhus, do you call perception? It perceives, bhikkhus, therefore it is called ‘perception.’ And what does it perceive? It perceives blue, it perceives yellow, it perceives red, it perceives white. It perceives, bhikkhus, therefore it is called ‘perception.’”

“Kiñca[M 2.0072], bhikkhave, saṅkhāre vadetha? Saṅkhatamabhisaṅkharontīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā ‘saṅkhārā’ti vuccati. Kiñca saṅkhatamabhisaṅkharonti? Rūpaṃ rūpattāya rūpatthāya (ka.) saṅkhatamabhisaṅkharonti, vedanaṃ vedanattāya saṅkhatamabhisaṅkharonti, saññaṃ saññattāya saṅkhatamabhisaṅkharonti, saṅkhāre saṅkhārattāya saṅkhatamabhisaṅkharonti, viññāṇaṃ viññāṇattāya saṅkhatamabhisaṅkharonti. Saṅkhatamabhisaṅkharontīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā ‘saṅkhārā’ti vuccati.

“And what, bhikkhus, do you call formations? ‘They fashion the fashioned,’ bhikkhus, therefore they are called ‘formations.’ And what fashioned thing do they fashion? They fashion fashioned form for the state of form; they fashion fashioned feeling for the state of feeling; they fashion fashioned perception for the state of perception; they fashion fashioned formations for the state of formations; they fashion fashioned consciousness for the state of consciousness. ‘They fashion the fashioned,’ bhikkhus, therefore they are called ‘formations.’”

“Kiñca, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ vadetha? Vijānātīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā ‘viññāṇa’nti vuccati. Kiñca vijānāti? Ambilampi vijānāti, tittakampi vijānāti, kaṭukampi vijānāti, madhurampi vijānāti, khārikampi vijānāti, akhārikampi vijānāti, loṇikampi vijānāti, aloṇikampi vijānāti. Vijānātīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā ‘viññāṇa’nti vuccati.

“And what, bhikkhus, do you call consciousness? ‘It cognizes,’ bhikkhus; therefore, it is called ‘consciousness.’ And what does it cognize? It cognizes sour, it cognizes bitter, it cognizes pungent, it cognizes sweet, it cognizes alkaline, it cognizes non-alkaline, it cognizes salty, it cognizes non-salty. ‘It cognizes,’ bhikkhus; therefore, it is called ‘consciousness.’”

“Tatra, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ kho etarahi rūpena khajjāmi. Atītampāhaṃ addhānaṃ evameva rūpena khajjiṃ, seyyathāpi etarahi paccuppannena rūpena khajjāmi. Ahañceva kho pana anāgataṃ rūpaṃ abhinandeyyaṃ, anāgatampāhaṃ addhānaṃ evameva rūpena khajjeyyaṃ, seyyathāpi etarahi paccuppannena rūpena khajjāmī’ti. So iti [V 2.0082] paṭisaṅkhāya atītasmiṃ rūpasmiṃ anapekkho hoti[T 3.0107]; anāgataṃ rūpaṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannassa rūpassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.

“Therein, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple reflects thus: ‘I am now being consumed by form. In the past, too, I was consumed by form in just this way, just as I am now being consumed by present form. And if I were to delight in future form, in the future, too, I would be consumed by form in just this way, just as I am now being consumed by present form.’ Having reflected thus, he is unconcerned with past form; he does not delight in future form; and he is practicing for the disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation of present form.

“‘Ahaṃ kho etarahi vedanāya khajjāmi. Atītampāhaṃ addhānaṃ evameva vedanāya khajjiṃ, seyyathāpi etarahi paccuppannāya [P 3.0088] vedanāya khajjāmi. Ahañceva kho pana anāgataṃ vedanaṃ abhinandeyyaṃ; anāgatampāhaṃ addhānaṃ evameva vedanāya khajjeyyaṃ, seyyathāpi etarahi paccuppannāya vedanāya khajjāmī’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya atītāya vedanāya anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ vedanaṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannāya vedanāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.

“‘I am now being consumed by feeling. In the past, too, I was consumed by feeling in this same way, just as I am now being consumed by present feeling. If I were to delight in future feeling, in the future, too, I would be consumed by feeling in this same way, just as I am now being consumed by present feeling.’ Having reflected thus, he is unconcerned with past feeling; he does not delight in future feeling; he is practicing for the disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation of present feeling.

“‘Ahaṃ kho etarahi saññāya khajjāmi…pe… ahaṃ kho etarahi saṅkhārehi khajjāmi. Atītampāhaṃ addhānaṃ evameva saṅkhārehi khajjiṃ, seyyathāpi etarahi paccuppannehi saṅkhārehi khajjāmīti. Ahañceva kho pana anāgate saṅkhāre abhinandeyyaṃ[M 2.0073]; anāgatampāhaṃ addhānaṃ evameva saṅkhārehi khajjeyyaṃ, seyyathāpi etarahi paccuppannehi saṅkhārehi khajjāmī’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya atītesu saṅkhāresu anapekkho hoti; anāgate saṅkhāre nābhinandati; paccuppannānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.

“‘I am now being consumed by perception… I am now being consumed by formations. In the past, too, I was consumed by formations in this same way, just as I am now being consumed by present formations. If I were to delight in future formations, in the future, too, I would be consumed by formations in this same way, just as I am now being consumed by present formations.’ Having reflected thus, he is unconcerned with past formations; he does not delight in future formations; he is practicing for the disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation of present formations.”

“‘Ahaṃ kho etarahi viññāṇena khajjāmi. Atītampi addhānaṃ evameva viññāṇena khajjiṃ, seyyathāpi etarahi paccuppannena viññāṇena khajjāmi. Ahañceva kho pana anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ abhinandeyyaṃ; anāgatampāhaṃ addhānaṃ evameva viññāṇena khajjeyyaṃ, seyyathāpi [T 3.0108] etarahi paccuppannena viññāṇena khajjāmī’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya atītasmiṃ viññāṇasmiṃ anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannassa viññāṇassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.

‘Indeed, I am now being consumed by consciousness. In the past, too, I was consumed by consciousness in this same way, just as I am now being consumed by present consciousness. If I were to delight in future consciousness, in the future, too, I would be consumed by consciousness in this same way, just as I am now being consumed by present consciousness.’ Having reflected thus, that person is unconcerned with past consciousness; he does not delight in future consciousness; he is practicing for the disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation of present consciousness.

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā [V 2.0083]… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ [P 3.0089] niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na [T 3.0109] meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ”.

“What do you think, monks, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Therefore, monks, whatever form there is—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all form should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness there is—past, future, or present… far or near—all consciousness should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako apacināti, no ācināti; pajahati no (sī.), na upādiyati; visineti no (sī.), na ussineti; vidhūpeti no (sī.), na sandhūpeti. Kiñca apacināti, no ācināti? Rūpaṃ apacināti, no ācināti; vedanaṃ [M 2.0074]… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ apacināti, no ācināti. Kiñca pajahati, na upādiyati? Rūpaṃ pajahati, na upādiyati; vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ pajahati, na upādiyati. Kiñca [P 3.0090] visineti, na ussineti? Rūpaṃ visineti, na ussineti; vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ visineti, na ussineti. Kiñca vidhūpeti, na sandhūpeti? Rūpaṃ vidhūpeti, na sandhūpeti; vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ vidhūpeti, na sandhūpeti.

Monks, this noble disciple is said to be one who diminishes, not one who accumulates; one who abandons, not one who clings; one who disperses, not one who gathers; one who extinguishes, not one who kindles. And what does he diminish, not accumulate? He diminishes form, he does not accumulate it; he diminishes feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness, he does not accumulate it. And what does he abandon, not cling to? He abandons form, he does not cling to it; he abandons feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness, he does not cling to it. And what does he disperse, not gather? He disperses form, he does not gather it; he disperses feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness, he does not gather it. And what does he extinguish, not kindle? He extinguishes form, he does not kindle it; he extinguishes feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness, he does not kindle it.

“Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi… saññāyapi… saṅkhāresupi… viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.

Monks, seeing thus, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with volitional formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When he is liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’

“Ayaṃ [V 2.0084] vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nevācināti na apacināti, apacinitvā ṭhito neva pajahati na upādiyati, pajahitvā ṭhito neva visineti na ussineti, visinetvā ṭhito neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti. Vidhūpetvā ṭhito kiñca nevācināti na apacināti? Apacinitvā ṭhito rūpaṃ [T 3.0110] nevācināti na apacināti; apacinitvā ṭhito vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ nevācināti na apacināti. Apacinitvā ṭhito kiñca neva pajahati na upādiyati? Pajahitvā ṭhito rūpaṃ neva pajahati na upādiyati; pajahitvā ṭhito vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ neva pajahati na upādiyati. Pajahitvā ṭhito kiñca neva visineti na ussineti? Visinetvā ṭhito rūpaṃ neva visineti na ussineti; visinetvā ṭhito vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ neva visineti na ussineti. Visinetvā ṭhito kiñca neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti? Vidhūpetvā ṭhito rūpaṃ neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti; vidhūpetvā ṭhito vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti. Vidhūpetvā ṭhito evaṃvimuttacittaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ saindā devā sabrahmakā sapajāpatikā ārakāva namassanti –

Monks, this monk is said to be one who neither accumulates nor diminishes; having diminished, he is established. He neither abandons nor clings; having abandoned, he is established. He neither disperses nor gathers; having dispersed, he is established. He neither extinguishes nor kindles; having extinguished, he is established. And what does he neither accumulate nor diminish? Having diminished, he is established; he neither accumulates nor diminishes form. Having diminished, he is established; he neither accumulates nor diminishes feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness. And what does he neither abandon nor cling to? Having abandoned, he is established; he neither abandons nor clings to form. Having abandoned, he is established; he neither abandons nor clings to feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness. And what does he neither disperse nor gather? Having dispersed, he is established; he neither disperses nor gathers form. Having dispersed, he is established; he neither disperses nor gathers feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness. And what does he neither extinguish nor kindle? Having extinguished, he is established; he neither extinguishes nor kindles form. Having extinguished, he is established; he neither extinguishes nor kindles feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness. Monks, the gods with Inda, with Brahmā, and with Pajāpati pay homage from afar to a monk whose mind is thus liberated:

“Namo [P 3.0091] te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Yassa te nābhijānāma, yampi nissāya jhāyasī”ti. sattamaṃ;

“Homage to you, O thoroughbred of men! Homage to you, O supreme among men! We do not know that, relying on which, you meditate.” Seventh.

8. Piṇḍolyasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Piṇḍolya

80. Ekaṃ [M 2.0075] samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho bhagavā kismiñcideva pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇāmetvā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kapilavatthuṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Kapilavatthusmiṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena mahāvanaṃ tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya[T 3.0111]. Mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā beluvalaṭṭhikāya mūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi.

80. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Park. Then the Blessed One, having dismissed the community of monks for some reason, dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe, and entered Kapilavatthu for alms. Having gone for alms in Kapilavatthu, after the meal, on returning from the alms round, he approached the Great Wood for the day's abiding. Having entered the Great Wood, he sat down at the foot of a young wood-apple tree for the day's abiding.

Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “mayā kho bhikkhusaṅgho pabāḷho. Santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ. Tesaṃ mamaṃ apassantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo. Seyyathāpi nāma vacchassa [V 2.0085] taruṇassa mātaraṃ apassantassa siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo, evameva santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ tesaṃ mamaṃ apassantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo. Seyyathāpi nāma bījānaṃ taruṇānaṃ udakaṃ alabhantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo, evameva santettha…pe… tesaṃ mamaṃ alabhantānaṃ dassanāya siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yatheva mayā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito, evameva etarahi anuggaṇheyyaṃ bhikkhusaṅgha”nti.

Then, while the Blessed One was in seclusion and solitude, this reflection arose in his mind: 'The Saṅgha of monks has been dismissed by me. There are monks here who are new, not long gone forth, recently come to this Dhamma and Discipline. For them, not seeing me, there might be an alteration, there might be a reversal. Just as for a young calf, not seeing its mother, there might be an alteration, there might be a reversal, so too there are monks here who are new, not long gone forth, recently come to this Dhamma and Discipline; for them, not seeing me, there might be an alteration, there might be a reversal. Just as for young seeds, not obtaining water, there might be an alteration, there might be a reversal, so too there are monks here… for them, not obtaining the sight of me, there might be an alteration, there might be a reversal. What if I were to support the Saṅgha of monks now, just as I supported the Saṅgha of monks before?'

Atha kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ sammiñjitaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi. Atha [P 3.0092] kho brahmā sahampati ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “evametaṃ, bhagavā; evametaṃ, sugata[T 3.0112]! Bhagavato, bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho pabāḷho. Santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ. Tesaṃ bhagavantaṃ apassantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo. Seyyathāpi nāma vacchassa taruṇassa mātaraṃ apassantassa siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo, evameva santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā [M 2.0076] adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ tesaṃ bhagavantaṃ apassantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo. Seyyathāpi nāma bījānaṃ taruṇānaṃ udakaṃ alabhantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo, evameva santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, tesaṃ bhagavantaṃ alabhantānaṃ dassanāya siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo. Abhinandatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ; abhivadatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ. Yatheva bhagavatā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito, evameva etarahi anuggaṇhātu bhikkhusaṅgha”nti.

Then Brahmā Sahampati, knowing with his mind the reflection in the Blessed One’s mind—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—disappeared from the Brahmā world and reappeared before the Blessed One. Then Brahmā Sahampati arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined hands in reverential salutation toward the Blessed One, and said to him: 'So it is, Blessed One! So it is, Sugata!
