Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa attānudiṭṭhi uppajjati. Vedanāya [P 3.0186] sati… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa attānudiṭṭhi uppajjati[M 2.0152]. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya attānudiṭṭhi uppajjeyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya attānudiṭṭhi uppajjeyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… [V 2.0171] nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

156. At Savatthi. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does self-view arise?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, self-view arises. When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, self-view arises. What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And as for that which is impermanent, without clinging to it, would self-view arise?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And as for that which is impermanent, without clinging to it, would self-view arise?” “No, venerable sir.” “Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The seventh.

8. Abhinivesasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Adherence

157. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa uppajjanti saṃyojanābhinivesavinibandhā”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa uppajjanti saṃyojanābhinivesavinibandhā. Vedanāya [T 3.0227] sati… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa uppajjanti saṃyojanābhinivesavinibandhā. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya uppajjeyyuṃ saṃyojanābhinivesavinibandhā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”…pe… “evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

157. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, do fetters, adherences, and bonds arise?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, fetters, adherences, and bonds arise. When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, fetters, adherences, and bonds arise. What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent… without clinging to it, would fetters, adherences, and bonds arise?” “Surely not, venerable sir.” … “Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is no more for this state of being.’” The eighth.

9. Dutiyaabhinivesasuttaṃ

9. The Second Discourse on Adherence

158. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0187]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa uppajjanti saṃyojanābhinivesavinibandhājjhosānā”ti? vinibandhā ajjhosānāti (sī. ka.) Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa uppajjanti saṃyojanābhinivesavinibandhājjhosānā. Vedanāya sati [V 2.0172]… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa uppajjanti saṃyojanābhinivesavinibandhājjhosānā. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti[T 3.0228]? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya uppajjeyyuṃ saṃyojanābhinivesavinibandhājjhosānā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”…pe… “evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Navamaṃ.

158. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, do fetters, adherences, bonds, and attachments arise?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, fetters, adherences, bonds, and attachments arise. When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, fetters, adherences, bonds, and attachments arise. What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent… without clinging to it, would fetters, adherences, bonds, and attachments arise?” “Surely not, venerable sir.” … “Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is no more for this state of being.’” The ninth.

10. Ānandasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse to Ānanda

159. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0153]. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā…pe… bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti.

159. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached… he said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, ānanda, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ [V 2.0173] – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante” no hetaṃ bhante. tasmātihānanda yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… daṭṭhabbaṃ. (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). “Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… [T 3.0229][P 3.0188] nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“What do you think, Ānanda, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “It is not, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “It is not, venerable sir.” “Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is no more for this state of being.’” The tenth.

Diṭṭhivaggo pañcadasamo.

The Chapter on Views, the Fifteenth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Ajjhattikaṃ etaṃmama, soattā nocamesiyā;

Micchāsakkāyattānu dve, abhinivesā ānandenāti.

Internal, This is Mine, That Self, and It Should Not Be Mine; Wrong, Identity, and Self-View; two on Adherence, together with Ānanda.

Uparipaṇṇāsako samatto.

The Upper Fifty is concluded.

Tassa uparipaṇṇāsakassa vagguddānaṃ –

The summary of the chapters for that Upper Fifty:

Anto [T 3.0230] dhammakathikā vijjā, kukkuḷaṃ diṭṭhipañcamaṃ;

Tatiyo paṇṇāsako vutto, nipātoti pavuccatīti nipāto tena vuccatīti (sī. syā. kaṃ.).

Ends, Dhamma Speakers, Knowledge, Embers, and Views as the fifth; the Third Fifty is stated, also called a division.

Khandhasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Aggregates are concluded.

2. Rādhasaṃyuttaṃ

2. The Connected Discourses with Rādha

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Mārasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Death

160. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0231][V 2.0174][M 2.0154]. Atha kho āyasmā rādho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[P 3.0189]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

160. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Rādha approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. As he sat to one side, the Venerable Rādha said this to the Blessed One:

“‘Māro, māro’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, māro”ti? “Rūpe kho, rādha, sati māro vā assa māretā vā yo vā pana mīyati. Tasmātiha tvaṃ, rādha, rūpaṃ māroti passa, māretāti passa, mīyatīti passa, rogoti passa, gaṇḍoti passa, sallanti passa, aghanti passa, aghabhūtanti passa. Ye naṃ evaṃ passanti te sammā passanti. Vedanāya sati… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati māro vā assa māretā vā yo vā pana mīyati. Tasmātiha tvaṃ, rādha, viññāṇaṃ māroti passa, māretāti passa, mīyatīti passa, rogoti passa, gaṇḍoti passa, sallanti passa, aghanti passa, aghabhūtanti passa. Ye naṃ evaṃ passanti, te sammā passantī”ti.

“‘Death, death,’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is it said to be ‘death’?” “When there is form, Rādha, there might be death, or the one who causes death, or the one who dies. Therefore, in this teaching, Rādha, you should see form as ‘death’; see it as ‘the one who causes death’; see it as ‘the one who dies’; see it as ‘a disease’; see it as ‘a boil’; see it as ‘a dart’; see it as ‘pain’; see it as ‘a state of pain’. Those who see it thus, see rightly. When there is feeling… when there is perception… when there are formations… when there is consciousness, there might be death, or the one who causes death, or the one who dies. Therefore, in this teaching, Rādha, you should see consciousness as ‘death’; see it as ‘the one who causes death’; see it as ‘the one who dies’; see it as ‘a disease’; see it as ‘a boil’; see it as ‘a dart’; see it as ‘pain’; see it as ‘a state of pain’. Those who see it thus, see rightly.”

“Sammādassanaṃ pana, bhante, kimatthiya”nti? “Sammādassanaṃ kho, rādha, nibbidatthaṃ”. “Nibbidā pana, bhante, kimatthiyā”ti? “Nibbidā kho, rādha, virāgatthā”. “Virāgo [T 3.0232] pana, bhante[V 2.0175], kimatthiyo”ti? “Virāgo kho, rādha, vimuttattho”. “Vimutti pana, bhante, kimatthiyā”ti? “Vimutti kho, rādha, nibbānatthā”. “Nibbānaṃ pana, bhante, kimatthiya”nti? “Accayāsi accasarā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), assa (pī.), accayā (ka.), rādha, pañhaṃ, nāsakkhi pañhassa pariyantaṃ gahetuṃ. Nibbānogadhañhi, rādha, brahmacariyaṃ vussati, nibbānaparāyanaṃ nibbānapariyosāna”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“But, venerable sir, what is the purpose of right seeing?” “Right seeing, Rādha, is for the purpose of disenchantment.” “And what, venerable sir, is the purpose of disenchantment?” “Disenchantment, Rādha, is for the purpose of dispassion.” “And what, venerable sir, is the purpose of dispassion?” “Dispassion, Rādha, is for the purpose of release.” “And what, venerable sir, is the purpose of release?” “Release, Rādha, is for the purpose of Nibbāna.” “And what, venerable sir, is the purpose of Nibbāna?” “You have gone beyond the question, Rādha; you were not able to grasp the limit of the question. For, Rādha, the holy life is lived grounded in Nibbāna, with Nibbāna as its destination, and Nibbāna as its culmination.” The first.

2. Sattasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on a Being

161. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ [P 3.0190] etadavoca – “‘satto, satto’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante[M 2.0155], sattoti vuccatī”ti? “Rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, tatra satto, tatra visatto, tasmā sattoti vuccati. Vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhāresu… viññāṇe yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, tatra satto, tatra visatto, tasmā sattoti vuccati”.

161. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, it is said, ‘attached, attached.’ To what extent, Venerable Sir, is one said to be ‘attached’?” “Rādha, whatever desire, whatever passion, whatever delight, whatever craving there is for form, therein one is attached, therein one is thoroughly attached. Therefore, one is said to be ‘attached.’ Whatever desire, whatever passion, whatever delight, whatever craving there is for feeling… for perception… for formations… for consciousness, therein one is attached, therein one is thoroughly attached. Therefore, one is said to be ‘attached.’”

“Seyyathāpi, rādha, kumārakā vā kumārikāyo vā paṃsvāgārakehi kīḷanti. Yāvakīvañca tesu paṃsvāgārakesu avigatarāgā honti avigatacchandā avigatapemā avigatapipāsā avigatapariḷāhā avigatataṇhā, tāva tāni paṃsvāgārakāni allīyanti keḷāyanti dhanāyanti [T 3.0233] manāyanti (sī. pī. ka.) mamāyanti. Yato ca kho, rādha, kumārakā vā kumārikāyo vā tesu paṃsvāgārakesu vigatarāgā honti vigatacchandā vigatapemā vigatapipāsā vigatapariḷāhā vigatataṇhā, atha kho tāni paṃsvāgārakāni hatthehi ca pādehi ca vikiranti vidhamanti viddhaṃsenti vikīḷaniyaṃ vikīḷanikaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) karonti. Evameva kho, rādha, tumhepi rūpaṃ vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṃsetha vikīḷaniyaṃ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha. Vedanaṃ vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṃsetha vikīḷaniyaṃ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha. Saññaṃ… saṅkhāre vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṃsetha vikīḷaniyaṃ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha. Viññāṇaṃ vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṃsetha vikīḷaniyaṃ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha. Taṇhākkhayo hi, rādha, nibbāna”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Suppose, Rādha, that young boys or girls are playing with little sandcastles. For as long as they are not without passion, not without desire, not without affection, not without thirst, not without fever, and not without craving for those little sandcastles, they cling to them, play with them, treat them as treasure, and cherish them as ‘mine.’ But when, Rādha, those young boys or girls are without passion, without desire, without affection, without thirst, without fever, and without craving for those little sandcastles, then they scatter them with their hands and feet, demolish them, destroy them, and make an end of playing with them. In the same way, Rādha, you too should scatter form, demolish it, destroy it, and make an end of playing with it; practice for the destruction of craving. Scatter feeling, demolish it, destroy it, and make an end of playing with it; practice for the destruction of craving. Scatter perception… Scatter formations, demolish them, destroy them, and make an end of playing with them; practice for the destruction of craving. Scatter consciousness, demolish it, destroy it, and make an end of playing with it; practice for the destruction of craving. For the destruction of craving, Rādha, is Nibbāna.”

3. Bhavanettisuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Cord of Existence

162. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘bhavanettinirodho [V 2.0176] bhavanetti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), bhavanettinirodho’ti bhavanettīti (sī. syā. kaṃ.), bhante, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, bhante, bhavanetti, katamo bhavanettinirodho”ti? “Rūpe [P 3.0191] kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā – ayaṃ vuccati bhavanetti. Tesaṃ nirodho nirodhā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhavanettinirodho. Vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhāresu [M 2.0156]… viññāṇe yo chando…pe… adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā [T 3.0234] – ayaṃ vuccati bhavanetti. Tesaṃ nirodho bhavanettinirodho”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

162. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “‘The cessation of the cord of existence, the cessation of the cord of existence,’ it is said, venerable sir. But what, venerable sir, is the cord of existence, and what is the cessation of the cord of existence?” “Rādha, whatever desire, passion, delight, craving, attachments and clingings, mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies there are regarding form—this is called the cord of existence. The cessation of these is the cessation of the cord of existence. Regarding feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, whatever desire… and so forth… mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies there are—this is called the cord of existence. The cessation of these is the cessation of the cord of existence.”

4. Pariññeyyasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on What Is to Be Fully Understood

163. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Āyasmā rādho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rādhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

163. At Sāvatthī. The Venerable Rādha approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Rādha:

“Pariññeyye ca, rādha, dhamme desessāmi pariññañca pariññātāviṃ puggalañca. Taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā rādho bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca – “katame ca, rādha, pariññeyyā dhammā? Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, pariññeyyo dhammo, vedanā pariññeyyo dhammo, saññā pariññeyyo dhammo, saṅkhārā pariññeyyo dhammo, viññāṇaṃ pariññeyyo dhammo. Ime vuccanti, rādha, pariññeyyā dhammā. Katamā ca, rādha, pariññā? Yo kho, rādha, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – ayaṃ vuccati, rādha, pariññā. Katamo ca, rādha, pariññātāvī puggalo? ‘Arahā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Yvāyaṃ āyasmā evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto – ayaṃ vuccati, rādha, pariññātāvī puggalo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“I will teach you, Rādha, the things to be fully understood, full understanding, and the person who has fully understood. Listen to that and attend closely; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Rādha replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “And what, Rādha, are the things to be fully understood? Form, Rādha, is a thing to be fully understood; feeling is a thing to be fully understood; perception is a thing to be fully understood; formations are a thing to be fully understood; consciousness is a thing to be fully understood. These, Rādha, are called the things to be fully understood. And what, Rādha, is full understanding? The destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion—this, Rādha, is called full understanding. And who, Rādha, is the person who has fully understood? He is to be called an ‘arahant.’ That venerable one of such a name and clan—this, Rādha, is called the person who has fully understood.”

5. Samaṇasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Ascetics

164. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rādhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “pañcime, rādha, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho[V 2.0177], saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ye hi [T 3.0235] keci, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṃ pañcannaṃ [P 3.0192] upādānakkhandhānaṃ assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti; na me te, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti. Ye ca kho keci, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānanti; te kho me, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā[M 2.0157], te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

164. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to the Venerable Rādha: “Rādha, there are these five aggregates subject to clinging. Which five? The form aggregate subject to clinging, the feeling aggregate subject to clinging, the perception aggregate subject to clinging, the formations aggregate subject to clinging, and the consciousness aggregate subject to clinging. Rādha, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand as it actually is the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to these five aggregates subject to clinging—I do not consider them to be ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins, nor do those venerable ones, having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge, enter upon and dwell in the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood in this very life. But, Rādha, whatever ascetics or brahmins do understand as it actually is the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to these five aggregates subject to clinging—I consider them to be ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins, and those venerable ones, having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge, enter upon and dwell in the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood in this very life.”

6. Dutiyasamaṇasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Ascetics

165. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rādhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “pañcime, rādha, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho…pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ye hi keci, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti…pe… sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

165. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to Venerable Rādha: “Rādha, there are these five aggregates of clinging. Which five? The form aggregate of clinging … the consciousness aggregate of clinging. Rādha, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand as it actually is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to these five aggregates of clinging—I do not consider them to be ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins, nor do those venerable ones, having realized for themselves with direct knowledge, enter and dwell in the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood in this very life. But, Rādha, whatever ascetics or brahmins do understand as it actually is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to these five aggregates of clinging—I consider them to be ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins, and those venerable ones, having realized for themselves with direct knowledge, enter and dwell in the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood in this very life.” The Sixth.

7. Sotāpannasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Stream-Enterer

166. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0236]. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rādhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “pañcime, rādha, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho…pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Yato [P 3.0193] kho, rādha, ariyasāvako imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti – ayaṃ vuccati, rādha, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Sattamaṃ.

166. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to Venerable Rādha: “Rādha, there are these five aggregates of clinging. Which five? The form aggregate of clinging... the consciousness aggregate of clinging. Rādha, since a noble disciple understands as it truly is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these five aggregates of clinging, this one is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not subject to states of woe, fixed, with enlightenment as his destination.” The Seventh.

8. Arahantasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Arahant

167. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0178]. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rādhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “pañcime, rādha, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho…pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Yato kho, rādha, bhikkhu imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādāvimutto hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, rādha, arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññāvimutto”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

167. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to Venerable Rādha: “Rādha, there are these five aggregates of clinging. Which five? The form aggregate of clinging... the consciousness aggregate of clinging. Rādha, since a bhikkhu, having known as it truly is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these five aggregates of clinging, is liberated without clinging, he is called an Arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, who has done what had to be done, who has laid down the burden, who has attained his own goal, whose fetter of becoming is destroyed, and who is liberated by right final knowledge.” The Eighth.

9. Chandarāgasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Desire and Lust

168. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rādhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṃ pajahatha. Evaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ pahīnaṃ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ. Vedanāya yo [M 2.0158] chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṃ pajahatha[T 3.0237]. Evaṃ sā vedanā pahīnā bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Saññāya… saṅkhāresu yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṃ pajahatha. Evaṃ te saṅkhārā pahīnā bhavissanti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Viññāṇe [P 3.0194] yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṃ pajahatha. Evaṃ taṃ viññāṇaṃ pahīnaṃ bhavissati…pe… anuppādadhamma”nti. Navamaṃ.

168. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to Venerable Rādha: “Rādha, whatever desire, whatever lust, whatever delight, whatever craving there is for form, abandon it. In this way, that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and not subject to future arising. Whatever desire, whatever lust, whatever delight, whatever craving there is for feeling, abandon it. In this way, that feeling will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and not subject to future arising. …for perception… Whatever desire, whatever lust, whatever delight, whatever craving there is for volitional formations, abandon it. In this way, those volitional formations will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and not subject to future arising. Whatever desire, whatever lust, whatever delight, whatever craving there is for consciousness, abandon it. In this way, that consciousness will be abandoned… not subject to future arising.” The Ninth.

10. Dutiyachandarāgasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on Desire and Lust

169. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rādhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha. Evaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ pahīnaṃ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ. Vedanāya yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha. Evaṃ sā vedanā pahīnā [V 2.0179] bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Saññāya… saṅkhāresu yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha. Evaṃ te saṅkhārā pahīnā bhavissanti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Viññāṇe [T 3.0238] yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha. Evaṃ taṃ viññāṇaṃ pahīnaṃ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhamma”nti. Dasamaṃ.

169. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to the Venerable Rādha: “Rādha, abandon the desire, lust, delight, craving, attachments, clingings, mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies for form. Thus, that form will be abandoned—cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise again in the future. Abandon the desire, lust, delight, craving, attachments, clingings, mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies for feeling. Thus, that feeling will be abandoned—cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise again in the future. Abandon the desire, lust, delight, craving, attachments, clingings, mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies for perception… Abandon the desire, lust, delight, craving, attachments, clingings, mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies for formations. Thus, those formations will be abandoned—cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise again in the future. Abandon the desire, lust, delight, craving, attachments, clingings, mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies for consciousness. Thus, that consciousness will be abandoned—cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise again in the future.” The Tenth.

Rādhasaṃyuttassa paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter of the Rādha Saṃyutta.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Māro satto bhavanetti, pariññeyyā samaṇā duve;

Sotāpanno arahā ca, chandarāgāpare duveti.

Māra, a Being, the Guide to Existence, To Be Fully Understood; two on the Recluse, the Stream-enterer, and the Arahant; and two others on Desire and Lust.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Mārasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Māra

170. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0239][M 2.0159][P 3.0195]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘māro, māro’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, māro”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, māro, vedanā māro, saññā māro, saṅkhārā māro, viññāṇaṃ māro. Evaṃ passaṃ, rādha, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

170. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, it is said, ‘death, death.’ What now, Venerable Sir, is death?” “Form, Rādha, is death; feeling is death; perception is death; volitional formations are death; consciousness is death. Seeing thus, Rādha, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with volitional formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When he is liberated, the knowledge arises, ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’” The First.

2. Māradhammasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Nature of Death

171. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0180]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘māradhammo, māradhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, māradhammo”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, māradhammo, vedanā māradhammo, saññā māradhammo, saṅkhārā māradhammo, viññāṇaṃ māradhammo. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

171. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘of the nature of death, of the nature of death.’ What, venerable sir, is of the nature of death?” “Form, Rādha, is of the nature of death; feeling is of the nature of death; perception is of the nature of death; volitional formations are of the nature of death; consciousness is of the nature of death. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is no more for this state of being.’” The Second.

3. Aniccasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Impermanence

172. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘aniccaṃ, anicca’nti, bhante, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu [T 3.0240] kho, bhante, anicca”nti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, aniccaṃ, vedanā aniccā, saññā aniccā, saṅkhārā aniccā, viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

172. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘impermanent, impermanent.’ What, venerable sir, is impermanent?” “Form, Rādha, is impermanent; feeling is impermanent; perception is impermanent; volitional formations are impermanent; consciousness is impermanent. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is no more for this state of being.’” The Third.

4. Aniccadhammasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Nature of Impermanence

173. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘aniccadhammo, aniccadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, aniccadhammo”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, aniccadhammo, vedanā aniccadhammo[P 3.0196], saññā aniccadhammo, saṅkhārā aniccadhammo, viññāṇaṃ aniccadhammo. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… [V 2.0181] nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

173. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘of the nature of impermanence, of the nature of impermanence.’ What, venerable sir, is of the nature of impermanence?” “Form, Rādha, is of the nature of impermanence; feeling is of the nature of impermanence; perception is of the nature of impermanence; volitional formations are of the nature of impermanence; consciousness is of the nature of impermanence. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Fourth.

5. Dukkhasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Suffering

174. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0160]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘dukkhaṃ, dukkha’nti, bhante, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, bhante, dukkha”nti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, dukkhaṃ, vedanā dukkhā, saññā dukkhā, saṅkhārā dukkhā, viññāṇaṃ dukkhaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

174. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘suffering, suffering.’ What, venerable sir, is suffering?” “Form, Rādha, is suffering; feeling is suffering; perception is suffering; volitional formations are suffering; consciousness is suffering. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Fifth.

6. Dukkhadhammasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Nature of Suffering

175. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘dukkhadhammo, dukkhadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, dukkhadhammo”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, dukkhadhammo, vedanā dukkhadhammo, saññā dukkhadhammo, saṅkhārā dukkhadhammo, viññāṇaṃ dukkhadhammo. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

175. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘of the nature of suffering, of the nature of suffering.’ What, venerable sir, is of the nature of suffering?” “Form, Rādha, is of the nature of suffering; feeling is of the nature of suffering; perception is of the nature of suffering; volitional formations are of the nature of suffering; consciousness is of the nature of suffering. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Sixth.

7. Anattasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Not-Self

176. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ [T 3.0241] etadavoca – “‘anattā, anattā’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, anattā”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, anattā, vedanā anattā, saññā anattā, saṅkhārā anattā, viññāṇaṃ anattā. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… [V 2.0182] nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

176. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘not-self, not-self.’ What, venerable sir, is not-self?” “Form, Rādha, is not-self; feeling is not-self; perception is not-self; volitional formations are not-self; consciousness is not-self. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Seventh.

8. Anattadhammasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Nature of Not-Self

177. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘anattadhammo, anattadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, anattadhammo”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, anattadhammo, vedanā anattadhammo[P 3.0197], saññā anattadhammo, saṅkhārā anattadhammo, viññāṇaṃ anattadhammo. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

177. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘of the nature of not-self, of the nature of not-self.’ What, venerable sir, is of the nature of not-self?” “Form, Rādha, is of the nature of not-self; feeling is of the nature of not-self; perception is of the nature of not-self; volitional formations are of the nature of not-self; consciousness is of the nature of not-self. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Eighth.

9.Khayadhammasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Nature of Destruction

178. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘khayadhammo, khayadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, khayadhammo”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, khayadhammo, vedanā khayadhammo, saññā [M 2.0161] khayadhammo, saṅkhārā khayadhammo, viññāṇaṃ khayadhammo. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Navamaṃ.

178. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘of the nature of destruction, of the nature of destruction.’ What, venerable sir, is of the nature of destruction?” “Form, Rādha, is of the nature of destruction; feeling is of the nature of destruction; perception is of the nature of destruction; volitional formations are of the nature of destruction; consciousness is of the nature of destruction. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Ninth.

10. Vayadhammasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Nature of Perishing

179. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘vayadhammo, vayadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, vayadhammo”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, vayadhammo, vedanā vayadhammo, saññā vayadhammo, saṅkhārā vayadhammo, viññāṇaṃ vayadhammo[V 2.0183]. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

179. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘of the nature of perishing, of the nature of perishing.’ What, venerable sir, is of the nature of perishing?” “Form, Rādha, is of the nature of perishing; feeling is of the nature of perishing; perception is of the nature of perishing; volitional formations are of the nature of perishing; consciousness is of the nature of perishing. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Tenth.

11. Samudayadhammasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on the Nature of Arising

180. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0242]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘samudayadhammo, samudayadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, samudayadhammo”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, samudayadhammo, vedanā samudayadhammo, saññā samudayadhammo, saṅkhārā samudayadhammo, viññāṇaṃ samudayadhammo. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

180. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘of the nature of arising, of the nature of arising.’ What, venerable sir, is of the nature of arising?” “Form, Rādha, is of the nature of arising; feeling is of the nature of arising; perception is of the nature of arising; volitional formations are of the nature of arising; consciousness is of the nature of arising. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Eleventh.

12. Nirodhadhammasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on the Nature of Cessation

181. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘nirodhadhammo, nirodhadhammo’ti[P 3.0198], bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, nirodhadhammo”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo, vedanā nirodhadhammo, saññā nirodhadhammo, saṅkhārā nirodhadhammo, viññāṇaṃ nirodhadhammo. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

181. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘of the nature of cessation, of the nature of cessation.’ What, venerable sir, is of the nature of cessation?” “Form, Rādha, is of the nature of cessation; feeling is of the nature of cessation; perception is of the nature of cessation; volitional formations are of the nature of cessation; consciousness is of the nature of cessation. Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Twelfth.

Rādhasaṃyuttassa dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter of the Rādha Saṃyutta.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that chapter:

Māro [V 2.0184] ca māradhammo ca, aniccena apare duve;

Dukkhena ca duve vuttā, anattena anattehi (sī. syā. kaṃ.) tatheva ca;

Khayavayasamudayaṃ, nirodhadhammena dvādasāti.

Māra and Māradhamma, and two others with impermanence; two are spoken of with suffering, and likewise with not-self; Perishing, Vanishing, Arising, and with the Nature of Cessation, making twelve in all.

3. Āyācanavaggo

3. The Third Chapter: On Requesting

1-11. Mārādisuttaekādasakaṃ

1–11. The Eleven Discourses Beginning with Māra

182. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0243][M 2.0162]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti.

182. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and with my mind directed to Nibbāna.'

“Yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo sīhaḷapotthake pana “tatra te chando pahātabboti ekaṃ suttaṃ, tatra te rāgo pahātabboti ekaṃ suttaṃ, tatra te chandarāgo pahātabboti ekaṃ sutta”nti evaṃ visuṃ visuṃ tīṇi suttāni vibhajitvā dassitāni. evamuparisuttesupi. Ko ca, rādha, māro? Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo sīhaḷapotthake pana “tatra te chando pahātabboti ekaṃ suttaṃ, tatra te rāgo pahātabboti ekaṃ suttaṃ, tatra te chandarāgo pahātabboti ekaṃ sutta”nti evaṃ visuṃ visuṃ tīṇi suttāni vibhajitvā dassitāni. evamuparisuttesupi. Vedanā māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… saññā māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… saṅkhārā māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… viññāṇaṃ māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.

'Rādha, whatever is death, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust. And what, Rādha, is death? Form, Rādha, is death; therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust. Feeling is death; therein you should abandon desire... perception is death; therein you should abandon desire... volitional formations are death; therein you should abandon desire... consciousness is death; therein you should abandon desire... Whatever, Rādha, is death, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust.'

183. Yo kho, rādha, māradhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo…pe….

183. 'Rādha, whatever has the nature of death, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

184. Yaṃ [P 3.0199] kho, rādha, aniccaṃ…pe….

184. 'Rādha, whatever is impermanent, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

185. Yo [V 2.0185] kho, rādha, aniccadhammo…pe….

185. 'Rādha, whatever has the nature of impermanence, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

186. Yaṃ kho, rādha, dukkhaṃ…pe….

186. 'Rādha, whatever is suffering, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

187. Yo kho, rādha, dukkhadhammo…pe….

187. 'Rādha, whatever has the nature of suffering, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

188. Yo [T 3.0244] kho, rādha, anattā…pe….

188. 'Rādha, whatever is not-self, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

189. Yo [M 2.0163] kho, rādha, anattadhammo…pe….

189. 'Rādha, whatever has the nature of not-self, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

190. Yo kho, rādha, khayadhammo…pe….

190. 'Rādha, whatever has the nature of perishing, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

191. Yo kho, rādha, vayadhammo…pe….

191. 'Rādha, whatever has the nature of vanishing, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

192. Yo kho, rādha, samudayadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo…pe….

192. 'Rādha, whatever has the nature of arising, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust...'

12. Nirodhadhammasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on the Nature of Cessation

193. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti.

193. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rādha said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and with my mind directed to Nibbāna.”

“Yo [V 2.0186] kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Ko ca, rādha, nirodhadhammo? Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… vedanā nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… saññā nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… saṅkhārā nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… viññāṇaṃ nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti sīhaḷapotthake pana imasmiṃ vagge chattiṃsa suttāni vibhattāni ekekaṃ suttaṃ tīṇi tīṇi katvā, evaṃ catutthavaggepi.

“Rādha, whatever has the nature of cessation, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust. And what, Rādha, has the nature of cessation? Form, Rādha, has the nature of cessation; therein you should abandon desire… Feeling has the nature of cessation; therein you should abandon desire… Perception has the nature of cessation; therein you should abandon desire… Volitional formations have the nature of cessation; therein you should abandon desire… Consciousness has the nature of cessation; therein you should abandon desire… Rādha, whatever has the nature of cessation, therein you should abandon desire, you should abandon lust, you should abandon desire-lust.”

Āyācanavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on Requesting.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this is:

Māro [T 3.0245][P 3.0200] ca māradhammo ca, aniccena apare duve;

Dukkhena ca duve vuttā, anattena tatheva ca;

Khayavayasamudayaṃ, nirodhadhammena dvādasāti.

Māra and Māradhamma, and two others with impermanence; two are spoken of with suffering, and likewise with not-self; Perishing, Vanishing, Arising, and with the Nature of Cessation, making twelve in all.

4. Upanisinnavaggo

4. The Fourth Chapter: On Being Seated Nearby

1-11. Mārādisuttaekādasakaṃ

1-11. The Eleven Discourses Beginning with Māra

194. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0246][M 2.0164]. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rādhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Ko ca, rādha, māro? Rūpaṃ kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… viññāṇaṃ māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.

194. At Sāvatthī. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Rādha, who was sitting to one side: “Rādha, whatever is death, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned. And what, Rādha, is death? Form, Rādha, is death; therein your desire should be abandoned… Consciousness is death; therein your desire should be abandoned… Whatever, Rādha, is death, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned.”

195. Yo kho, rādha, māradhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo [V 2.0187] pahātabbo…pe….

196. Yaṃ kho, rādha, aniccaṃ…pe….

196. “Rādha, whatever is impermanent, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned…”

197. Yo kho, rādha, aniccadhammo…pe….

197. “Rādha, whatever has the nature of impermanence, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned…”

198. Yaṃ [P 3.0201] kho, rādha, dukkhaṃ…pe….

198. “Rādha, whatever is suffering, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned…”

199. Yo kho, rādha, dukkhadhammo…pe….

199. “Rādha, whatever has the nature of suffering, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned…”

200. Yo kho, rādha, anattā…pe….

200. “Rādha, whatever is not-self, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned…”

201. Yo kho, rādha, anattadhammo…pe….

201. “Rādha, whatever has the nature of not-self, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned…”

202. Yo kho, rādha, khayadhammo…pe….

202. “Rādha, whatever has the nature of perishing, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned…”

203. Yo kho, rādha, vayadhammo…pe….

203. “Rādha, whatever has the nature of vanishing, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned…”

204. Yo [T 3.0247] kho, rādha, samudayadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo [V 2.0188] pahātabbo…pe….

204. “Rādha, whatever has the nature of arising, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned…”

12. Nirodhadhammasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on the Nature of Cessation

205. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rādhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Ko ca, rādha, nirodhadhammo? Rūpaṃ [M 2.0165] kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇaṃ nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.

205. At Sāvatthī. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Rādha, who was sitting to one side: “Rādha, whatever has the nature of cessation, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned. And what, Rādha, has the nature of cessation? Form, Rādha, has the nature of cessation; therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned. Feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness has the nature of cessation; therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned. Whatever, Rādha, has the nature of cessation, therein your desire should be abandoned, your lust should be abandoned, your desire-lust should be abandoned.”

Upanisinnavaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter on Being Seated Nearby.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Māro ca māradhammo ca, aniccena apare duve;

Dukkhena ca duve vuttā, anattena tatheva ca;

Khayavayasamudayaṃ, nirodhadhammena dvādasāti.

Māra and Māradhamma, and two others with impermanence; two are spoken of with suffering, and likewise with not-self; Perishing, Vanishing, Arising, and with the Nature of Cessation, making twelve in all.

Rādhasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses with Rādha are completed.

3. Diṭṭhisaṃyuttaṃ

3. The Connected Discourses on Views

1. Sotāpattivaggo

1. The Chapter on Stream-Entry

1. Vātasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Wind

206. Ekaṃ [T 3.0248][V 2.0189][M 2.0166] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane. Bhagavā etadavoca [P 3.0202] – “kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti?

206. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view as this arise: ‘The winds do not blow, the rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the sun and moon do not rise or set, but stand firm like a pillar’?”

“Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaññeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One, guided by the Blessed One, and have the Blessed One as their refuge. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One himself would elucidate the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will bear it in mind.” “Then, bhikkhus, listen and attend carefully; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’ti. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’ti. Taṃ [T 3.0249] kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”[V 2.0190]. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti? “No [P 3.0203] hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view as this arises: ‘The winds do not blow, the rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the sun and moon do not rise or set, but stand firm like a pillar.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view as this arises: ‘The winds do not blow, the rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the sun and moon do not rise or set, but stand firm like a pillar.’ What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, could such a view as this arise without clinging to it: ‘The winds do not blow, the rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the sun and moon do not rise or set, but stand firm like a pillar’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Vedanā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti… “saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti [M 2.0167] vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ yamidaṃ (aññattha) diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Is feeling permanent or impermanent?”… “Is perception… are volitional formations… is consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, could such a view as this arise without clinging to it: ‘The winds do not blow, the rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the sun and moon do not rise or set, but stand firm like a pillar’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought, and mentally pondered—is that too permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, could such a view as this arise without clinging to it: ‘The winds do not blow, the rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the sun and moon do not rise or set, but stand firm like a pillar’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca imesu chasu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) evamuparipi ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā [T 3.0250] hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhasamudayepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhanirodhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple’s doubt concerning these six bases is abandoned, his doubt concerning suffering is also abandoned, his doubt concerning the origin of suffering is also abandoned, his doubt concerning the cessation of suffering is also abandoned, and his doubt concerning the path leading to the cessation of suffering is also abandoned—this, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not subject to fall, assured, and heading for full enlightenment.” First.

2. Etaṃmamasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on ‘This is Mine’

207. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe [P 3.0204] kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati [V 2.0191]… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti.

207. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view as this arise: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view as this arises: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view as this arises: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… “vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi [T 3.0251] niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.”… “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… is consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.”… “Could such a view as this arise without clinging to it: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought, and mentally pondered—is that too permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, could such a view as this arise without clinging to it: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Yato [M 2.0168] kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple has abandoned doubt in these instances, and for whom doubt about suffering is also abandoned… for whom doubt about the path of practice leading to the cessation of suffering is also abandoned—this, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not subject to perdition, assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Second.

3. Soattāsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on ‘That Is the Self’

208. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘so attā, so loko, so pecca bhavissāmi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā [P 3.0205] no, bhante, dhammā…pe….

208. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view as this arise: ‘That which is the self is the world; after death I shall be that—permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…”

“Rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘so attā, so loko, so pecca bhavissāmi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo’ti[V 2.0192]. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘so attā, so loko, so pecca bhavissāmi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view as this arises: ‘That which is the self is the world; after death I shall be that—permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view as this arises: ‘That which is the self is the world; after death I shall be that—permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ bhante”…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ [T 3.0252] diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘so attā…pe… avipariṇāmadhammo’ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘so attā…pe… avipariṇāmadhammo’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘so attā, so loko, so pecca bhavissāmi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.”… “Without clinging to that, could such a view as this arise: ‘That which is the self is the world; after death I shall be that… not subject to change’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.”… “Without clinging to that, could such a view as this arise: ‘That which is the self is the world; after death I shall be that… not subject to change’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Also, that which is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and explored by the mind—is that permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.”… “Without clinging to that, could such a view as this arise: ‘That which is the self is the world; after death I shall be that—permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple has abandoned doubt in these instances, and for whom doubt about suffering is also abandoned… for whom doubt about the path of practice leading to the cessation of suffering is also abandoned—this, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not subject to perdition, assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Third.

4. Nocamesiyāsuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on ‘It Would Not Be Mine’

209. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0169]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me [T 3.0253] bhavissatī’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe….

209. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view as this arise: ‘I would not be, and it would not be mine; I will not be, and it will not be mine’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…”

“Rūpe [V 2.0193] kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa [P 3.0206] evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti. Vedanāya sati… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view as this arises: ‘I would not be, and it would not be mine; I will not be, and it will not be mine.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view as this arises: ‘I would not be, and it would not be mine; I will not be, and it will not be mine.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘no cassaṃ, no ca me siyā, nābhavissa, na me bhavissatī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to that, would such a view as this arise: ‘I would not be, and it would not be mine; I will not be, and it will not be mine’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to that, would such a view as this arise: ‘I would not be, and it would not be mine; I will not be, and it will not be mine’?” “No, venerable sir.” “And that which is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and explored by the mind—is that also permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to that, would such a view as this arise: ‘I would not be, and it would not be mine; I will not be, and it will not be mine’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple has abandoned doubt in these instances, and for whom doubt about suffering is also abandoned… for whom doubt about the path of practice leading to the cessation of suffering is also abandoned—this, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not of a nature to fall into lower realms, assured, and bound for enlightenment.” Fourth.

5. Natthidinnasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on ‘There Is Nothing Given’

210. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0254]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ [V 2.0194] sukkaṭadukkaṭānaṃ (sī. pī.) kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko; natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā; natthi loke [M 2.0170] samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā samaggatā (ka.) sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedenti. Cātumahābhūtiko cātummahābhūtiko (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ayaṃ puriso yadā [P 3.0207] kālaṅkaroti pathavī pathavīkāyaṃ anupeti anupagacchati, āpo āpokāyaṃ anupeti anupagacchati, tejo tejokāyaṃ anupeti anupagacchati, vāyo vāyokāyaṃ anupeti anupagacchati. Ākāsaṃ indriyāni saṅkamanti. Āsandipañcamā purisā mataṃ ādāya gacchanti. Yāva āḷāhanā padāni paññāyanti. Kāpotakāni aṭṭhīni bhavanti. Bhassantā āhutiyo. Dattupaññattaṃ yadidaṃ dānaṃ dattupaññattamidaṃ dānaṃ nāma (sabbattha). Tesaṃ tucchaṃ musā vilāpo ye keci atthikavādaṃ vadanti. Bāle ca paṇḍite ca kāyassa bhedā ucchijjanti vinassanti na honti paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… kāyassa bhedā ucchijjanti vinassanti na honti paraṃ maraṇā’ti. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati[T 3.0255], viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… kāyassa bhedā ucchijjanti vinassanti na honti paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

210. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view as this arise: ‘There is nothing given, nothing sacrificed, nothing offered; there is no fruit or result of good and bad deeds; there is no this world, no other world; there is no mother, there is no father; there are no spontaneously arisen beings; there are no ascetics or brahmins in the world who are rightly directed and rightly practiced, who, having realized this world and the other world for themselves by direct knowledge, make it known. This person is composed of the four great elements. When one dies, the earth element returns and goes back to the body of earth; the water element returns and goes back to the body of water; the fire element returns and goes back to the body of fire; the air element returns and goes back to the body of air. The faculties pass into space. Men, with the bier as the fifth, carry away the dead. As far as the charnel ground, their footprints are seen. The bones become dove-colored. Offerings end in ashes. This which is called giving is a teaching of fools. The talk of those who speak of an existence-doctrine is empty, false, and babble. Both the foolish and the wise, with the breakup of the body, are annihilated, they perish, they do not exist after death’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view as this arises: ‘There is nothing given, nothing sacrificed… they do not exist after death.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view as this arises: ‘There is nothing given, nothing sacrificed… they do not exist after death.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… kāyassa bhedā ucchijjanti vinassanti na honti paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… kāyassa [P 3.0208] bhedā ucchijjanti vinassanti na honti paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… ye keci atthikavādaṃ [V 2.0195] vadanti; bāle ca paṇḍite ca kāyassa bhedā ucchijjanti vinassanti na honti paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to it, would such a view arise: ‘There is nothing given, nothing sacrificed… with the breakup of the body, they are annihilated, they perish, and do not exist after death’?” “Indeed not, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to it, would such a view arise: ‘There is nothing given, nothing sacrificed… with the breakup of the body, they are annihilated, they perish, and do not exist after death’?” “Indeed not, venerable sir.” “And whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and pondered by the mind—is that also permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to it, would such a view arise: ‘There is nothing given, nothing sacrificed… whoever speaks the doctrine of existence, both the foolish and the wise, with the breakup of the body, are annihilated, perish, and do not exist after death’?” “Indeed not, venerable sir.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa [M 2.0171] kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave[T 3.0256], ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple has abandoned doubt in these instances, and for whom doubt in suffering is abandoned… and for whom doubt in the path leading to the cessation of suffering is abandoned—this, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not subject to perdition, assured, and destined for enlightenment.”

6. Karotosuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Doer

211. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘karoto kārayato chindato chedāpayato pacato pācāpayato socato socāpayato kilamato kilamāpayato phandato phandāpayato pāṇamatipātayato adinnaṃ ādiyato sandhiṃ chindato nillopaṃ harato ekāgārikaṃ karoto paripanthe tiṭṭhato paradāraṃ gacchato musā bhaṇato karoto na karīyati pāpaṃ. Khurapariyantena cepi cakkena yo imissā pathaviyā pāṇe ekamaṃsakhalaṃ ekamaṃsapuñjaṃ kareyya, natthi tatonidānaṃ pāpaṃ, natthi pāpassa āgamo. Dakkhiṇaṃ cepi gaṅgāya tīraṃ gaccheyya; hananto [P 3.0209] ghātento chindanto chedāpento pacanto pācento, natthi tatonidānaṃ pāpaṃ, natthi pāpassa āgamo. Uttaraṃ cepi gaṅgāya tīraṃ gaccheyya; dadanto dāpento yajanto yajāpento, natthi tatonidānaṃ puññaṃ, natthi puññassa āgamo. Dānena damena saṃyamena saccavajjena natthi puññaṃ natthi puññassa āgamo’”ti. Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘karoto kārayato…pe… natthi puññaṃ natthi puññassa āgamo’ti. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe [T 3.0257] sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘karoto kārayato…pe… natthi puññaṃ natthi puññassa āgamo’”ti.

211. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view arise: ‘For one who acts or causes another to act; who cuts or causes another to cut; who oppresses or causes another to oppress; who sorrows or causes another to sorrow; who becomes weary or causes another to be weary; who trembles or causes another to tremble; who kills living beings; who takes what is not given; who breaks into houses; who plunders; who robs a single house; who commits highway robbery; who goes to another’s wife; who speaks falsehood—for one who acts thus, no evil is done. Even if with a razor-edged wheel one were to make all the living beings on this earth into a single mass of flesh, a single heap of flesh, there would be no evil from that cause, no accrual of evil. If one were to go along the southern bank of the Ganges killing and causing to kill, cutting and causing to cut, oppressing and causing to oppress, there would be no evil from that cause, no accrual of evil. If one were to go along the northern bank of the Ganges giving and causing to give, sacrificing and causing to sacrifice, there would be no merit from that cause, no accrual of merit. Through giving, taming, restraint, and truthful speech, there is no merit, no accrual of merit’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view arises: ‘For one who acts or causes another to act… there is no merit, no accrual of merit.’ When feeling exists… When perception exists… When formations exist… When consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view arises: ‘For one who acts or causes another to act… there is no merit, no accrual of merit.’”

“Taṃ [V 2.0196] kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘karoto…pe… natthi puññaṃ natthi puññassa āgamo”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘karoto kārayato [M 2.0172] …pe… natthi puññaṃ natthi puññassa āgamo’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘karoto kārayato…pe… natthi puññaṃ natthi puññassa āgamo’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.
