“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘For one who acts… there is no merit, there is no accrual of merit’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘For one who acts, for one who causes another to act… there is no merit, there is no accrual of merit’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and explored by the mind—is that also permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘For one who acts, for one who causes another to act… there is no merit, there is no accrual of merit’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple has abandoned doubt in these instances, and for whom doubt concerning suffering is abandoned… and for whom doubt concerning the path leading to the cessation of suffering is abandoned—this one, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not subject to fall, fixed in destiny, and bound for enlightenment.” The sixth.

7. Hetusuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Cause

212. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0210]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘natthi hetu, natthi paccayo sattānaṃ [T 3.0258] saṃkilesāya. Ahetū appaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti. Natthi hetu, natthi paccayo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā. Ahetū appaccayā sattā visujjhanti. Natthi balaṃ natthi vīriyaṃ natthi purisathāmo natthi purisaparakkamo. Sabbe sattā sabbe pāṇā sabbe bhūtā sabbe jīvā avasā abalā avīriyā niyatisaṅgatibhāvapariṇatā chasvevābhijātīsu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘natthi hetu, natthi paccayo…pe… sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’ti[V 2.0197]. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘natthi hetu, natthi paccayo…pe… sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’”ti.

212. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view arise: ‘There is no cause, no condition for the defilement of beings. Beings are defiled without cause or condition. There is no cause, no condition for the purification of beings. Beings are purified without cause or condition. There is no strength, no energy, no manly force, no manly exertion. All beings, all breathing things, all creatures, all living things are powerless, without strength, without energy, transformed by destiny, confluence, and nature, experiencing pleasure and pain in the six classes of birth’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view arises: ‘There is no cause, no condition… experiencing pleasure and pain in the six classes of birth.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view arises: ‘There is no cause, no condition… experiencing pleasure and pain in the six classes of birth.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘natthi hetu, natthi paccayo…pe… sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘natthi hetu, natthi paccayo…pe… sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api [T 3.0259] nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘natthi hetu natthi paccayo…pe… sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir… subject to change. Without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘There is no cause, no condition… they experience pleasure and pain’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir… Without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘There is no cause, no condition… they experience pleasure and pain’?” “No, venerable sir.” “And whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and explored by the mind—is that also permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir… Without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘There is no cause, no condition… they experience pleasure and pain’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Yato [M 2.0173] kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti [P 3.0211] …pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple has abandoned doubt in these matters, and doubt about suffering has been abandoned… and doubt about the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been abandoned—this, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not liable to fall, fixed in destiny, bound for full enlightenment.” The seventh.

8. Mahādiṭṭhisuttaṃ

8. The Great View Discourse

213. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘sattime kāyā akaṭā, akaṭavidhā, animmitā, animmātā, vañjhā, kūṭaṭṭhā, esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā; te na iñjanti, na vipariṇamanti na vipariṇāmenti (pī. ka.), na aññamaññaṃ [V 2.0198] byābādhenti; nālaṃ aññamaññassa sukhāya vā dukkhāya vā sukhadukkhāya vā. Katame satta? Pathavīkāyo, āpokāyo, tejokāyo, vāyokāyo, sukhe, dukkhe, jīve sattame. Ime satta jīve. sattime (bahūsu) kāyā akaṭā, akaṭavidhā, animmitā, animmātā, vañjhā, kūṭaṭṭhā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā; te na iñjanti, na vipariṇamanti, na aññamaññaṃ byābādhenti; nālaṃ aññamaññassa sukhāya vā dukkhāya vā sukhadukkhāya vā. Yopi tiṇhena satthena sīsaṃ chindati, na sopi kañci na koci kañci (sī. syā. kaṃ.), na koci taṃ (pī. ka.) jīvitā voropeti; sattannaṃtveva kāyānamantarena satthaṃ vivaramanupavisati vivaramanupatati (katthaci) dīghamajjhimesupi. Cuddasa kho panimāni yonipamukhasatasahassāni saṭṭhi ca satāni cha ca satāni pañca ca kammuno satāni pañca ca kammāni, tīṇi ca kammāni[T 3.0260], kamme ca aḍḍhakamme ca dvaṭṭhipaṭipadā, dvaṭṭhantarakappā, chaḷābhijātiyo, aṭṭhapurisabhūmiyo, ekūnapaññāsa ājīvakasate, ekūnapaññāsa paribbājakasate, ekūnapaññāsa nāgavāsasate, vīse indriyasate, tiṃse nirayasate, chattiṃsarajodhātuyo, satta saññīgabbhā, satta asaññīgabbhā, satta nigaṇṭhigabbhā, satta devā[P 3.0212], satta mānusā, satta pesācā, satta sarā, satta pavuṭā sapuṭā (ka.), pavudhā (pī.), satta papātā, satta ca papātasatāni, satta supinā, satta supinasatāni, cullāsīti mahākappino mahākappuno (sī. pī.) satasahassāni, yāni bāle ca paṇḍite ca sandhāvitvā [M 2.0174] saṃsaritvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Tattha natthi imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā aparipakkaṃ vā kammaṃ paripācessāmi; paripakkaṃ vā kammaṃ phussa phussa byantīkarissāmīti hevaṃ natthi doṇamite sukhadukkhe pariyantakate saṃsāre, natthi hāyanavaḍḍhane, natthi ukkaṃsāvakaṃse. Seyyathāpi nāma suttaguḷe khitte nibbeṭhiyamānameva paleti; evameva bāle ca paṇḍite ca nibbeṭhiyamānā sukhadukkhaṃ palentī’”ti?

213. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view arise: ‘There are these seven bodies—unmade, unfashioned, uncreated, not caused to be created, barren, standing firm like a mountain peak, standing firm like a pillar. They do not move, do not change, do not harm one another, and are incapable of causing one another pleasure, or pain, or both pleasure and pain. Which seven? The earth-body, the water-body, the fire-body, the wind-body, pleasure, pain, and life as the seventh. These seven bodies are unmade, unfashioned, uncreated, not caused to be created, barren, standing firm like a mountain peak, standing firm like a pillar. They do not move, do not change, do not harm one another, and are incapable of causing one another pleasure, or pain, or both pleasure and pain. Even if one were to cut off someone’s head with a sharp sword, one would not be depriving anyone of life; the sword would merely pass through the space between these seven bodies. There are one million four hundred thousand principal origins of birth, and sixty-six hundred more; five hundred kammas, and five kammas, and three kammas, and a kamma, and a half-kamma; sixty-two paths, sixty-two intermediate aeons, six classes of birth, eight grounds for men, forty-nine hundred Ājīvakas, forty-nine hundred wanderers, forty-nine hundred Nāga abodes, two thousand faculties, three thousand hells, thirty-six dust-realms, seven conceptions with perception, seven conceptions without perception, seven joint-like conceptions, seven devas, seven humans, seven goblins, seven lakes, seven knots, seven precipices, and seven hundred precipices; seven great dreams and seven hundred dreams; eighty-four hundred thousand great aeons, through which fools and the wise alike, having run on and transmigrated, will make an end of suffering. Therein, there is no such thing as: ‘By this virtue, or observance, or austerity, or holy life, I will bring unripened kamma to maturity, or, having repeatedly experienced ripened kamma, I will make an end of it.’ There is no such thing. Pleasure and pain are measured out, the wandering-on has its limit fixed. There is no decrease or increase, no excelling or falling short. Just as a ball of string, when thrown, runs on unwinding; so too fools and the wise alike, unwinding, run on through pleasure and pain.’”

Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘sattime kāyā akaṭā, akaṭavidhā…pe… sukhadukkhaṃ palentī’ti. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ [T 3.0261] abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘sattime kāyā akaṭā, akaṭavidhā…pe… sukhadukkhaṃ palentī’”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… [V 2.0199] “yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘sattime kāyā akaṭā akaṭavidhā…pe… sukhadukkhaṃ palentī’”ti? “No [P 3.0213] hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘sattime kāyā akaṭā akaṭavidhā…pe… nibbeṭhiyamānā sukhadukkhaṃ palentī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Venerable sir, for us, the teachings are rooted in the Blessed One… ‘Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view arises: “These seven bodies are unmade, unfashioned… and so on… they run on through pleasure and pain.” When there is feeling… when there is perception… when there are formations… when there is consciousness, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view arises: “These seven bodies are unmade, unfashioned… and so on… they run on through pleasure and pain.”

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.”… “That which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—without clinging to it, would such a view arise: ‘These seven bodies are unmade, unfashioned… and so on… they run on through pleasure and pain’?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.”

“And that which is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought, and continuously reflected upon by the mind—is that too permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.”… “Without clinging to it, would such a view arise: ‘These seven bodies are unmade, unfashioned… and so on… unwinding, they run on through pleasure and pain’?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple’s doubt concerning these six grounds is abandoned, and his doubt concerning suffering is abandoned… and his doubt concerning the path of practice leading to the cessation of suffering is abandoned—this one, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, no longer bound for the nether world, fixed in destiny, with enlightenment as his destination.” The eighth.

9. Sassatadiṭṭhisuttaṃ

9. Discourse on the Eternalist View

214. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘sassato loko’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā [T 3.0262] no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘sassato loko’ti. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe [M 2.0175] sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘sassato loko’”ti.

214. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view as this arise: ‘The world is eternal’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view as this arises: ‘The world is eternal.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view as this arises: ‘The world is eternal.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘sassato loko’ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā [V 2.0200]… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘sassato loko’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ [P 3.0214] vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘sassato loko’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “It is subject to change. Without clinging to it, could such a view as this arise: ‘The world is eternal’?” “Surely not, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to it, could such a view as this arise: ‘The world is eternal’?” “Surely not, venerable sir.” “And that which is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought, and mentally pondered—is that too permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “But, without clinging to what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, could such a view as this arise: ‘The world is eternal’?” “Surely not, venerable sir.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Navamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple’s doubt concerning these instances is abandoned, his doubt concerning suffering is also abandoned… his doubt concerning the path leading to the cessation of suffering is also abandoned. This, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not subject to the state of downfall, assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Ninth.

10. Asassatadiṭṭhisuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the View that the World is Non-eternal

215. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0263]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘asassato loko’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati…pe… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – asassato lokoti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘asassato loko’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

215. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by insisting on what, does such a view arise: ‘The world is non-eternal’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” … “Bhikkhus, when form exists… is consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to that, could such a view arise: ‘The world is non-eternal’?” “Surely not, venerable sir.” “And that which is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought, and mentally pondered—is that also permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Without clinging to that, could such a view arise: ‘The world is non-eternal’?” “Surely not, venerable sir.”

“Yato [V 2.0201] kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple’s doubt concerning these instances is abandoned, his doubt concerning suffering is also abandoned… his doubt concerning the path leading to the cessation of suffering is also abandoned. This, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not subject to the state of downfall, assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Tenth.

11. Antavāsuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on the Finite

216. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0176]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘antavā loko’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

216. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by insisting on what, does such a view arise: ‘The world is finite’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One... ...assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Eleventh.

12. Anantavāsuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on the Infinite

217. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0264][P 3.0215]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘anantavā loko’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… [V 2.0202] niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

217. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by insisting on what, does such a view arise: ‘The world is infinite’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One... ...assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Twelfth.

13. Taṃjīvaṃtaṃsarīraṃsuttaṃ

13. The Discourse on ‘The Life-Principle is the Body’

218. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’”nti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Terasamaṃ.

218. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by insisting on what, does such a view arise: ‘The life-principle is the body’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One... ...assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Thirteenth.

14. Aññaṃjīvaṃaññaṃsarīraṃsuttaṃ

14. The Discourse on ‘The Life-Principle Is One Thing, the Body Another’

219. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’”nti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… [V 2.0203] niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Cuddasamaṃ.

219. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by insisting on what, does such a view arise: ‘The life-principle is one thing, the body is another’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One... ...assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Fourteenth.

15. Hotitathāgatosuttaṃ

15. The Discourse on ‘A Tathāgata Exists After Death’

220. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Pannarasamaṃ.

220. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by insisting on what, does such a view arise: ‘A Tathāgata exists after death’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One... ...assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Fifteenth.

16. Nahotitathāgatosuttaṃ

16. The Discourse on ‘A Tathāgata Does Not Exist After Death’

221. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa [V 2.0204] evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Soḷasamaṃ.

221. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by insisting on what, does such a view arise: ‘A Tathāgata does not exist after death’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One... ...assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Sixteenth.

17. Hoticanacahotitathāgatosuttaṃ

17. The Discourse on ‘A Tathāgata Both Exists and Does Not Exist After Death’

222. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0177]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya[P 3.0216], kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Sattarasamaṃ.

222. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by insisting on what, does such a view arise: ‘A Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One... ...assured, and bound for enlightenment.” The Seventeenth.

18. Nevahotinanahotitathāgatosuttaṃ

18. The Discourse on ‘A Tathāgata Neither Exists Nor Does Not Exist After Death’

223. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0205]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe [T 3.0265] kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti…pe….

223. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by insisting on what, does such a view arise: ‘A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One... “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by insisting on form, such a view arises: ‘A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’...”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yampidaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … That which is subject to change—without clinging to it, would such a view arise: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death’?” “No, venerable sir.” “And whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and examined by the mind—is that too permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “That which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—without clinging to it, would such a view arise: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhasamudayepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhanirodhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti. Aṭṭhārasamaṃ[P 3.0217].

“When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple’s doubt in these matters has been abandoned, and his doubt about suffering, about the origin of suffering, about the cessation of suffering, and about the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been abandoned—this, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling away, assured, and destined for enlightenment.” The Eighteenth.

Sotāpattivaggo.

The Chapter on Stream-Entry.

Aṭṭhārasaveyyākaraṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighteen Explanations are completed.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Vātaṃ [V 2.0206][M 2.0178] etaṃ mama, so attā no ca me siyā;

Natthi karoto hetu ca, mahādiṭṭhena aṭṭhamaṃ.

Vāta, Etaṃ Mama, So Attā, and No Ca Me Siyā; Natthi, Karoto, and Hetu; and with Mahādiṭṭhi as the eighth.

Sassato loko ca, asassato ca antavā ca;

Anantavā ca taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti;

Aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti ca.

The world is eternal, and not eternal; finite, and infinite; the soul is the same as the body; and the soul is one thing, the body another.

Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti;

Na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti;

Neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti.

A being exists after death; a being does not exist after death; a being neither exists nor does not exist after death.

2. Dutiyagamanavaggo

2. The Second Chapter on the Course

1. Vātasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Wind

224. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0266]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā, esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’ti. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati…pe… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti.

224. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view arise: ‘The winds do not blow, the rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the moon and sun do not rise or set, but stand fixed like a boundary pillar’?” “Venerable sir, for us, the teachings have the Blessed One as their root…” “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view arises: ‘The winds do not blow… but stand fixed like a boundary pillar.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view arises: ‘The winds do not blow… but stand fixed like a boundary pillar.’”

“Taṃ [V 2.0207] kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ[P 3.0218], bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe sati, dukkhaṃ upādāya, dukkhaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti? “No [T 3.0267] hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe sati, dukkhaṃ upādāya, dukkhaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā, esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … That which is subject to change—without clinging to it, would such a view arise: ‘The winds do not blow… but stand fixed like a boundary pillar’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, when suffering exists, by clinging to suffering, by adhering to suffering, such a view arises: ‘The winds do not blow… but stand fixed like a boundary pillar.’ “Is feeling… perception… formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … That which is subject to change—without clinging to it, would such a view arise: ‘The winds do not blow… but stand fixed like a boundary pillar’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, when suffering exists, by clinging to suffering, by adhering to suffering, such a view arises: ‘The winds do not blow, the rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the moon and sun do not rise or set, but stand fixed like a boundary pillar.’” First.

225-240. (Purimavagge viya aṭṭhārasa veyyākaraṇāni vitthāretabbānīti[M 2.0179].) Sattarasamaṃ.

(The eighteen explanations should be elaborated as in the previous chapter.) The Seventeenth.

18. Nevahotinanahotisuttaṃ

18. The Discourse on Neither Exists Nor Does Not Exist

241. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti. Vedanāya sati… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

241. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view arise: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” “Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view arises: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view arises: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

“Taṃ [V 2.0208] kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe sati, dukkhaṃ upādāya, dukkhaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Vedanā… saññā [T 3.0268]… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe sati, dukkhaṃ upādāya dukkhaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. Aṭṭhārasamaṃ.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” …pe… “It is of a nature to change; without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, when suffering exists, by clinging to suffering, by being intent on suffering, such a view arises: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” …pe… “It is of a nature to change; without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, when suffering exists, by clinging to suffering, by being intent on suffering, such a view arises: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’” The Eighteenth.

19. Rūpīattāsuttaṃ

19. The Sutta on the Self with Form

242. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya[P 3.0219], kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘rūpī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘rūpī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’ti. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘rūpī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

242. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what is present, by clinging to what, by being intent on what, does such a view arise: ‘The self has form and is healthy after death’?” “Venerable sir, for us, the teachings have the Blessed One as their root…pe… “Bhikkhus, when form is present, by clinging to form, by being intent on form, such a view arises: ‘The self has form and is healthy after death.’ When feeling is present…pe… when perception is present… when volitional formations are present… when consciousness is present, by clinging to consciousness, by being intent on consciousness, such a view arises: ‘The self has form and is healthy after death.’”

“Taṃ [M 2.0180] kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘rūpī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe sati, dukkhaṃ upādāya, dukkhaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘rūpī [V 2.0209] attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “Vedanā…pe… [T 3.0269] “no hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe sati, dukkhaṃ upādāya, dukkhaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘rūpī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. Ekūnavīsatimaṃ.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” …pe… “It is subject to change; without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘The self has form and is healthy after death’?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, when suffering is present, by clinging to suffering, by being intent on suffering, such a view arises: ‘The self has form and is healthy after death.’ Feeling…pe… “Certainly not, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, when suffering is present, by clinging to suffering, by being intent on suffering, such a view arises: ‘The self has form and is healthy after death.’” The Nineteenth.

20. Arūpīattāsuttaṃ

20. The Sutta on the Formless Self

243. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘arūpī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? (Peyyālo) vīsatimaṃ.

243. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what is present, by clinging to what, by being intent on what, does such a view arise: ‘The self is formless and is healthy after death’?” (Repetition) The Twentieth.

21. Rūpīcaarūpīcaattāsuttaṃ

21. The Sutta on the Self That Is Both with Form and Formless

244. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpī ca arūpī ca attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā”ti…pe…. Ekavīsatimaṃ.

244. At Sāvatthī. … “The self is both with form and formless and is healthy after death”…pe…. The Twenty-first.

22. Nevarūpīnārūpīattāsuttaṃ

22. The Sutta on the Self That Is Neither with Form Nor Formless

245. “Neva rūpī nārūpī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā”ti…pe…. Bāvīsatimaṃ.

245. … “The self is neither with form nor formless and is healthy after death”…pe…. The Twenty-second.

23. Ekantasukhīsuttaṃ

23. The Sutta on the Exclusively Happy Self

246. “Ekantasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā”ti…pe…. Tevīsatimaṃ.

246. … “The self is exclusively happy and is healthy after death”…pe…. The Twenty-third.

24. Ekantadukkhīsuttaṃ

24. The Sutta on the Exclusively Suffering Self

247. “Ekantadukkhī [V 2.0210][P 3.0220] attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā”ti…pe…. Catuvīsatimaṃ.

247. … “The self is exclusively suffering and is healthy after death”…pe…. The Twenty-fourth.

25. Sukhadukkhīsuttaṃ

25. The Sutta on the Self with Pleasure and Pain

248. “Sukhadukkhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā”ti…pe…. Pañcavīsatimaṃ.

248. … “The self has pleasure and pain and is healthy after death”…pe…. The Twenty-fifth.

26. Adukkhamasukhīsuttaṃ

26. The Sutta on the Self with Neither-Pain-Nor-Pleasure

249. “Adukkhamasukhī [M 2.0181] attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’ti. Vedanāya sati… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā [T 3.0270] hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

249. “Does such a view arise: ‘The self has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and is healthy after death’?” “Venerable sir, for us, the teachings have the Blessed One as their root…pe… “Bhikkhus, when form is present, by clinging to form, by being intent on form, such a view arises: ‘The self has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and is healthy after death.’ When feeling is present… when perception is present… when volitional formations are present… when consciousness is present, by clinging to consciousness, by being intent on consciousness, such a view arises: ‘The self has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and is healthy after death.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe sati, dukkhaṃ upādāya, dukkhaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave[V 2.0211], dukkhe sati, dukkhaṃ upādāya, dukkhaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. Chabbīsatimaṃ.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” …pe… “It is of a nature to change. Without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘The self has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and is healthy after death’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, when suffering is present, by clinging to suffering, by being intent on suffering, such a view arises: ‘The self has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and is healthy after death.’ Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” …pe… “It is of a nature to change. Without clinging to it, could such a view arise: ‘The self has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and is healthy after death’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, when suffering is present, by clinging to suffering, by being intent on suffering, such a view arises: ‘The self has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and is healthy after death.’” The Twenty-sixth.

Dutiyapeyyālo.

The Second Repetition Series is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Vātaṃ etaṃ mama so, attā no ca me siyā;

Natthi karoto hetu ca, mahādiṭṭhena aṭṭhamaṃ.

Wind, This is Mine, That Self, and It Should Not Be Mine; There Is Not, One Who Acts, Cause, and with Great View as the eighth.

Sassato asassato [P 3.0221] ceva, antānantavā ca vuccati;

Taṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ jīvañca, tathāgatena cattāro.

Eternal and Not Eternal are spoken of, and Finite and Infinite; That Which is the Soul, Another Soul, and four concerning the Tathāgata.

Rūpī attā hoti, arūpī ca attā hoti;

Rūpī ca arūpī ca attā hoti;

Neva rūpī nārūpī attā hoti, ekantasukhī attā hoti.

The self has form, and the self is formless; The self is both with form and formless; The self is neither with form nor formless, the self is exclusively happy.

Ekantadukkhī attā hoti, sukhadukkhī attā hoti;

Adukkhamasukhī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇāti;

Ime chabbīsati suttā, dutiyavārena desitā.

The sutta ‘The Self is Exclusively Suffering,’ the sutta ‘The Self is Happy and Suffering,’ the sutta ‘The Self is Neither-Suffering-Nor-Happy,’ and the sutta ‘Healthy After Death.’ These twenty-six suttas were taught in the second section.

3. Tatiyagamanavaggo

3. The Third Gamana Chapter

1. Navātasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Winds Not Blowing

250. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0271][M 2.0182]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo [V 2.0212] vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe….

250. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view arise: ‘Winds do not blow, rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the moon and sun do not rise or set, but stand fixed like a pillar’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings have the Blessed One as their root…”

“Rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – na vātā vāyanti…pe… vedanāya sati… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view arises: ‘Winds do not blow…’ When feeling exists… When perception exists… When formations exist… When consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view arises: ‘Winds do not blow… but stand fixed like a pillar.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. Tasmiṃ sati, tadupādāya, evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ[T 3.0272], bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. Tasmiṃ sati, tadupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” …pe… “subject to change, would such a view arise without clinging to it: ‘Winds do not blow…pe… stand fixed like a pillar’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, what is impermanent is suffering. When that suffering exists, by clinging to it, such a view arises: ‘Winds do not blow, the rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the moon and sun do not rise or set, but stand fixed like a pillar.’ “Is feeling… perception… formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” …pe… “subject to change, would such a view arise without clinging to it: ‘Winds do not blow…pe… stand fixed like a pillar’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, what is impermanent is suffering. When that suffering exists, by clinging to it, such a view arises: ‘Winds do not blow…pe… stand fixed like a pillar.’”

251-274. (Dutiyavagge viya catuvīsati suttāni pūretabbāni.) Pañcavīsatimaṃ.

251-274. (Twenty-four suttas are to be completed as in the second section.) The twenty-fifth.

26. Adukkhamasukhīsuttaṃ

26. The Discourse on Neither-Painful-Nor-Pleasant

275. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0213][P 3.0222]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe….

275. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view arise: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant, permanent after death’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings have the Blessed One as their root…pe….”

“Rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’ti. Vedanāya sati [M 2.0183] …pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view arises: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant, permanent after death.’ When feeling exists…pe… when perception exists… when formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view arises: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant, permanent after death.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. Tasmiṃ sati, tadupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Vedanā…pe… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ[T 3.0273], api nu taṃ anupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. Tasmiṃ sati, tadupādāya evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. Chabbīsatimaṃ.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … subject to change, would such a view arise without clinging to it: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant and is healthy after death’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, what is impermanent is suffering. When that exists, by clinging to it, such a view arises: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant and is healthy after death.’ “Is feeling… perception… formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … subject to change, would such a view arise without clinging to it: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant and is healthy after death’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Thus, bhikkhus, what is impermanent is suffering. When that exists, by clinging to it, such a view arises: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant and is healthy after death.’” The twenty-sixth.

Tatiyapeyyālo.

The Third Repetition Series.

4. Catutthagamanavaggo

4. The Fourth Gamana Chapter

1. Navātasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Winds Not Blowing

276. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0274][V 2.0214]. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti[P 3.0223], na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe….

276. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view arise: ‘Winds do not blow, rivers do not flow, pregnant women do not give birth, the moon and sun do not rise or set but stand firm like a pillar’?” “Venerable sir, for us the teachings have the Blessed One as their root…”

“Rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’ti. Vedanāya sati…pe… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘na vātā vāyanti…pe… esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā [M 2.0184]… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Indeed, bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view arises: ‘The winds do not blow… fixed like a pillar.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view arises: ‘The winds do not blow… fixed like a pillar.’ What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “But what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “But what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Tasmātiha[T 3.0275], bhikkhave, yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā, oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama[V 2.0215], nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ.

“Therefore, here, bhikkhus, whatever form—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all form should be seen with right wisdom as it truly is thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all consciousness should be seen with right wisdom as it truly is thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Seeing thus… he understands: ‘There is nothing further for this state of being.’” First.

277-300. (Dutiyavagge viya catuvīsati suttāni pūretabbāni.) Pañcavīsatimaṃ.

(Twenty-four discourses are to be completed as in the second section.) The twenty-fifth.

26. Adukkhamasukhīsuttaṃ

26. The Discourse on Neither-Painful-Nor-Pleasant

301. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Kismiṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṃ upādāya, kiṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe….

301. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, by adhering to what, does such a view arise: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant, permanent after death’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…”

“Rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṃ upādāya, rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’ti. Vedanāya sati… saññāya sati… saṅkhāresu sati… viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṃ upādāya, viññāṇaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati – ‘adukkhamasukhī attā hoti, arogo paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, when form exists, by clinging to form, by adhering to form, such a view arises: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant, permanent after death.’ When feeling exists… when perception exists… when volitional formations exist… when consciousness exists, by clinging to consciousness, by adhering to consciousness, such a view arises: ‘The self is neither painful nor pleasant, permanent after death.’”

“Taṃ [P 3.0224] kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”[V 2.0216]. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante [T 3.0276]”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ [M 2.0185] vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “But what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “But what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā, oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’”ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ.

“Therefore, here, bhikkhus, whatever form—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all form should be seen with right wisdom as it truly is thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all consciousness should be seen with right wisdom as it truly is thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ[T 3.0277], nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Chabbīsatimaṃ.

“Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the well-instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with volitional formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’” The twenty-sixth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Purimagamane aṭṭhārasa veyyākaraṇā;

Dutiyagamane chabbīsaṃ vitthāretabbāni.

In the first section, eighteen explanations; in the second section, twenty-six are to be elaborated.

Tatiyagamane [V 2.0217] chabbīsaṃ vitthāretabbāni;

Catutthagamane chabbīsaṃ vitthāretabbāni.

In the third section, twenty-six are to be elaborated; in the fourth section, twenty-six are to be elaborated.

Diṭṭhisaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Views is complete.

4. Okkantasaṃyuttaṃ

4. The Connected Discourses on Entry

1. Cakkhusuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Eye

302. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0278][V 2.0218][P 3.0225][M 2.0186]. “Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, aniccaṃ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi; sotaṃ aniccaṃ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi; ghānaṃ aniccaṃ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi; jivhā aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī vipariṇāminī aññathābhāvinī (?); kāyo anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī; mano anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ saddahati adhimuccati – ayaṃ vuccati saddhānusārī, okkanto sammattaniyāmaṃ, sappurisabhūmiṃ okkanto, vītivatto puthujjanabhūmiṃ; abhabbo taṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ, yaṃ kammaṃ katvā nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā pettivisayaṃ vā upapajjeyya; abhabbo ca abhabbova (sī. syā. kaṃ.) tāva kālaṃ kātuṃ yāva na sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikaroti”.

302. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, the eye is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. The ear is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. The nose is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. The tongue is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. The body is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. The mind is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. Bhikkhus, whoever thus has faith in and is resolved upon these phenomena is called a faith-follower: one who has entered the fixed course of rightness, entered the plane of superior persons, and transcended the plane of ordinary people. Such a one is incapable of performing any action by which they might be reborn in hell, in the animal realm, or in the sphere of ghosts; and is incapable of dying before realizing the fruit of stream-entry."

“Yassa kho, bhikkhave, ime dhammā evaṃ paññāya mattaso nijjhānaṃ khamanti, ayaṃ vuccati – ‘dhammānusārī, okkanto sammattaniyāmaṃ, sappurisabhūmiṃ okkanto, vītivatto puthujjanabhūmiṃ; abhabbo taṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ, yaṃ kammaṃ katvā nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā pettivisayaṃ vā upapajjeyya; abhabbo ca tāva kālaṃ kātuṃ yāva na sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikaroti’. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ pajānāti evaṃ passati, ayaṃ vuccati – ‘sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano’”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

"Bhikkhus, one for whom these phenomena are, to a measure, approved of upon reflection with wisdom, is called a Dhamma-follower: one who has entered the fixed course of rightness, entered the plane of superior persons, and transcended the plane of ordinary people. Such a one is incapable of performing any action by which they might be reborn in hell, in the animal realm, or in the sphere of ghosts; and is incapable of dying before realizing the fruit of stream-entry. Bhikkhus, one who thus understands and sees these phenomena is called a stream-enterer: one not subject to falling into states of deprivation, who is assured and destined for enlightenment." First.

2. Rūpasuttaṃ

2. The Sutta on Forms

303. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpā, bhikkhave, aniccā vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino; saddā aniccā vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino; gandhā aniccā [T 3.0279] vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino[V 2.0219]; rasā aniccā vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino; phoṭṭhabbā aniccā vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino; dhammā aniccā vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino. Yo[P 3.0226], bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ saddahati adhimuccati, ayaṃ vuccati saddhānusārī, okkanto sammattaniyāmaṃ, sappurisabhūmiṃ okkanto, vītivatto puthujjanabhūmiṃ; abhabbo taṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ, yaṃ kammaṃ katvā nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā pettivisayaṃ [M 2.0187] vā upapajjeyya; abhabbo ca tāva kālaṃ kātuṃ yāva na sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikaroti”.

303. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, forms are impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration; sounds are impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration; odors are impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration; tastes are impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration; tangible objects are impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration; mental phenomena are impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. Bhikkhus, whoever thus has faith in and is resolved upon these phenomena is called a faith-follower: one who has entered the fixed course of rightness, entered the plane of superior persons, and transcended the plane of ordinary people. That person is incapable of performing any action by which they might be reborn in hell, in the animal realm, or in the sphere of ghosts; and is incapable of passing away before realizing the fruit of stream-entry."

“Yassa kho, bhikkhave, ime dhammā evaṃ paññāya mattaso nijjhānaṃ khamanti, ayaṃ vuccati – ‘dhammānusārī, okkanto sammattaniyāmaṃ, sappurisabhūmiṃ okkanto, vītivatto puthujjanabhūmiṃ; abhabbo taṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ, yaṃ kammaṃ katvā nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā pettivisayaṃ vā upapajjeyya; abhabbo ca tāva kālaṃ kātuṃ yāva na sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikaroti’. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ pajānāti evaṃ passati, ayaṃ vuccati – ‘sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano’”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

"Bhikkhus, one for whom these phenomena are, to a measure, approved of upon reflection with wisdom, is called a Dhamma-follower: one who has entered the fixed course of rightness, entered the plane of superior persons, and transcended the plane of ordinary people. That person is incapable of performing any action by which they might be reborn in hell, in the animal realm, or in the sphere of ghosts; and is incapable of passing away before realizing the fruit of stream-entry. Bhikkhus, one who thus knows and sees these phenomena is called a stream-enterer: one not subject to falling into states of deprivation, who is assured and destined for enlightenment." Second.

3. Viññāṇasuttaṃ

3. The Sutta on Consciousness

304. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, aniccaṃ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi; sotaviññāṇaṃ… ghānaviññāṇaṃ… jivhāviññāṇaṃ… kāyaviññāṇaṃ… manoviññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi. Yo bhikkhave…pe… sambodhiparāyano”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

304. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, eye-consciousness is impermanent, subject to change, subject to becoming otherwise; ear-consciousness… nose-consciousness… tongue-consciousness… body-consciousness… mind-consciousness is impermanent, subject to change, subject to becoming otherwise. Bhikkhus, one who… destined for enlightenment." Third.

4. Samphassasuttaṃ

4. The Sutta on Contact

305. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cakkhusamphasso, bhikkhave, anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī[T 3.0280]; sotasamphasso… ghānasamphasso… jivhāsamphasso… kāyasamphasso… manosamphasso anicco vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ saddahati adhimuccati, ayaṃ vuccati ‘saddhānusārī…pe… sambodhiparāyano’”ti. Catutthaṃ.

305. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, eye-contact is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration; ear-contact… nose-contact… tongue-contact… body-contact… mind-contact is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. Bhikkhus, whoever thus has faith in and is resolved upon these phenomena is called a 'faith-follower'… destined for enlightenment." Fourth.

5. Samphassajāsuttaṃ

5. The Sutta on What is Born of Contact

306. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0220]. “Cakkhusamphassajā, bhikkhave, vedanā aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī; sotasamphassajā vedanā…pe… ghānasamphassajā vedanā…pe… jivhāsamphassajā vedanā…pe… kāyasamphassajā vedanā…pe… manosamphassajā vedanā aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ saddahati adhimuccati, ayaṃ vuccati ‘saddhānusārī…pe… sambodhiparāyano’”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

306. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, feeling born of eye-contact is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration; feeling born of ear-contact… feeling born of nose-contact… feeling born of tongue-contact… feeling born of body-contact… feeling born of mind-contact is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. Bhikkhus, whoever thus has faith in and is resolved upon these phenomena is called a 'faith-follower'… destined for enlightenment." Fifth.

6. Rūpasaññāsuttaṃ

6. The Sutta on Perception of Forms

307. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0188][P 3.0227]. “Rūpasaññā, bhikkhave, aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī; saddasaññā… gandhasaññā… rasasaññā… phoṭṭhabbasaññā… dhammasaññā aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ saddahati adhimuccati, ayaṃ vuccati ‘saddhānusārī…pe… sambodhiparāyano’”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

307. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, the perception of forms is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration; the perception of sounds… smells… tastes… tactile objects… mental phenomena is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. Bhikkhus, whoever thus has faith in and is resolved upon these phenomena is called a 'faith-follower'… destined for enlightenment." Sixth.

7. Rūpasañcetanāsuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on Intention Regarding Forms

308. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpasañcetanā, bhikkhave, aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī; saddasañcetanā… gandhasañcetanā… rasasañcetanā… phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā… dhammasañcetanā aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ saddahati adhimuccati, ayaṃ vuccati ‘saddhānusārī…pe… sambodhiparāyano’”ti. Sattamaṃ.

308. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, intention regarding forms is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration; intention regarding sounds… smells… tastes… tactile objects… mental phenomena is impermanent, subject to change, subject to alteration. Bhikkhus, whoever thus has faith in and is resolved upon these phenomena is called a 'faith-follower'… destined for enlightenment." Seventh.

8. Rūpataṇhāsuttaṃ

8. The Sutta on Craving for Forms

309. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0281]. “Rūpataṇhā, bhikkhave, aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī; saddataṇhā… gandhataṇhā… rasataṇhā… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā… dhammataṇhā aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī[V 2.0221]. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ saddahati adhimuccati, ayaṃ vuccati ‘saddhānusārī…pe… sambodhiparāyano’”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

309. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, craving for forms is impermanent, perishable, and subject to alteration; craving for sounds… smells… tastes… tactile objects… mental phenomena is impermanent, perishable, and subject to alteration. Bhikkhus, whoever has faith in and inclines the mind towards these phenomena in this way is called a faith-follower… bound for enlightenment.' Eighth.

9. Pathavīdhātusuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Earth Element

310. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Pathavīdhātu, bhikkhave, aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī; āpodhātu… tejodhātu… vāyodhātu… ākāsadhātu… viññāṇadhātu aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ saddahati adhimuccati, ayaṃ vuccati ‘saddhānusārī…pe… sambodhiparāyano’”ti. Navamaṃ.

310. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, the earth element is impermanent, perishable, and subject to alteration; the water element… the fire element… the air element… the space element… the consciousness element is impermanent, perishable, and subject to alteration. Bhikkhus, whoever has faith in and inclines the mind towards these phenomena in this way is called a faith-follower… bound for enlightenment.' Ninth.

10. Khandhasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Aggregates

311. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, aniccaṃ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi; vedanā aniccā vipariṇāmī aññathābhāvī; saññā… saṅkhārā aniccā vipariṇāmino aññathābhāvino; viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ vipariṇāmi aññathābhāvi[M 2.0189]. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ saddahati adhimuccati, ayaṃ vuccati saddhānusārī, okkanto sammattaniyāmaṃ[P 3.0228], sappurisabhūmiṃ [T 3.0282] okkanto, vītivatto puthujjanabhūmiṃ; abhabbo taṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ, yaṃ kammaṃ katvā nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā pettivisayaṃ vā upapajjeyya; abhabbo ca tāva kālaṃ kātuṃ yāva na sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikaroti”.

311. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, form is impermanent, perishable, and subject to alteration; feeling is impermanent, perishable, and subject to alteration; perception… volitional formations are impermanent, perishable, and subject to alteration; consciousness is impermanent, perishable, and subject to alteration. Bhikkhus, whoever has faith in and inclines the mind towards these phenomena in this way is called a faith-follower, one who has entered the fixed course of rightness, has entered the plane of true persons, and has transcended the plane of ordinary people. He is incapable of doing any deed by which he might be reborn in hell, in the animal realm, or in the sphere of afflicted spirits; and is incapable of dying before he has realized the fruit of stream-entry.'

“Yassa kho, bhikkhave, ime dhammā evaṃ paññāya mattaso nijjhānaṃ khamanti, ayaṃ vuccati – ‘dhammānusārī, okkanto sammattaniyāmaṃ, sappurisabhūmiṃ okkanto, vītivatto puthujjanabhūmiṃ; abhabbo taṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ, yaṃ kammaṃ katvā nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā pettivisayaṃ vā upapajjeyya; abhabbo ca tāva kālaṃ kātuṃ yāva na sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikaroti’. Yo, bhikkhave, ime dhamme evaṃ pajānāti evaṃ passati, ayaṃ vuccati – ‘sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano’”ti. Dasamaṃ.

'Indeed, bhikkhus, for whatever person these phenomena are amenable to reflection to a certain measure through wisdom, this person is called a Dhamma-follower, one who has entered the fixed course of rightness, one who has entered the plane of a superior person, one who has transcended the plane of an ordinary person. He is incapable of doing that action by which, having done it, he might arise in hell, or in the animal realm, or in the sphere of petas; and he is incapable of dying so long as he has not realized the fruit of stream-entry. Bhikkhus, whoever knows and sees these phenomena thus, this person is called a stream-enterer, one whose nature is not to fall, who is fixed, with enlightenment as his destination.' Tenth.

Okkantasaṃyuttaṃ okkantikasaṃyuttaṃ (pī. ka.) samattaṃ.

The Okkanta Saṃyutta is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that:

Cakkhu [V 2.0222] rūpañca viññāṇaṃ, phasso ca vedanāya ca;

Saññā ca cetanā taṇhā, dhātu khandhena te dasāti.

Eye, Form, and Consciousness, Contact and Feeling; Perception, Intention, Craving, Elements, and Aggregates—these are the ten.

5. Uppādasaṃyuttaṃ

5. The Connected Discourses on Arising

1. Cakkhusuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Eye

312. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0283][V 2.0223][M 2.0190]. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, cakkhussa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo sotassa uppādo ṭhiti…pe… yo ghānassa uppādo ṭhiti… yo jivhāya uppādo ṭhiti… yo kāyassa uppādo ṭhiti… yo manassa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso [P 3.0229] uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo ca, bhikkhave, cakkhussa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo. Yo sotassa nirodho…pe… yo ghānassa nirodho… yo jivhāya nirodho… yo kāyassa nirodho… yo manassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

312. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, persistence, new production, and manifestation of the eye, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. Whatever is the arising, persistence... of the ear... of the nose... of the tongue... of the body... Whatever is the arising, persistence, new production, and manifestation of the mind, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. And, bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation, appeasement, and disappearance of the eye, that is the cessation of suffering, the appeasement of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death. Whatever is the cessation... of the ear... of the nose... of the tongue... of the body... Whatever is the cessation, appeasement, and disappearance of the mind, that is the cessation of suffering, the appeasement of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death.' First.

2. Rūpasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Forms

313. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, rūpānaṃ uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo saddānaṃ… yo gandhānaṃ… yo rasānaṃ… yo phoṭṭhabbānaṃ… yo dhammānaṃ uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo [T 3.0284] ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpānaṃ nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo. Yo saddānaṃ… yo gandhānaṃ… yo rasānaṃ… yo phoṭṭhabbānaṃ… yo dhammānaṃ nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

313. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, persistence, new production, and manifestation of forms is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. Of sounds… of odors… of tastes… of tangibles… Whatever is the arising, persistence, new production, and manifestation of mental phenomena is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. And, bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation, appeasement, and disappearance of forms is the cessation of suffering, the appeasement of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death. Of sounds… of odors… of tastes… of tangibles… Whatever is the cessation, appeasement, and disappearance of mental phenomena is the cessation of suffering, the appeasement of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death.' Second.

3. Viññāṇasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Consciousness

314. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0224][M 2.0191]. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññāṇassa uppādo ṭhiti…pe… jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo…pe… yo manoviññāṇassa uppādo ṭhiti…pe… jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññāṇassa nirodho…pe… jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo…pe… yo manoviññāṇassa nirodho…pe… jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

314. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, persistence... of eye-consciousness... is the manifestation of aging and death... Whatever is the arising, persistence... of mind-consciousness... is the manifestation of aging and death. And, bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation... of eye-consciousness... is the disappearance of aging and death... Whatever is the cessation... of mind-consciousness... is the disappearance of aging and death.' Third.

4. Samphassasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Contact

315. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0230]. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, cakkhusamphassassa uppādo ṭhiti…pe… jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo…pe… yo manosamphassassa uppādo ṭhiti…pe… jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, cakkhusamphassassa nirodho…pe… jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo…pe… yo manosamphassassa nirodho…pe… jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

315. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, persistence... of eye-contact... is the manifestation of aging and death... Whatever is the arising, persistence... of mind-contact... is the manifestation of aging and death. And, bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation... of eye-contact... is the disappearance of aging and death... Whatever is the cessation... of mind-contact... is the disappearance of aging and death.' Fourth.

5. Samphassajasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on What is Born from Contact

316. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, cakkhusamphassajāya vedanāya uppādo ṭhiti…pe… jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo…pe….

316. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, persistence… of feeling born of eye-contact… is the manifestation of aging and death… and so on….'

Yo manosamphassajāya vedanāya uppādo ṭhiti…pe… [T 3.0285] jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, cakkhusamphassajāya vedanāya nirodho [V 2.0225] vūpasamo…pe… jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo…pe… yo manosamphassajāya vedanāya nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

Whatever arising and persistence of feeling born of mind-contact… is the manifestation of aging and death. And whatever, Bhikkhus, is the cessation, the calming of feeling born of eye-contact… is the disappearance of aging and death… and whatever is the cessation, the calming, the disappearance of feeling born of mind-contact, this is the cessation of suffering, the calming of diseases, the disappearance of aging and death.” Fifth.

6. Saññāsuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Perception

317. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, rūpasaññāya uppādo ṭhiti…pe… jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo…pe… yo dhammasaññāya uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpasaññāya nirodho…pe… jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo…pe… yo dhammasaññāya nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

317. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, the persistence of perception of forms… is the manifestation of aging and death… whatever is the arising, persistence, new arising, and manifestation of perception of mental objects, this is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, the manifestation of aging and death. And, Bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation of perception of forms… is the disappearance of aging and death… whatever is the cessation, the calming, the disappearance of perception of mental objects, this is the cessation of suffering, the calming of diseases, the disappearance of aging and death.” Sixth.

7. Sañcetanāsuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Volition

318. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0192]. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, rūpasañcetanāya uppādo ṭhiti…pe… jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo…pe… yo dhammasañcetanāya uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpasañcetanāya nirodho…pe… jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo…pe… yo dhammasañcetanāya nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

318. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, the persistence of volition regarding forms… is the manifestation of aging and death… whatever is the arising, persistence, new arising, and manifestation of volition regarding mental objects, this is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, the manifestation of aging and death. And, Bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation of volition regarding forms… is the disappearance of aging and death… whatever is the cessation, the calming, the disappearance of volition regarding mental objects, this is the cessation of suffering, the calming of diseases, the disappearance of aging and death.” Seventh.

8. Taṇhāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Craving

319. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0286]. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, rūpataṇhāya uppādo ṭhiti…pe… jarāmaraṇassa [V 2.0226] pātubhāvo…pe… yo dhammataṇhāya uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo [P 3.0231] ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpataṇhāya nirodho…pe… jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo…pe… yo dhammataṇhāya nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

319. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, the arising and persistence of craving for forms... is the manifestation of aging and death... the arising, persistence, new arising, and manifestation of craving for mental objects—this is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, the manifestation of aging and death. And, Bhikkhus, the cessation of craving for forms... is the disappearance of aging and death... the cessation, calming, and disappearance of craving for mental objects—this is the cessation of suffering, the calming of diseases, the disappearance of aging and death.” Eighth.

9. Dhātusuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Elements

320. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuyā uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo…pe… jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo; yo āpodhātuyā… yo tejodhātuyā… yo vāyodhātuyā… yo ākāsadhātuyā… yo viññāṇadhātuyā uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo.
