Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuyā nirodho…pe… jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo; yo āpodhātuyā nirodho… yo tejodhātuyā nirodho… yo vāyodhātuyā nirodho… yo ākāsadhātuyā nirodho… yo viññāṇadhātuyā nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Navamaṃ.

320. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, the arising, persistence, new arising, and manifestation of the earth element... is the manifestation of aging and death. The arising, persistence, new arising, and manifestation of the water element... of the fire element... of the air element... of the space element... of the consciousness element—this is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, the manifestation of aging and death. And, Bhikkhus, the cessation of the earth element... is the disappearance of aging and death. The cessation of the water element... the cessation of the fire element... the cessation of the air element... the cessation of the space element... and whatever is the cessation, calming, and disappearance of the consciousness element—this is the cessation of suffering, the calming of diseases, the disappearance of aging and death.” Ninth.

10. Khandhasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Aggregates

321. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0287][M 2.0193]. “Yo kho, bhikkhave, rūpassa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo vedanāya… yo saññāya… yo saṅkhārānaṃ… yo viññāṇassa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo. Yo vedanāya… yo saññāya… yo saṅkhārānaṃ… yo viññāṇassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

321. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, persistence, new arising, and manifestation of form, this is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. Whatever is the arising, persistence, new arising, and manifestation of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness, this is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. And, Bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation, calming, and disappearance of form, this is the cessation of suffering, the calming of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death. Whatever is the cessation, calming, and disappearance of feeling… of perception… of formations… of consciousness, this is the cessation of suffering, the calming of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death.” Tenth.

Uppādasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Arising is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Cakkhu [V 2.0227] rūpañca viññāṇaṃ, phasso ca vedanāya ca;

Saññā ca cetanā taṇhā, dhātu khandhena te dasāti.

Eye, Form, and Consciousness, Contact and also Feeling; Perception, Volition, Craving, Element, and with the Aggregate—these are the ten.

6. Kilesasaṃyuttaṃ

6. The Connected Discourses on Defilements

1. Cakkhusuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Eye

322. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0288][V 2.0228][P 3.0232][M 2.0194]. “Yo, bhikkhave, cakkhusmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo sotasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo ghānasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo jivhāya chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo kāyasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo manasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno imesu chasu ṭhānesu cetaso upakkileso pahīno hoti, nekkhammaninnañcassa cittaṃ hoti. Nekkhammaparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ kammaniyaṃ khāyati, abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

322. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever desire and lust there is for the eye, that is a defilement of the mind. Whatever desire and lust there is for the ear… for the nose… for the tongue… for the body… for the mind, that is a defilement of the mind. When, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has abandoned the defilement of the mind in these six instances, his mind inclines to renunciation. The mind, developed with renunciation, appears workable for realizing through higher knowledge those things that are to be realized.” First.

2. Rūpasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Form

323. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpesu chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo saddesu… yo gandhesu… yo rasesu… yo phoṭṭhabbesu… yo dhammesu chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno imesu chasu ṭhānesu cetaso upakkileso pahīno hoti, nekkhammaninnañcassa cittaṃ hoti. Nekkhammaparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ kammaniyaṃ khāyati, abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

323. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever desire and lust there is for forms, that is a defilement of the mind. Whatever desire and lust for sounds... for odors... for tastes... for tactile objects... whatever desire and lust there is for mental phenomena, that is a defilement of the mind. When, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has abandoned the defilement of the mind in these six instances, his mind inclines to renunciation. The mind, developed with renunciation, appears workable for realizing through higher knowledge those things that are to be realized.” Second.

3. Viññāṇasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Consciousness

324. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññāṇasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo sotaviññāṇasmiṃ… yo ghānaviññāṇasmiṃ… yo jivhāviññāṇasmiṃ… yo [V 2.0229] kāyaviññāṇasmiṃ… yo manoviññāṇasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yato kho[T 3.0289], bhikkhave, bhikkhuno imesu chasu ṭhānesu cetaso upakkileso pahīno hoti, nekkhammaninnañcassa cittaṃ [P 3.0233] hoti. Nekkhammaparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ kammaniyaṃ khāyati, abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

324. At Sāvatthī. 'Monks, whatever desire and lust there is for eye-consciousness, that is a defilement of the mind. Whatever desire and lust for ear-consciousness... for nose-consciousness... for tongue-consciousness... for body-consciousness... whatever desire and lust there is for mind-consciousness, that is a defilement of the mind. When, monks, a monk has abandoned the defilement of the mind in these six instances, his mind inclines to renunciation. A mind imbued with renunciation appears workable for realizing through direct knowledge those things that are to be realized.' The Third.

4. Samphassasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Contact

325. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0195]. “Yo, bhikkhave, cakkhusamphassasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo sotasamphassasmiṃ… yo ghānasamphassasmiṃ… yo jivhāsamphassasmiṃ… yo kāyasamphassasmiṃ… yo manosamphassasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno…pe… abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Catutthaṃ.

325. At Sāvatthī. 'Monks, whatever desire and lust there is for eye-contact, that is a defilement of the mind. ...for ear-contact... for nose-contact... for tongue-contact... for body-contact... whatever desire and lust there is for mind-contact, that is a defilement of the mind. When, monks, a monk... (the text is abbreviated)... his mind appears workable for realizing through direct knowledge those things that are to be realized.' The Fourth.

5. Samphassajasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on What is Born of Contact

326. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo, bhikkhave, cakkhusamphassajāya vedanāya chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo sotasamphassajāya vedanāya… yo ghānasamphassajāya vedanāya… yo jivhāsamphassajāya vedanāya… yo kāyasamphassajāya vedanāya… yo manosamphassajāya vedanāya chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno…pe… abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

326. At Sāvatthī. 'Monks, whatever desire and lust there is for feeling born of eye-contact, that is a defilement of the mind. ...for feeling born of ear-contact... for feeling born of nose-contact... for feeling born of tongue-contact... for feeling born of body-contact... whatever desire and lust there is for feeling born of mind-contact, that is a defilement of the mind. When, monks, a monk... (the text is abbreviated)... his mind appears workable for realizing through direct knowledge those things that are to be realized.' The Fifth.

6. Saññāsuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Perception

327. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpasaññāya chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo saddasaññāya… yo gandhasaññāya… yo rasasaññāya… yo phoṭṭhabbasaññāya… yo dhammasaññāya chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso[V 2.0230]. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno…pe… abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

327. At Sāvatthī. 'Monks, whatever desire and lust there is for perception of forms, that is a defilement of the mind. ...for perception of sounds... for perception of smells... for perception of tastes... for perception of tangible objects... whatever desire and lust there is for perception of mental phenomena, that is a defilement of the mind. When, monks, a monk... (the text is abbreviated)... his mind appears workable for realizing through direct knowledge those things that are to be realized.' The Sixth.

7. Sañcetanāsuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Volition

328. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpasañcetanāya chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo saddasañcetanāya… yo gandhasañcetanāya… yo [P 3.0234] rasasañcetanāya… yo phoṭṭhabbasañcetanāya… yo dhammasañcetanāya chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno…pe… abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Sattamaṃ.

328. At Sāvatthī. 'Monks, whatever desire and lust there is for volition regarding forms, that is a defilement of the mind. ...for volition regarding sounds... for volition regarding smells... for volition regarding tastes... for volition regarding tangible objects... whatever desire and lust there is for volition regarding mental phenomena, that is a defilement of the mind. When, monks, a monk... (the text is abbreviated)... his mind appears workable for realizing through direct knowledge those things that are to be realized.' The Seventh.

8. Taṇhāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Craving

329. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0196]. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpataṇhāya chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo saddataṇhāya… yo gandhataṇhāya… yo rasataṇhāya… yo phoṭṭhabbataṇhāya… yo dhammataṇhāya chandarāgo[T 3.0290], cittasseso upakkileso. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno…pe… abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

329. At Sāvatthī. 'Monks, whatever desire and lust there is in craving for forms, that is a defilement of the mind. ...in craving for sounds... in craving for smells... in craving for tastes... in craving for tangible objects... whatever desire and lust there is in craving for mental phenomena, that is a defilement of the mind. When, monks, a monk... (the text is abbreviated)... his mind appears workable for realizing through direct knowledge those things that are to be realized.' The Eighth.

9. Dhātusuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Elements

330. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuyā chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yo āpodhātuyā… yo tejodhātuyā… yo vāyodhātuyā… yo ākāsadhātuyā… yo viññāṇadhātuyā chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno imesu chasu ṭhānesu cetaso upakkileso pahīno hoti, nekkhammaninnañcassa cittaṃ [V 2.0231] hoti. Nekkhammaparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ kammaniyaṃ khāyati, abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Navamaṃ.

330. At Sāvatthī. 'Monks, whatever desire and lust there is for the earth element, that is a defilement of the mind. ...for the water element… for the fire element… for the air element… for the space element… whatever desire and lust there is for the consciousness element, that is a defilement of the mind. When, monks, a monk has abandoned the defilement of the mind in these six instances, his mind inclines to renunciation. A mind imbued with renunciation appears workable for realizing through direct knowledge those things that are to be realized.' The Ninth.

10. Khandhasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Aggregates

331. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso…pe… yo viññāṇasmiṃ chandarāgo, cittasseso upakkileso. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno imesu pañcasu ṭhānesu cetaso upakkileso pahīno hoti, nekkhammaninnañcassa cittaṃ hoti. Nekkhammaparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ kammaniyaṃ khāyati, abhiññā sacchikaraṇīyesu dhammesū”ti. Dasamaṃ.

331. At Sāvatthī. 'Monks, whatever desire and lust there is for form, that is a defilement of the mind; for feeling… for perception… for volitional formations… whatever desire and lust there is for consciousness, that is a defilement of the mind. When, monks, a monk has abandoned the defilement of the mind in these five instances, his mind inclines to renunciation. A mind imbued with renunciation appears workable for realizing through direct knowledge those things that are to be realized.' The Tenth.

Kilesasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Defilements is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Cakkhu [P 3.0235] rūpañca viññāṇaṃ, phasso ca vedanāya ca;

Saññā ca cetanā taṇhā, dhātu khandhena te dasāti.

Eye, Form, and Consciousness, Contact and Feeling; Perception, Volition, Craving, Elements, and with the Aggregates—these are ten.

7. Sāriputtasaṃyuttaṃ

7. The Connected Discourses with Sāriputta

1. Vivekajasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on What Is Born of Seclusion

332. Ekaṃ [T 3.0291][V 2.0232][M 2.0197] samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena andhavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Andhavanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi.

332. On one occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Sāriputta dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms. Having wandered for alms in Sāvatthī, after the meal, on returning from the alms round, he went to Andhavana for the day's abiding. Having entered Andhavana, he sat down at the foot of a certain tree for the day's abiding.

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena jetavanaṃ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “vippasannāni kho te, āvuso sāriputta, indriyāni; parisuddho mukhavaṇṇo pariyodāto. Katamenāyasmā sāriputto ajja vihārena vihāsī”ti?

Then, the Venerable Sāriputta, having arisen from seclusion in the evening, approached Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. The Venerable Ānanda saw the Venerable Sāriputta coming from afar. Having seen him, he said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Friend Sāriputta, your faculties are indeed serene; your facial complexion is pure and radiant. With what abiding did the Venerable Sāriputta abide today?”

“Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ [T 3.0292] paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ paṭhamā jhānā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. “Tathā [P 3.0236] hi panāyasmato sāriputtassa dīgharattaṃ ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā susamūhatā. Tasmā āyasmato sāriputtassa na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ paṭhamā jhānā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Here, friend, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I enter and abide in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained application, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. But, friend, it does not occur to me thus: ‘I am entering the first jhāna,’ or ‘I have entered the first jhāna,’ or ‘I have arisen from the first jhāna.’” “Indeed, it is because for the Venerable Sāriputta the underlying tendencies of I-making, my-making, and conceit have been well uprooted for a long time. Therefore, it does not occur to the Venerable Sāriputta thus: ‘I am entering the first jhāna,’ or ‘I have entered the first jhāna,’ or ‘I have arisen from the first jhāna.’” First.

2. Avitakkasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse Without Initial Application

333. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0233]. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando…pe… āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “vippasannāni kho te, āvuso sāriputta, indriyāni; parisuddho mukhavaṇṇo pariyodāto. Katamenāyasmā sāriputto ajja vihārena vihāsī”ti?

333. At Sāvatthī. The Venerable Ānanda saw… and said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Friend Sāriputta, your faculties are indeed serene; your facial complexion is pure and radiant. With what abiding did the Venerable Sāriputta abide today?”

“Idhāhaṃ[M 2.0198], āvuso, vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ dutiyā jhānā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. “Tathā hi panāyasmato sāriputtassa dīgharattaṃ ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā susamūhatā. Tasmā āyasmato sāriputtassa na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ dutiyā jhānā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Here, friend, with the stilling of initial and sustained application, I enter and abide in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without initial and sustained application, and is filled with the rapture and happiness born of concentration. Yet, friend, it does not occur to me: ‘I am entering the second jhāna,’ or ‘I have entered the second jhāna,’ or ‘I have arisen from the second jhāna.’” “Indeed, it is because for the Venerable Sāriputta the underlying tendencies of I-making, my-making, and conceit have been well uprooted for a long time. Therefore, it does not occur to the Venerable Sāriputta thus: ‘I am entering the second jhāna,’ or ‘I have entered the second jhāna,’ or ‘I have arisen from the second jhāna.’” Second.

3. Pītisuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Rapture

334. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando…pe… “vippasannāni kho te, āvuso sāriputta, indriyāni; parisuddho mukhavaṇṇo pariyodāto. Katamenāyasmā sāriputto ajja vihārena vihāsī”ti?

334. At Sāvatthī. The Venerable Ānanda saw… “Friend Sāriputta, your faculties are serene; your facial complexion is pure and radiant. In what abiding did the Venerable Sāriputta dwell today?”

“Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca vihāsiṃ sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedemi; yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti [P 3.0237] tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja [T 3.0293] viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ tatiyā jhānā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. “Tathā hi panāyasmato sāriputtassa dīgharattaṃ ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā susamūhatā. Tasmā āyasmato sāriputtassa na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ tatiyā jhānā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Here, friend, with the fading away of rapture, I dwelt equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and I experience happiness with the body. I abide having entered the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, one dwells happily.’ Yet, friend, it does not occur to me: ‘I am entering the third jhāna,’ or ‘I have entered the third jhāna,’ or ‘I have arisen from the third jhāna.’” “Indeed, it is because for the Venerable Sāriputta the underlying tendencies of I-making, my-making, and conceit have been well uprooted for a long time. Therefore, it does not occur to the Venerable Sāriputta thus: ‘I am entering the third jhāna,’ or ‘I have entered the third jhāna,’ or ‘I have arisen from the third jhāna.’” Third.

4. Upekkhāsuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Equanimity

335. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0234]. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando…pe… “vippasannāni kho te, āvuso sāriputta, indriyāni; parisuddho mukhavaṇṇo pariyodāto. Katamenāyasmā sāriputto ajja vihārena vihāsī”ti?

335. At Sāvatthī. The Venerable Ānanda saw…pe… “Friend Sāriputta, your faculties are serene, your facial complexion pure and radiant. In what abiding did the Venerable Sāriputta abide today?”

“Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ [M 2.0199] jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ catutthā jhānā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. “Tathā hi panāyasmato sāriputtassa dīgharattaṃ ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā susamūhatā. Tasmā āyasmato sāriputtassa na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ catutthā jhānā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Here, friend, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous passing away of joy and sorrow, I enter and abide in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. Yet, friend, it does not occur to me: ‘I am entering the fourth jhāna,’ or ‘I have entered the fourth jhāna,’ or ‘I have arisen from the fourth jhāna.’” “Indeed, it is because for the Venerable Sāriputta the underlying tendencies of I-making, my-making, and conceit have been well uprooted for a long time. Therefore, it does not occur to the Venerable Sāriputta thus: ‘I am entering the fourth jhāna,’ or ‘I have entered the fourth jhāna,’ or ‘I have arisen from the fourth jhāna.’” Fourth.

5. Ākāsānañcāyatanasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Base of Infinite Space

336. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0294]. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando…pe… “idhāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi…pe… vuṭṭhitoti vā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

336. At Sāvatthī. The Venerable Ānanda saw…pe… “Here, friend, by completely transcending perceptions of form, with the passing away of perceptions of resistance, not attending to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ I enter and abide in the base of infinite space…pe… or ‘I have arisen from it.’” Fifth.

6. Viññāṇañcāyatanasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Base of Infinite Consciousness

337. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando…pe… “idhāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma anantaṃ viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi…pe… vuṭṭhitoti vā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

337. At Sāvatthī. The Venerable Ānanda saw…pe… “Here, friend, having entirely transcended the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ I enter and abide in the base of infinite consciousness…pe… or ‘I have arisen from it.’” Sixth.

7. Ākiñcaññāyatanasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Base of Nothingness

338. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto…pe… “idhāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbaso [V 2.0235] viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma, natthi kiñcīti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi…pe… vuṭṭhitoti vā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

338. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Sāriputta…pe… “Here, friend, having entirely transcended the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing,’ I enter and abide in the base of nothingness…pe… or ‘I have arisen from it.’” Seventh.

8. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Base of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception

339. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0238]. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto…pe… “idhāhaṃ, āvuso, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi…pe… vuṭṭhitoti vā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

339. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Sāriputta…pe… “Here, friend, having transcended the base of nothingness, I enter and abide in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception…pe… or ‘I have arisen from it.’” Eighth.

9. Nirodhasamāpattisuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Attainment of Cessation

340. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto…pe…[T 3.0295]. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ [M 2.0200] upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. “Tathā hi panāyasmato sāriputtassa dīgharattaṃ ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā susamūhatā. Tasmā āyasmato sāriputtassa na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno’ti vā ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhā vuṭṭhito’ti vā”ti. Navamaṃ.

340. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Sāriputta... and so on.... 'Here, friend, having entirely transcended the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, I enter and dwell in the cessation of perception and feeling. To me, friend, it does not occur thus: “I am entering the cessation of perception and feeling,” or “I have entered the cessation of perception and feeling,” or “I have emerged from the cessation of perception and feeling.”' 'It is because for the Venerable Sāriputta, for a long time the underlying tendencies of I-making, mine-making, and conceit have been well uprooted. Therefore, it does not occur to the Venerable Sāriputta thus: “I am entering the cessation of perception and feeling,” or “I have entered the cessation of perception and feeling,” or “I have emerged from the cessation of perception and feeling.”' The ninth.

10. Sūcimukhīsuttaṃ

10. The Sūcimukhī Discourse

341. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahe piṇḍāya pāvisi. Rājagahe sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ aññataraṃ kuṭṭamūlaṃ kuḍḍamūlaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.), kuḍḍaṃ (pī.) nissāya paribhuñjati. Atha kho sūcimukhī paribbājikā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca [T 3.0296] –

341. On one occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling in Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Sāriputta dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Rājagaha for alms-food. After wandering for alms-food from house to house in Rājagaha, he was partaking of his alms-food leaning against the base of a certain wall. Then the female wanderer Sucimukhī approached the Venerable Sāriputta. Having approached, she said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“Kiṃ [V 2.0236] nu kho, samaṇa, adhomukho bhuñjasī”ti? “Na khvāhaṃ, bhagini, adhomukho bhuñjāmī”ti. “Tena hi, samaṇa, ubbhamukho uddhaṃmukho (sī. aṭṭha.) bhuñjasī”ti? “Na khvāhaṃ, bhagini, ubbhamukho bhuñjāmī”ti. “Tena [P 3.0239] hi, samaṇa, disāmukho bhuñjasī”ti? “Na khvāhaṃ, bhagini, disāmukho bhuñjāmī”ti. “Tena hi, samaṇa, vidisāmukho bhuñjasī”ti? “Na khvāhaṃ, bhagini, vidisāmukho bhuñjāmī”ti.

‘How now, recluse, do you eat looking downwards?’ ‘I do not, sister, eat looking downwards.’ ‘If so, recluse, do you eat looking upwards?’ ‘I do not, sister, eat looking upwards.’ ‘If so, recluse, do you eat looking towards the cardinal directions?’ ‘I do not, sister, eat looking towards the cardinal directions.’ ‘If so, recluse, do you eat looking towards the intermediate directions?’ ‘I do not, sister, eat looking towards the intermediate directions.’

“‘Kiṃ nu, samaṇa, adhomukho bhuñjasī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na khvāhaṃ, bhagini, adhomukho bhuñjāmī’ti vadesi. ‘Tena hi, samaṇa, ubbhamukho bhuñjasī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na khvāhaṃ, bhagini, ubbhamukho bhuñjāmī’ti vadesi. ‘Tena hi, samaṇa, disāmukho bhuñjasī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na khvāhaṃ, bhagini, disāmukho bhuñjāmī’ti vadesi. ‘Tena hi, samaṇa, vidisāmukho bhuñjasī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na khvāhaṃ, bhagini, vidisāmukho bhuñjāmī’ti vadesi”.

‘When asked, “How now, recluse, do you eat looking downwards?” you say, “I do not, sister, eat looking downwards.” When asked, “If so, recluse, do you eat looking upwards?” you say, “I do not, sister, eat looking upwards.” When asked, “If so, recluse, do you eat looking towards the cardinal directions?” you say, “I do not, sister, eat looking towards the cardinal directions.” When asked, “If so, recluse, do you eat looking towards the intermediate directions?” you say, “I do not, sister, eat looking towards the intermediate directions.”’

“Kathañcarahi[M 2.0201], samaṇa, bhuñjasī”ti? “Ye hi keci, bhagini, samaṇabrāhmaṇā samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā (sī.) nigamanavākye pana sabbatthāpi samāsoyeva dissati vatthuvijjātiracchānavijjāya micchājīvena jīvikaṃ jīvitaṃ (ka.) kappenti, ime vuccanti, bhagini, samaṇabrāhmaṇā ‘adhomukhā bhuñjantī’ti. Ye hi keci, bhagini, samaṇabrāhmaṇā nakkhattavijjātiracchānavijjāya micchājīvena jīvikaṃ kappenti, ime vuccanti, bhagini, samaṇabrāhmaṇā ‘ubbhamukhā bhuñjantī’ti. Ye hi keci, bhagini, samaṇabrāhmaṇā dūteyyapahiṇagamanānuyogāya … nuyogā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), … nuyogena (?) micchājīvena jīvikaṃ kappenti, ime vuccanti, bhagini, samaṇabrāhmaṇā ‘disāmukhā bhuñjantī’ti. Ye hi keci, bhagini, samaṇabrāhmaṇā aṅgavijjātiracchānavijjāya micchājīvena [T 3.0297] jīvikaṃ kappenti, ime vuccanti, bhagini, samaṇabrāhmaṇā ‘vidisāmukhā bhuñjantī’”ti.

‘How then, recluse, do you eat?’ ‘Sister, whatever recluses and brahmins make a living by wrong livelihood, by the base art of site-lore, these recluses and brahmins, sister, are said to ‘eat looking downwards.’ Whatever recluses and brahmins, sister, make a living by wrong livelihood, by the base art of astrology, these recluses and brahmins, sister, are said to ‘eat looking upwards.’ Whatever recluses and brahmins, sister, make a living by wrong livelihood by undertaking the going on messages and errands, these recluses and brahmins, sister, are said to ‘eat looking towards the cardinal directions.’ Whatever recluses and brahmins, sister, make a living by wrong livelihood, by the base art of limb-reading, these recluses and brahmins, sister, are said to ‘eat looking towards the intermediate directions.’’

“So khvāhaṃ, bhagini, na vatthuvijjātiracchānavijjāya micchājīvena jīvikaṃ kappemi, na nakkhattavijjātiracchānavijjāya micchājīvena jīvikaṃ kappemi, na dūteyyapahiṇagamanānuyogāya micchājīvena jīvikaṃ kappemi, na aṅgavijjātiracchānavijjāya micchājīvena jīvikaṃ kappemi. Dhammena bhikkhaṃ pariyesāmi; dhammena bhikkhaṃ pariyesitvā bhuñjāmī”ti.

Indeed, sister, I do not make a living by wrong livelihood through the base art of site-lore; I do not make a living by wrong livelihood through the base art of astrology; I do not make a living by wrong livelihood through the practice of going on messages and errands; I do not make a living by wrong livelihood through the base art of limb-reading. I seek alms righteously; having sought alms righteously, I eat.

Atha [V 2.0237][P 3.0240] kho sūcimukhī paribbājikā rājagahe rathiyāya rathiyaṃ, siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamārocesi – “dhammikaṃ samaṇā sakyaputtiyā āhāraṃ āhārenti; anavajjaṃ anavajjena (ka.) samaṇā sakyaputtiyā āhāraṃ āhārenti. Detha samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ piṇḍa”nti. Dasamaṃ.

Then the female wanderer Sūcimukhī went from street to street, from crossroads to crossroads in Rājagaha, announcing: “The ascetics, the sons of the Sakyans, consume righteous food; the ascetics, the sons of the Sakyans, consume blameless food. Give alms to the ascetics, the sons of the Sakyans!” The tenth.

Sāriputtasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses with Sāriputta is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Vivekajaṃ avitakkaṃ, pīti upekkhā catutthakaṃ;

Ākāsañceva viññāṇaṃ, ākiñcaṃ nevasaññinā;

Nirodho navamo vutto, dasamaṃ sūcimukhī cāti.

Born of Seclusion, Without Thought, Joy, and Equanimity as the fourth; Space, Consciousness, Nothingness, and Neither-Perception; Cessation is stated as the ninth, and the tenth is Sūcimukhī.

8. Nāgasaṃyuttaṃ

8. The Connected Discourses on Nāgas

1. Suddhikasuttaṃ

1. The Basic Discourse

342. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0298][V 2.0238][M 2.0202]. “Catasso imā, bhikkhave, nāgayoniyo. Katamā catasso? Aṇḍajā nāgā, jalābujā nāgā, saṃsedajā nāgā, opapātikā nāgā – imā kho, bhikkhave, catasso nāgayoniyo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

342. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of nāga births. What four? Egg-born nāgas, womb-born nāgas, moisture-born nāgas, and spontaneously-born nāgas. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of nāga births.” The first.

2. Paṇītatarasuttaṃ

2. More Excellent

343. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Catasso imā, bhikkhave, nāgayoniyo. Katamā catasso? Aṇḍajā nāgā, jalābujā nāgā, saṃsedajā nāgā, opapātikā nāgā. Tatra[P 3.0241], bhikkhave, aṇḍajehi nāgehi jalābujā ca saṃsedajā ca opapātikā ca nāgā paṇītatarā. Tatra, bhikkhave, aṇḍajehi ca jalābujehi ca nāgehi saṃsedajā ca opapātikā ca nāgā paṇītatarā. Tatra, bhikkhave, aṇḍajehi ca jalābujehi ca saṃsedajehi ca nāgehi opapātikā nāgā paṇītatarā. Imā kho, bhikkhave, catasso nāgayoniyo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

343. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of nāga births. What four? Egg-born nāgas, womb-born nāgas, moisture-born nāgas, and spontaneously-born nāgas. Among these, bhikkhus, the womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously-born nāgas are more excellent than the egg-born nāgas. Among these, bhikkhus, the moisture-born and spontaneously-born nāgas are more excellent than the egg-born and womb-born nāgas. Among these, bhikkhus, the spontaneously-born nāgas are more excellent than the egg-born, womb-born, and moisture-born nāgas. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of nāga births.” The second.

3. Uposathasuttaṃ

3. The Uposatha Discourse

344. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacce aṇḍajā nāgā uposathaṃ upavasanti vossaṭṭhakāyā ca bhavantī”ti?

344. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why in this world some egg-born nāgas observe the Uposatha and have relinquished bodies?'

“Idha[V 2.0239], bhikkhu, ekaccānaṃ [T 3.0299] aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘mayaṃ kho pubbe kāyena dvayakārino ahumha, vācāya dvayakārino, manasā dvayakārino. Te mayaṃ kāyena dvayakārino, vācāya dvayakārino, manasā dvayakārino, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapannā. Sacajja mayaṃ kāyena sucaritaṃ careyyāma, vācāya sucaritaṃ careyyāma, manasā sucaritaṃ careyyāma, evaṃ mayaṃ [M 2.0203] kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyāma. Handa, mayaṃ etarahi kāyena sucaritaṃ carāma, vācāya sucaritaṃ carāma, manasā sucaritaṃ carāmā’ti. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacce aṇḍajā nāgā uposathaṃ upavasanti vossaṭṭhakāyā ca bhavantī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

‘Here, bhikkhu, for some egg-born nāgas it occurs thus: “In the past, we engaged in twofold conduct by body, twofold conduct by speech, and twofold conduct by mind. Those of us who engaged in twofold conduct by body, speech, and mind, with the breakup of the body, after death, have arisen in the company of egg-born nāgas. If today we were to practice good conduct by body, good conduct by speech, and good conduct by mind, then with the breakup of the body, after death, we might arise in a good destination, a heavenly world. Come, let us now practice good conduct by body, good conduct by speech, and good conduct by mind.” This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the reason, why in this world some egg-born nāgas observe the Uposatha and have relinquished bodies.’

4. Dutiyauposathasuttaṃ

4. The Second Uposatha Sutta

345. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0242]. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacce jalābujā nāgā uposathaṃ upavasanti vossaṭṭhakāyā ca bhavantī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu…pe… ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacce jalābujā nāgā uposathaṃ upavasanti vossaṭṭhakāyā ca bhavantī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

345. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One… and sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why in this world some womb-born nāgas observe the Uposatha and have relinquished bodies?' 'Here, bhikkhu… (the text should be expanded as in the preceding sutta, substituting “womb-born” for “egg-born”) … This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the reason, why in this world some womb-born nāgas observe the Uposatha and have relinquished bodies.' Fourth.

5. Tatiyauposathasuttaṃ

5. The Third Uposatha Sutta

346. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacce saṃsedajā nāgā uposathaṃ upavasanti vossaṭṭhakāyā ca bhavantī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu…pe… ayaṃ [T 3.0300] kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacce saṃsedajā nāgā uposathaṃ upavasanti vossaṭṭhakāyā ca bhavantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

346. At Sāvatthī. Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why in this world some moisture-born nāgas observe the Uposatha and have relinquished bodies?' 'Here, bhikkhu… (the text should be expanded as in the preceding sutta, substituting “moisture-born” for “egg-born”) … This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the reason, why in this world some moisture-born nāgas observe the Uposatha and have relinquished bodies.' Fifth.

6. Catutthauposathasuttaṃ

6. The Fourth Uposatha Sutta

347. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko [V 2.0240] nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacce opapātikā nāgā uposathaṃ upavasanti vossaṭṭhakāyā ca bhavantī”ti?

347. At Sāvatthī. Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why in this world some spontaneously born nāgas observe the Uposatha and have relinquished bodies?'

“Idha, bhikkhu, ekaccānaṃ opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘mayaṃ kho pubbe kāyena dvayakārino ahumha, vācāya dvayakārino, manasā dvayakārino. Te mayaṃ kāyena dvayakārino, vācāya dvayakārino, manasā dvayakārino, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapannā. Sacajja [P 3.0243] mayaṃ kāyena sucaritaṃ careyyāma[M 2.0204], vācāya… manasā sucaritaṃ careyyāma, evaṃ mayaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyāma. Handa, mayaṃ etarahi kāyena sucaritaṃ carāma, vācāya… manasā sucaritaṃ carāmā’ti. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacce opapātikā nāgā uposathaṃ upavasanti vossaṭṭhakāyā ca bhavantī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

‘Here, bhikkhu, for some spontaneously born nāgas it occurs thus: “In the past, we engaged in twofold conduct by body, twofold conduct by speech, and twofold conduct by mind. Those of us who engaged in twofold conduct by body, speech, and mind, with the breakup of the body, after death, have arisen in the company of spontaneously born nāgas. If today we were to practice good conduct by body, … and good conduct by mind, then with the breakup of the body, after death, we might arise in a good destination, a heavenly world. Come, let us now practice good conduct by body, … and good conduct by mind.” This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the reason, why in this world some spontaneously born nāgas observe the Uposatha and have relinquished bodies.’ Sixth.

7. Sutasuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on What is Heard

348. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti[T 3.0301]?

348. At Sāvatthī. Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why in this world a certain person, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of egg-born nāgas?'

“Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī hoti, manasā dvayakārī hoti. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘aṇḍajā nāgā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

‘Here, bhikkhu, a certain person engages in twofold conduct by body, twofold conduct by speech, and twofold conduct by mind. He has heard: ‘The egg-born nāgas are long-lived, beautiful, and have much happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the company of the egg-born nāgas!’ With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the company of the egg-born nāgas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the reason, why in this world a certain person, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the egg-born nāgas.’ Seventh.

8. Dutiyasutasuttaṃ

8. The Second Sutta on What is Heard

349. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko [V 2.0241] nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā jalābujānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti?…Pe… ayaṃ [P 3.0244] kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā jalābujānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatīti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

349. At Sāvatthī. Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why in this world a certain person, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the womb-born nāgas?' … (The text should be expanded as in the preceding sutta, substituting “womb-born” for “egg-born”) … This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the reason, why in this world a certain person, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the womb-born nāgas.’ Eighth.

9. Tatiyasutasuttaṃ

9. The Third Sutta on What is Heard

350. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa [M 2.0205] bhedā paraṃ maraṇā saṃsedajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti?…Pe… ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā saṃsedajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatīti. Navamaṃ.

350. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: 'What, Venerable Sir, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, is reborn into companionship with the moisture-born nāgas?' … This, Bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby a certain person here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, is reborn into companionship with the moisture-born nāgas. Ninth.

10. Catutthasutasuttaṃ

10. The Fourth Sutta on What Was Heard

351. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa [T 3.0302] bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti?

351. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: 'What, Venerable Sir, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, is reborn into companionship with the spontaneously born nāgas?'

“Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘opapātikā nāgā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices twofold conduct by body, twofold conduct by speech, and twofold conduct by mind. He has heard: ‘The spontaneously born nāgas are long-lived, beautiful, and have much happiness.’ The wish arises in him: ‘Oh, that with the breaking up of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the companionship of the spontaneously born nāgas!’ With the breaking up of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of the spontaneously born nāgas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which a certain person here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, is reborn into the companionship of the spontaneously born nāgas.” Tenth.

11-20. Aṇḍajadānūpakārasuttadasakaṃ

11–20. The Decad of Suttas on the Benefit of Gifts to the Egg-Born

352-361. Ekamantaṃ [V 2.0242] nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco [P 3.0245] kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti?

Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, is reborn into the companionship of the egg-born nāgas?”

“Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘aṇḍajā nāgā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So annaṃ deti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu…pe… upapajjatīti…pe… so pānaṃ deti…pe… vatthaṃ deti…pe… yānaṃ deti…pe… mālaṃ deti…pe… gandhaṃ deti…pe… vilepanaṃ deti…pe… seyyaṃ deti…pe… āvasathaṃ deti…pe… padīpeyyaṃ [M 2.0206] deti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena [T 3.0303] midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Vīsatimaṃ.

“Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices twofold conduct by body, twofold conduct by speech, and twofold conduct by mind. He has heard: ‘The egg-born nāgas are long-lived, beautiful, and have much happiness.’ The wish arises in him: ‘Oh, that with the breaking up of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the companionship of the egg-born nāgas!’ He gives food, he gives drink, he gives clothing, he gives a vehicle, he gives garlands, he gives perfume, he gives ointment, he gives bedding, he gives lodging, he gives a lamp. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of the egg-born nāgas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which a certain person here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, is reborn into the companionship of the egg-born nāgas.” Twentieth.

21-50. Jalābujādidānūpakārasuttattiṃsakaṃ

21–50. The Thirty Suttas on the Benefit of Gifts to the Womb-Born and Others

362-391. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā jalābujānaṃ nāgānaṃ…pe… saṃsedajānaṃ nāgānaṃ…pe… opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti?

362–391. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby some person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of womb-born nāgas… moisture-born nāgas… spontaneously born nāgas?”

“Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘opapātikā nāgā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So annaṃ deti…pe… pānaṃ deti…pe… padīpeyyaṃ deti. So kāyassa bhedā [V 2.0243] paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco [P 3.0246] kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ nāgānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti.

“Here, bhikkhu, a certain person performs twofold deeds by body, twofold deeds by speech, and twofold deeds by mind. He has heard: ‘Spontaneously born nāgas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that I, with the breakup of the body, after death, might be reborn into companionship with the spontaneously born nāgas!’ He gives food… he gives drink… he gives a lamp. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into companionship with the spontaneously born nāgas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby some person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into companionship with the spontaneously born nāgas.”

(Iminā peyyālena dasa dasa suttantā kātabbā. Evaṃ catūsu yonīsu cattālīsaṃ veyyākaraṇā honti. Purimehi pana dasahi suttantehi saha honti paṇṇāsasuttantāti.)

(By this extended passage, ten suttas each are to be made. Thus, there are forty expositions concerning the four modes of generation. Together with the preceding ten suttas, there are fifty suttas in total.)

Nāgasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Nāgas are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Suddhikaṃ [T 3.0304] paṇītataraṃ, caturo ca uposathā;

Tassa sutaṃ caturo ca, dānūpakārā ca tālīsaṃ;

Paṇṇāsa piṇḍato suttā, nāgamhi suppakāsitāti.

The Pure, the More Refined, and four on the Uposatha; Four on What Was Heard, and forty on the Benefit of Gifts; Fifty discourses in total are well expounded in the Nāga [Saṃyutta].

9. Supaṇṇasaṃyuttaṃ

9. The Connected Discourses on Garuḍas

1. Suddhikasuttaṃ

1. The Pure Sutta

392. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0244][M 2.0207]. “Catasso imā, bhikkhave, supaṇṇayoniyo. Katamā catasso? Aṇḍajā supaṇṇā, jalābujā supaṇṇā, saṃsedajā supaṇṇā, opapātikā supaṇṇā – imā kho, bhikkhave, catasso supaṇṇayoniyo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

392. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four modes of generation for garuḍas. Which four? Egg-born garuḍas, womb-born garuḍas, moisture-born garuḍas, and spontaneously born garuḍas. These, bhikkhus, are the four modes of generation for garuḍas.” First.

2. Harantisuttaṃ

2. The Sutta on Seizing

393. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0247]. “Catasso imā, bhikkhave, supaṇṇayoniyo. Katamā catasso? Aṇḍajā…pe… imā kho, bhikkhave, catasso supaṇṇayoniyo. Tatra, bhikkhave, aṇḍajā supaṇṇā aṇḍajeva nāge haranti, na jalābuje, na saṃsedaje, na opapātike. Tatra, bhikkhave, jalābujā supaṇṇā aṇḍaje ca jalābuje ca nāge haranti, na saṃsedaje, na opapātike. Tatra, bhikkhave, saṃsedajā supaṇṇā aṇḍaje ca jalābuje ca saṃsedaje ca nāge haranti, na opapātike. Tatra, bhikkhave, opapātikā supaṇṇā aṇḍaje ca jalābuje ca saṃsedaje ca opapātike ca nāge haranti. Imā kho, bhikkhave, catasso supaṇṇayoniyo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

393. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four modes of generation for garuḍas. Which four? Egg-born… and so on… These, bhikkhus, are the four modes of generation for garuḍas. Therein, bhikkhus, egg-born garuḍas seize only egg-born nāgas, not womb-born, not moisture-born, not spontaneously born. Therein, bhikkhus, womb-born garuḍas seize egg-born and womb-born nāgas, not moisture-born, not spontaneously born. Therein, bhikkhus, moisture-born garuḍas seize egg-born, womb-born, and moisture-born nāgas, not spontaneously born. Therein, bhikkhus, spontaneously born garuḍas seize egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously born nāgas. These, bhikkhus, are the four modes of generation for garuḍas.” Second.

3. Dvayakārīsuttaṃ

3. The Sutta on the Doer of Twofold Deeds

394. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā [V 2.0245] aṇḍajānaṃ [T 3.0306] supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘aṇḍajā supaṇṇā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo[M 2.0208], yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

394. At Sāvatthī. A certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born garuḍas?” “Here, bhikkhu, a certain person is a doer of two kinds of deeds by body, a doer of two kinds of deeds by speech, and a doer of two kinds of deeds by mind. He has heard: ‘Egg-born garuḍas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of egg-born garuḍas!’ With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of egg-born garuḍas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born garuḍas.” Third.

4-6. Dutiyādidvayakārīsuttattikaṃ

4-6. The Triplet of Discourses on the Doer of Two Kinds of Deeds, from the Second Onwards

395-397. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ [P 3.0248] etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā jalābujānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ…pe… saṃsedajānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ…pe… opapātikānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘opapātikā supaṇṇā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

395-397. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of womb-born garuḍas… moisture-born garuḍas… or spontaneously-born garuḍas?” “Here, bhikkhu, a certain person is a doer of two kinds of deeds by body, a doer of two kinds of deeds by speech, and a doer of two kinds of deeds by mind. He has heard: ‘The spontaneously-born garuḍas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the spontaneously-born garuḍas!’ With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of the spontaneously-born garuḍas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the spontaneously-born garuḍas.” Sixth.

7-16. Aṇḍajadānūpakārasuttadasakaṃ

7-16. The Ten Discourses on Beneficial Giving Regarding the Egg-Born

398-407. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0307]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘aṇḍajā supaṇṇā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā [V 2.0246] paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So annaṃ deti…pe… pānaṃ deti… vatthaṃ deti… yānaṃ deti… mālaṃ deti… gandhaṃ deti… vilepanaṃ deti… seyyaṃ deti… āvasathaṃ deti… padīpeyyaṃ deti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Soḷasamaṃ.

398-407. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born garuḍas?” “Here, bhikkhu, a certain person is a doer of two kinds of deeds by body, a doer of two kinds of deeds by speech, and a doer of two kinds of deeds by mind. He has heard: ‘The egg-born garuḍas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of egg-born garuḍas!’ He gives food, drink, clothing, a vehicle, a garland, perfume, ointment, a bed, a dwelling, and a lamp. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of egg-born garuḍas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born garuḍas.” Sixteenth.

17-46. Jalābujādidānūpakārasuttatiṃsakaṃ

17-46. The Thirty Discourses on Beneficial Giving Regarding the Womb-Born and Others

408-437. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0209]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ [P 3.0249] etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā jalābujānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ…pe… saṃsedajānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ…pe… opapātikānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘opapātikā supaṇṇā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā [T 3.0308] paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So annaṃ deti…pe… pānaṃ deti…pe… padīpeyyaṃ deti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā opapātikānaṃ supaṇṇānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Chacattālīsamaṃ.

408-437. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of womb-born garuḍas… moisture-born garuḍas… or spontaneously-born garuḍas?” “Here, bhikkhu, a certain person is a doer of two kinds of deeds by body, a doer of two kinds of deeds by speech, and a doer of two kinds of deeds by mind. He has heard: ‘The spontaneously-born garuḍas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the spontaneously-born garuḍas!’ He gives food, drink, … and a lamp. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of the spontaneously-born garuḍas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the spontaneously-born garuḍas.” Forty-sixth.

(Evaṃ piṇḍakena chacattālīsaṃ suttantā honti.)

[Thus, in total, there are forty-six discourses.]

Supaṇṇasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Garuḍas is complete.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Suddhikaṃ haranti ceva, dvayakārī ca caturo;

Dānūpakārā tālīsaṃ, supaṇṇe suppakāsitāti.

The Suddhika and the Harati, and four on the doer of two kinds of deeds; Forty on beneficial giving, are well-proclaimed in the Supaṇṇa.

10. Gandhabbakāyasaṃyuttaṃ

10. The Connected Discourses on the Gandhabba Host

1. Suddhikasuttaṃ

1. The Simple Sutta

438. Ekaṃ [T 3.0309][V 2.0247][M 2.0210] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme …pe… bhagavā etadavoca – “gandhabbakāyike [P 3.0250] vo, bhikkhave, deve desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, gandhabbakāyikā devā? Santi, bhikkhave, mūlagandhe adhivatthā devā. Santi, bhikkhave, sāragandhe adhivatthā devā. Santi, bhikkhave, pheggugandhe adhivatthā devā. Santi, bhikkhave, tacagandhe adhivatthā devā. Santi, bhikkhave, papaṭikagandhe adhivatthā devā. Santi, bhikkhave, pattagandhe adhivatthā devā. Santi, bhikkhave, pupphagandhe adhivatthā devā. Santi, bhikkhave, phalagandhe adhivatthā devā. Santi, bhikkhave, rasagandhe adhivatthā devā. Santi, bhikkhave, gandhagandhe adhivatthā devā. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, gandhabbakāyikā devā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

438. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park... the Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the devas of the gandhabba host. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, are the devas of the gandhabba host? There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over root fragrance. There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over heartwood fragrance. There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over sapwood fragrance. There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over bark fragrance. There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over outer bark fragrance. There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over leaf fragrance. There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over flower fragrance. There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over fruit fragrance. There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over sap fragrance. There are, bhikkhus, devas who preside over the fragrance of scents. These, bhikkhus, are called the devas of the gandhabba host.” The First.

2. Sucaritasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Good Conduct

439. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gandhabbakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṃ carati, vācāya sucaritaṃ carati, manasā sucaritaṃ carati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘gandhabbakāyikā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā [T 3.0310] paraṃ maraṇā gandhabbakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gandhabbakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu[V 2.0248], hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gandhabbakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

439. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the companionship of the devas of the gandhabba host?” “Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices good conduct by body, practices good conduct by speech, and practices good conduct by mind. He has heard: ‘The devas of the gandhabba host are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the companionship of the devas of the gandhabba host!’ With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of the devas of the gandhabba host. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the companionship of the devas of the gandhabba host.” The Second.

3. Mūlagandhadātāsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Giver of Root Fragrances

440. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ [P 3.0251] etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti[M 2.0211]? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṃ carati, vācāya sucaritaṃ carati, manasā sucaritaṃ carati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘mūlagandhe adhivatthā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So dātā hoti mūlagandhānaṃ. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu…pe… yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

440. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the companionship of the devas who preside over root fragrance?” “Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices good conduct by body, good conduct by speech, and good conduct by mind. He has heard: ‘The devas who preside over root fragrance are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the companionship of the devas who preside over root fragrance!’ He is a giver of root fragrances. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of the devas who preside over root fragrance. This, bhikkhu, is the cause… whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the companionship of the devas who preside over root fragrance.” The Third.

4-12. Sāragandhādidātāsuttanavakaṃ

4-12. The Group of Nine Discourses on Givers of Heartwood Fragrances and So Forth

441-449. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [T 3.0311] – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sāragandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ…pe… pheggugandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… tacagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… papaṭikagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… pattagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… pupphagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… phalagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… rasagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… gandhagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṃ carati, vācāya sucaritaṃ carati, manasā sucaritaṃ carati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘sāragandhe adhivatthā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sāragandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ…pe… pheggugandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… tacagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… papaṭikagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… pattagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… pupphagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… phalagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… rasagandhe adhivatthānaṃ [V 2.0249] devānaṃ… gandhagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So dātā hoti sāragandhānaṃ…pe… so dātā hoti pheggugandhānaṃ… so dātā hoti tacagandhānaṃ… so [P 3.0252] dātā hoti papaṭikagandhānaṃ… so dātā hoti pattagandhānaṃ… so dātā hoti pupphagandhānaṃ… so dātā hoti phalagandhānaṃ… so dātā hoti rasagandhānaṃ… so dātā hoti gandhagandhānaṃ. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gandhagandhe [T 3.0312] adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ [M 2.0212] paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gandhagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

441-449. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the companionship of the devas who preside over heartwood fragrance… over sapwood fragrance… over bark fragrance… over outer bark fragrance… over leaf fragrance… over flower fragrance… over fruit fragrance… over sap fragrance… over the fragrance of scents?” “Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices good conduct by body, good conduct by speech, and good conduct by mind. He has heard: ‘The devas who preside over heartwood fragrance are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the companionship of the devas who preside over heartwood fragrance… over sapwood fragrance… over bark fragrance… over outer bark fragrance… over leaf fragrance… over flower fragrance… over fruit fragrance… over sap fragrance… over the fragrance of scents!’ He is a giver of heartwood fragrances… a giver of sapwood fragrances… a giver of bark fragrances… a giver of outer bark fragrances… a giver of leaf fragrances… a giver of flower fragrances… a giver of fruit fragrances… a giver of sap fragrances… a giver of scent fragrances. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of the devas who preside over the fragrance of scents. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the companionship of the devas who preside over the fragrance of scents.” The Twelfth.

13-22. Mūlagandhadānūpakārasuttadasakaṃ

13-22. The Decad of Discourses on the Benefits of Offering Root Fragrances

450-459. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṃ carati, vācāya sucaritaṃ carati, manasā sucaritaṃ carati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘mūlagandhe adhivatthā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So annaṃ deti…pe… pānaṃ deti… vatthaṃ deti… yānaṃ deti… mālaṃ deti… gandhaṃ deti… vilepanaṃ deti… seyyaṃ deti… āvasathaṃ deti… padīpeyyaṃ deti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā mūlagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Bāvīsatimaṃ.

450-459. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that monk said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why a certain person here, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the devas who preside over fragrant roots?” “Here, monk, a certain person practices good conduct by body, speech, and mind. They have heard: ‘The devas who preside over fragrant roots are long-lived, beautiful, and have abundant happiness.’ The wish arises in them: ‘Oh, that on the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the company of the devas who preside over fragrant roots!’ They give food… they give drink… they give clothing… they give a vehicle… they give garlands… they give perfume… they give ointment… they give a bed… they give lodging… they give a lamp. On the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn into the company of the devas who preside over fragrant roots. This, monk, is the cause, this is the reason why a certain person here, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the devas who preside over fragrant roots.” The twenty-second.

23-112. Sāragandhādidānūpakārasuttanavutikaṃ

23-112. The Ninety Discourses on the Benefits of Offerings of Heartwood Scents and so on

460-549. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0253]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sāragandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ…pe… pheggugandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… tacagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ [T 3.0313]… papaṭikagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… pattagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… pupphagandhe [V 2.0250] adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… phalagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… rasagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ… gandhagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṃ carati, vācāya sucaritaṃ carati, manasā sucaritaṃ carati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘gandhagandhe adhivatthā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gandhagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So annaṃ deti…pe… pānaṃ deti… vatthaṃ deti… yānaṃ deti… mālaṃ deti… gandhaṃ deti… vilepanaṃ [M 2.0213] deti… seyyaṃ deti… āvasathaṃ deti… padīpeyyaṃ deti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gandhagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gandhagandhe adhivatthānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Dvādasasatimaṃ.

460-549. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that monk said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why a certain person here, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the devas who preside over fragrant heartwood… the devas who preside over fragrant softwood… the devas who preside over fragrant bark… the devas who preside over fragrant rind… the devas who preside over fragrant leaves… the devas who preside over fragrant flowers… the devas who preside over fragrant fruits… the devas who preside over fragrant sap… the devas who preside over all fragrances?” “Here, monk, a certain person practices good conduct by body, speech, and mind. They have heard: ‘The devas who preside over all fragrances are long-lived, beautiful, and have abundant happiness.’ The wish arises in them: ‘Oh, that on the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the company of the devas who preside over all fragrances!’ They give food… they give drink… they give clothing… they give a vehicle… they give garlands… they give perfume… they give ointment… they give a bed… they give lodging… they give a lamp. On the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn into the company of the devas who preside over all fragrances. This, monk, is the cause, this is the reason why a certain person here, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the devas who preside over all fragrances.” The one hundred and twelfth.

(Evaṃ piṇḍakena ekasatañca dvādasa ca suttantā honti.)

Thus, with the summary, there are one hundred and twelve discourses.

Gandhabbakāyasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Gandhabba Host is completed.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for it:

Suddhikañca sucaritaṃ, dātā hi apare dasa;

Dānūpakārā satadhā, gandhabbe suppakāsitāti.

Suddhika and Sucarita, and ten others concerning giving; the supports of giving are a hundredfold. Thus is the Gandhabba [Saṃyutta] well proclaimed.

11. Valāhakasaṃyuttaṃ

11. The Connected Discourses on Cloud Devas

1. Suddhikasuttaṃ

1. The Suddhika Discourse

550. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0314][M 2.0214][P 3.0254][V 2.0251]. “Valāhakakāyike vo, bhikkhave, deve desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha. Katame ca, bhikkhave, valāhakakāyikā devā? Santi, bhikkhave, sītavalāhakā devā; santi uṇhavalāhakā devā; santi abbhavalāhakā devā; santi vātavalāhakā devā; santi vassavalāhakā devā – ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, ‘valāhakakāyikā devā’”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

550. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, I will teach you about the host of Valāhaka devas. Listen to that. And what, monks, are the host of Valāhaka devas? There are, monks, cold-cloud devas; there are hot-cloud devas; there are cloud-bank devas; there are wind-cloud devas; there are rain-cloud devas. These, monks, are called the host of Valāhaka devas.” First.

2. Sucaritasuttaṃ

2. The Sucarita Discourse

551. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṃ carati, vācāya sucaritaṃ carati, manasā sucaritaṃ carati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘valāhakakāyikā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṃ [T 3.0315] devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

551. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, that monk said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why a certain person here, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the host of Valāhaka devas?” “Here, monk, a certain person practices good conduct by body, speech, and mind. They have heard: ‘The host of Valāhaka devas are long-lived, beautiful, and have abundant happiness.’ The wish arises in them: ‘Oh, that on the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the company of the host of Valāhaka devas!’ On the breakup of the body, after death, that person is reborn into the company of the host of Valāhaka devas. This, monk, is the cause, this is the reason why a certain person here, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the host of Valāhaka devas.” Second.

3-12. Sītavalāhakadānūpakārasuttadasakaṃ

3-12. The Decad on the Benefit of Giving to the Cold-Cloud Devas

552-561. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ [P 3.0255] etadavoca [V 2.0252] – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sītavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṃ carati, vācāya sucaritaṃ carati, manasā sucaritaṃ carati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘sītavalāhakā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ [M 2.0215] hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sītavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So annaṃ deti…pe… padīpeyyaṃ deti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sītavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sītavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, by which a certain person here, on the breaking up of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the cold-cloud devas?” “Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices good conduct by body, speech, and mind. He has heard: ‘The cold-cloud devas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, may I, on the breaking up of the body, after death, be reborn into the company of the cold-cloud devas!’ He gives food... he gives lamps. He, on the breaking up of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the cold-cloud devas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which a certain person here, on the breaking up of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the cold-cloud devas.” The Twelfth.

13-52. Uṇhavalāhakadānūpakārasuttacālīsakaṃ

The Forty Discourses on the Benefit of Giving Regarding the Hot-Cloud Devas

562-601. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā uṇhavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ…pe… abbhavalāhakānaṃ [T 3.0316] devānaṃ…pe… vātavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ…pe… vassavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṃ carati, vācāya sucaritaṃ carati, manasā sucaritaṃ carati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘vassavalāhakā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā vassavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So annaṃ deti…pe… padīpeyyaṃ deti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā vassavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā vassavalāhakānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti. Dvepaññāsamaṃ.

At Sāvatthī.
