That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, by which a certain person here, on the breaking up of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the hot-cloud devas... the mist-cloud devas... the wind-cloud devas... the rain-cloud devas?” “Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices good conduct by body, speech, and mind. He has heard: ‘The rain-cloud devas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’ It occurs to him: ‘Oh, may I, on the breaking up of the body, after death, be reborn into the company of the rain-cloud devas!’ He gives food... he gives lamps. He, on the breaking up of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the rain-cloud devas. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which a certain person here, on the breaking up of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the rain-cloud devas.” The Fifty-second.

53. Sītavalāhakasuttaṃ

53. The Discourse on the Cold-Cloud Devas

602. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0256]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yenekadā sītaṃ hotī”ti? “Santi, bhikkhu, sītavalāhakā nāma devā. Tesaṃ yadā evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūna mayaṃ sakāya ratiyā vaseyyāmā’ti [V 2.0253] rameyyāmāti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) evamuparipi, tesaṃ taṃ cetopaṇidhimanvāya sītaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yenekadā sītaṃ hotī”ti. Tepaññāsamaṃ.

602. At Sāvatthī. That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, by which it is sometimes cold?” “There are, bhikkhu, devas named the cold-cloud devas. When it occurs to them: ‘Would that we might dwell in our own delight!’, then in accordance with that mental resolve of theirs, it becomes cold. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which it is sometimes cold.” The Fifty-third.

54. Uṇhavalāhakasuttaṃ

54. The Discourse on the Hot-Cloud Devas

603. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0317][M 2.0216]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yenekadā uṇhaṃ hotī”ti? “Santi, bhikkhu, uṇhavalāhakā nāma devā. Tesaṃ yadā evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūna mayaṃ sakāya ratiyā vaseyyāmā’ti, tesaṃ taṃ cetopaṇidhimanvāya uṇhaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yenekadā uṇhaṃ hotī”ti. Catupaññāsamaṃ.

603. At Sāvatthī. That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, what, indeed, is the cause, what is the condition, for which it is sometimes hot?” “Bhikkhu, there are devas named the Hot-Cloud devas. When the wish arises for them thus: ‘Would that we might dwell in our own delight!’—then, depending on that mental resolve of theirs, it becomes hot. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, for which it is sometimes hot.” The Fifty-fourth.

55. Abbhavalāhakasuttaṃ

55. The Discourse on the Mist-Cloud Devas

604. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yenekadā abbhaṃ hotī”ti? “Santi, bhikkhu, abbhavalāhakā nāma devā. Tesaṃ yadā evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūna mayaṃ sakāya ratiyā vaseyyāmā’ti, tesaṃ taṃ cetopaṇidhimanvāya abbhaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yenekadā abbhaṃ hotī”ti. Pañcapaññāsamaṃ.

604. At Sāvatthī. That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, what, indeed, is the cause, what is the condition, for which there is sometimes mist?” “Bhikkhu, there are devas named the Mist-Cloud devas. When the wish arises for them thus: ‘Would that we might dwell in our own delight!’—then, depending on that mental resolve of theirs, there is mist. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, for which there is sometimes mist.” The Fifty-fifth.

56. Vātavalāhakasuttaṃ

56. The Discourse on the Wind-Cloud Devas

605. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0254]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yenekadā vāto hotī”ti? “Santi, bhikkhu, vātavalāhakā nāma devā. Tesaṃ yadā [P 3.0257] evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūna mayaṃ sakāya ratiyā vaseyyāmā’ti, tesaṃ taṃ cetopaṇidhimanvāya vāto hoti. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yenekadā vāto hotī”ti. Chappaññāsamaṃ.

605. At Sāvatthī. That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, what, indeed, is the cause, what is the condition, for which there is sometimes wind?” “Bhikkhu, there are devas named the Wind-Cloud devas. When the wish arises for them thus: ‘Would that we might dwell in our own delight!’—then, depending on that mental resolve of theirs, there is wind. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, for which there is sometimes wind.” The Fifty-sixth.

57. Vassavalāhakasuttaṃ

57. The Discourse on the Rain-Cloud Devas

606. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [T 3.0318] – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yenekadā devo vassatī”ti? “Santi, bhikkhu, vassavalāhakā nāma devā. Tesaṃ yadā [M 2.0217] evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūna mayaṃ sakāya ratiyā vaseyyāmā’ti, tesaṃ taṃ cetopaṇidhimanvāya devo vassati. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yenekadā devo vassatī”ti. Sattapaññāsamaṃ.

606. At Sāvatthī. That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, by which it sometimes rains?” “Bhikkhu, there are devas named the Rain-Cloud devas. When for them there is this wish: ‘Would that we might dwell in our own delight!’ then, in accordance with that mental resolve of theirs, it rains. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which it sometimes rains.” The Fifty-seventh.

Sattapaññāsasuttantaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifty-seven discourses are concluded.

Valāhakasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Cloud Devas is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this is:

Suddhikaṃ sucaritañca dānūpakārapaññāsaṃ;

Sītaṃ uṇhañca abbhañca vātavassavalāhakāti.

The Simple, Good Conduct, and the fifty on the benefit of giving; Cold, Hot, Mist, Wind, and the Rain-Cloud devas.

12. Vacchagottasaṃyuttaṃ

12. The Connected Discourses with Vacchagotta

1. Rūpaaññāṇasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Ignorance of Form

607. Ekaṃ [T 3.0319][V 2.0255][M 2.0218] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ [P 3.0258] etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yānimāni yenimāni (?) anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti? “Rūpe kho, vaccha, aññāṇā, rūpasamudaye aññāṇā, rūpanirodhe aññāṇā, rūpanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇā; evamimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vāti. Ayaṃ kho, vaccha, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yānimāni yena (sī.), yenimāni (?) anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ [T 3.0320] maraṇāti vā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

607. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, what is the cause, what is the condition, why these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"; "The world is finite," or "The world is infinite"; "The life-principle and the body are the same," or "The life-principle is one thing and the body another"; "A Tathāgata exists after death," or "A Tathāgata does not exist after death," or "A Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death," or "A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death"?' 'Vaccha, it is through ignorance of form, ignorance of the origin of form, ignorance of the cessation of form, and ignorance of the practice leading to the cessation of form that these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal"... or "A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death." This, Vaccha, is the cause, this is the condition, why these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death."

2. Vedanāaññāṇasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Ignorance of Feeling

608. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni [V 2.0256] loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti? “Vedanāya kho, vaccha, aññāṇā, vedanāsamudaye aññāṇā, vedanānirodhe aññāṇā, vedanānirodhagāminiyā [M 2.0219] paṭipadāya aññāṇā; evamimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vāti. Ayaṃ kho, vaccha, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

608. At Sāvatthī. Sitting to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, what is the cause, what is the condition, why these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death"?' 'Vaccha, it is through ignorance of feeling, ignorance of the origin of feeling, ignorance of the cessation of feeling, and ignorance of the practice leading to the cessation of feeling that these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death." This, Vaccha, is the cause, this is the condition, why these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death."' The Second.

3. Saññāaññāṇasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Ignorance of Perception

609. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako [P 3.0259] bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti? “Saññāya kho, vaccha, aññāṇā, saññāsamudaye aññāṇā, saññānirodhe aññāṇā, saññānirodhagāminiyā [T 3.0321] paṭipadāya aññāṇā; evamimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vāti. Ayaṃ kho, vaccha, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

609. At Sāvatthī. Sitting to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, what is the cause, what is the condition, why these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death"?' 'Vaccha, it is through ignorance of perception, ignorance of the origin of perception, ignorance of the cessation of perception, and ignorance of the practice leading to the cessation of perception that these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death." This, Vaccha, is the cause, this is the condition, why these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death."' The Third.

4. Saṅkhāraaññāṇasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Ignorance of Formations

610. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti? “Saṅkhāresu kho, vaccha, aññāṇā, saṅkhārasamudaye [V 2.0257] aññāṇā, saṅkhāranirodhe aññāṇā, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇā; evamimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vāti. Ayaṃ kho, vaccha, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke [M 2.0220] uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

610. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, what is the cause, what is the condition, why these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death"?' 'Vaccha, it is through ignorance of formations, ignorance of the origin of formations, ignorance of the cessation of formations, and ignorance of the practice leading to the cessation of formations that these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death." This, Vaccha, is the cause, this is the condition, why these various speculative views arise in the world: "The world is eternal," or "The world is not eternal"... or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death."' The Fourth.

5. Viññāṇaaññāṇasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Ignorance of Consciousness

611. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0322]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā [P 3.0260] …pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti? “Viññāṇe kho, vaccha, aññāṇā, viññāṇasamudaye aññāṇā, viññāṇanirodhe aññāṇā, viññāṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇā; evamimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vāti. Ayaṃ kho, vaccha, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

611. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: “What, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition, for these various speculative views to arise in the world—‘the world is eternal,’ or ‘the world is not eternal’… or ‘after death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist’?” “It is, Vaccha, through not knowing consciousness, through not knowing the origin of consciousness, through not knowing the cessation of consciousness, and through not knowing the path leading to the cessation of consciousness that these various speculative views arise in the world—‘the world is eternal,’ or ‘the world is not eternal’… or ‘after death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist.’ This, Vaccha, is the cause, this is the condition, for these various speculative views to arise in the world—‘the world is eternal,’ or ‘the world is not eternal’… or ‘after death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist.’”

6-10. Rūpaadassanādisuttapañcakaṃ

6-10. The Five Discourses Beginning with Not Seeing Form.

612-616. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti? Rūpe kho, vaccha, adassanā…pe… rūpanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya adassanā…pe… vedanāya [V 2.0258]… saññāya [T 3.0323]… saṅkhāresu kho, vaccha, adassanā…pe… viññāṇe kho, vaccha, adassanā…pe… viññāṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya adassanā…pe…. Dasamaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: “What, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition, for these various speculative views to arise in the world—‘the world is eternal,’ or ‘the world is not eternal’… or ‘after death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist’?” “It is, Vaccha, through not seeing form… through not seeing the path leading to the cessation of form…. It is through not seeing feeling… perception… formations…. It is, Vaccha, through not seeing consciousness… and through not seeing the path leading to the cessation of consciousness that these various speculative views arise in the world….”

11-15. Rūpaanabhisamayādisuttapañcakaṃ

11-15. The Five Discourses Beginning with Non-Comprehension of Form.

617-621. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0221]. Rūpe kho, vaccha, anabhisamayā…pe… rūpanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya anabhisamayā…pe….

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through non-comprehension of form… and through non-comprehension of the path leading to the cessation of form….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Vedanāya kho, vaccha, anabhisamayā…pe….

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through non-comprehension of feeling….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0259]. Saññāya kho, vaccha, anabhisamayā…pe….

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through non-comprehension of perception….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Saṅkhāresu kho, vaccha, anabhisamayā…pe….

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through non-comprehension of volitional formations….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Viññāṇe kho, vaccha, anabhisamayā…pe…. Pannarasamaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through non-comprehension of consciousness….” Fifteenth.

16-20. Rūpaananubodhādisuttapañcakaṃ

16-20. The Five Discourses Beginning with Not Properly Knowing Form.

622-626. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0261]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo…pe… rūpe kho, vaccha, ananubodhā…pe… rūpanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ananubodhā…pe….

At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: “What, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition…?” “It is, Vaccha, through not properly knowing form… and through not properly knowing the practice leading to the cessation of form….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Vedanāya kho, vaccha…pe….

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through not properly knowing feeling….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Saññāya kho, vaccha…pe….

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through not properly knowing perception….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Saṅkhāresu kho, vaccha…pe….

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through not properly knowing volitional formations….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Viññāṇe kho, vaccha ananubodhā…pe… viññāṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ananubodhā. Vīsatimaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through not properly knowing consciousness… and through not properly knowing the practice leading to the cessation of consciousness.” Twentieth.

21-25. Rūpaappaṭivedhādisuttapañcakaṃ

21-25. The Five Discourses Beginning with Non-Penetration of Form.

627-631. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo…pe…[T 3.0324]. Rūpe kho, vaccha, appaṭivedhā…pe… viññāṇe kho, vaccha, appaṭivedhā…pe…. Pañcavīsatimaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “What, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition…?” “It is, Vaccha, through not penetrating form… and through not penetrating consciousness….” Twenty-fifth.

26-30. Rūpaasallakkhaṇādisuttapañcakaṃ

26-30. The Five Discourses Beginning with Not Marking Form Well.

632-636. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Rūpe kho, vaccha, asallakkhaṇā…pe… viññāṇe kho, vaccha, asallakkhaṇā…pe…. Tiṃsatimaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through not marking form well… and through not marking consciousness well….” Thirtieth.

31-35. Rūpaanupalakkhaṇādisuttapañcakaṃ

31-35. The Five Discourses Beginning with Not Properly Marking Form.

637-641. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0222]. Rūpe kho, vaccha, anupalakkhaṇā…pe… viññāṇe kho, vaccha, anupalakkhaṇā…pe…. Pañcatiṃsatimaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through not properly marking form… and through not properly marking consciousness….” Thirty-fifth.

36-40. Rūpaappaccupalakkhaṇādisuttapañcakaṃ

36-40. The Five Discourses Beginning with Not Recognizing Form When Present.

642-646. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0260]. Rūpe kho, vaccha, appaccupalakkhaṇā…pe… viññāṇe kho, vaccha, appaccupalakkhaṇā…pe…. Cattālīsamaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through not recognizing form when present… and through not recognizing consciousness when present….” Fortieth.

41-45. Rūpaasamapekkhaṇādisuttapañcakaṃ

41-45. The Five Discourses Beginning with Not Contemplating Form Well.

647-651. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Rūpe kho, vaccha, asamapekkhaṇā…pe… viññāṇe kho, vaccha, asamapekkhaṇā…pe…. Pañcacattālīsamaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through not contemplating form well… and through not contemplating consciousness well….” Forty-fifth.

46-50. Rūpaappaccupekkhaṇādisuttapañcakaṃ

46-50. The Five Discourses Beginning with Non-Reflection on Form.

652-656. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 3.0262]. Rūpe kho, vaccha, appaccupekkhaṇā…pe… viññāṇe kho, vaccha, appaccupekkhaṇā…pe…. Paññāsamaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, through non-reflection on form… and through non-reflection on consciousness….” Fiftieth.

51-54. Rūpaappaccakkhakammādisuttacatukkaṃ

51–54. Four Discourses Beginning with Not Directly Knowing Form.

657-660. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti? Rūpe kho, vaccha, appaccakkhakammā, rūpasamudaye appaccakkhakammā[T 3.0325], rūpanirodhe appaccakkhakammā, rūpanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya appaccakkhakammā…pe….

At Sāvatthī. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their courteous and amiable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: “What, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition, for these various kinds of speculative views to arise in the world—‘The world is eternal,’ or… ‘After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist’?” “It is, Vaccha, because of not directly knowing form, not directly knowing the origin of form, not directly knowing the cessation of form, and not directly knowing the path leading to the cessation of form….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0261]. Vedanāya kho, vaccha, appaccakkhakammā…pe… vedanānirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya appaccakkhakammā…pe….

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, because of not directly knowing feeling… and because of not directly knowing the path leading to the cessation of feeling….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Saññāya kho, vaccha, appaccakkhakammā…pe… saññānirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya appaccakkhakammā…pe….

At Sāvatthī. “It is, Vaccha, because of not directly knowing perception… and because of not directly knowing the path leading to the cessation of perception….”

Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0223]. Saṅkhāresu kho, vaccha, appaccakkhakammā…pe… saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya appaccakkhakammā…pe…. Catupaññāsamaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “Vaccha, it is because of not directly knowing volitional formations... because of not directly knowing the way leading to the cessation of volitional formations…. The Fifty-fourth.”

55. Viññāṇaappaccakkhakammasuttaṃ

55. The Discourse on Not Directly Knowing Consciousness

661. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Viññāṇe kho, vaccha, appaccakkhakammā, viññāṇasamudaye appaccakkhakammā, viññāṇanirodhe appaccakkhakammā, viññāṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya appaccakkhakammā; evamimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti [P 3.0263] – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vāti. Ayaṃ kho, vaccha, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo[T 3.0326], yānimāni anekavihitāni diṭṭhigatāni loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti. Pañcapaññāsamaṃ.

661. At Sāvatthī. “Vaccha, it is because of not directly realizing consciousness, not directly realizing the origin of consciousness, not directly realizing the cessation of consciousness, not directly realizing the practice leading to the cessation of consciousness, that these various kinds of speculative views arise in the world: ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal,’… ‘After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist.’ This, Vaccha, is the cause, this is the condition, for the arising in the world of these various kinds of speculative views: ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal’; ‘The world is finite,’ or ‘The world is infinite’; ‘The life-principle is the same as the body,’ or ‘The life-principle is one thing and the body is another’; ‘After death a Tathāgata exists,’ or ‘After death a Tathāgata does not exist,’ or ‘After death a Tathāgata both exists and does not exist,’ or ‘After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist.’” The Fifty-fifth.

Vacchagottasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Vacchagotta Saṃyutta is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Aññāṇā adassanā ceva, anabhisamayā ananubodhā;

Appaṭivedhā asallakkhaṇā, anupalakkhaṇena appaccupalakkhaṇā;

Asamapekkhaṇā appaccupekkhaṇā, appaccakkhakammanti.

Ignorance and not seeing, not comprehending, not awakening; not penetrating, not discerning, by not observing, not directly observing; not considering, not directly considering, and not directly realizing.

13. Jhānasaṃyuttaṃ

13. The Jhāna Saṃyutta

1. Samādhimūlakasamāpattisuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Attainment Rooted in Concentration

662. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 3.0327][V 2.0262][M 2.0224]. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha[P 3.0264], bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho pāmokkho (syā. kaṃ.) evamuparipi ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṃ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo tatra aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

662. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four jhāna-attainers. Which four? Here, bhikkhus, one jhāna-attainer is skilled in concentration but not skilled in attainment. Here, bhikkhus, one jhāna-attainer is skilled in attainment but not skilled in concentration. Here, bhikkhus, one jhāna-attainer is skilled neither in concentration nor in attainment. Here, bhikkhus, one jhāna-attainer is skilled both in concentration and in attainment. Among these four jhāna-attainers, bhikkhus, the one who is skilled both in concentration and in attainment is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk, from milk comes curd, from curd comes fresh butter, from fresh butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes the cream of ghee, which is said to be the foremost among them; in the same way, bhikkhus, the jhāna-attainer who is skilled both in concentration and in attainment is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent of these four jhāna-attainers.” The first.

2. Samādhimūlakaṭhitisuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Stability Rooted in Concentration

663. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco [T 3.0328] jhāyī samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti[V 2.0263], samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ [P 3.0265] catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṃ, navanītamhā [M 2.0225] sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo tatra aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

663. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four jhāna-attainers. Which four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in concentration, but not skilled in maintaining concentration. Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in maintaining concentration, but not skilled in concentration. Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is neither skilled in concentration nor skilled in maintaining concentration. Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in concentration and is also skilled in maintaining concentration. Among these four jhāna-attainers, bhikkhus, the one who is skilled in concentration and is also skilled in maintaining concentration is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk, from milk comes curd, from curd comes fresh butter, from fresh butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes cream of ghee—which is said to be the foremost; even so, bhikkhus, among these four jhāna-attainers, the one who is skilled in concentration and is also skilled in maintaining concentration is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent.” The Second.

3. Samādhimūlakavuṭṭhānasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Arising Rooted in Concentration

664. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ [T 3.0329] jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

664. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four jhāna-attainers. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in concentration, but not skilled in emerging from concentration. Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in emerging from concentration, but not skilled in concentration. Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is neither skilled in concentration nor skilled in emerging from concentration. Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in concentration and is also skilled in emerging from concentration. Among these four jhāna-attainers, bhikkhus, the one who is skilled in concentration and is also skilled in emerging from concentration is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk… and is the most excellent.” The Third.

4. Samādhimūlakakallitasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Refinement Rooted in Concentration

665. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha [P 3.0266] pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca [V 2.0264] mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

665. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four jhāna-attainers. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration, but not skilled in making concentration suitable. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in making concentration suitable, but not skilled in the constituents of concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is neither skilled in the constituents of concentration nor skilled in making concentration suitable. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration and is also skilled in making concentration suitable. Among them, bhikkhus, that jhāna-attainer who is skilled in the constituents of concentration and is also skilled in making concentration suitable—this one, among these four jhāna-attainers, is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk… and is the most excellent.”

5. Samādhimūlakaārammaṇasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Object Rooted in Concentration

666. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0226]. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo [T 3.0330] ca hoti, samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

666. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four jhāna-attainers. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration, but not skilled in the object for concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the object for concentration, but not skilled in the constituents of concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is neither skilled in the constituents of concentration nor skilled in the object for concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration and is also skilled in the object for concentration. Among them, bhikkhus, that jhāna-attainer who is skilled in the constituents of concentration and is also skilled in the object for concentration—this one, among these four jhāna-attainers, is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk… and is the most excellent.”

6. Samādhimūlakagocarasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Range Rooted in Concentration

667. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha [P 3.0267] pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

667. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four jhāna-attainers. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration, but not skilled in the range for concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the range for concentration, but not skilled in the constituents of concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is neither skilled in the constituents of concentration nor skilled in the range for concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration and is also skilled in the range for concentration. Among them, bhikkhus, that jhāna-attainer who is skilled in the constituents of concentration and is also skilled in the range for concentration—this one, among these four jhāna-attainers, is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk… and is the most excellent.”

7. Samādhimūlakaabhinīhārasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Directing Rooted in Concentration

668. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0265]. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha [M 2.0227] pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo[T 3.0331]. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

668. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four jhāna-attainers. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration, but is not skilled in directing the mind in concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in directing the mind in concentration, but is not skilled in the constituents of concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is neither skilled in the constituents of concentration nor skilled in directing the mind in concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration and is also skilled in directing the mind in concentration. Among these, bhikkhus, that jhāna-attainer who is skilled in the constituents of concentration and is also skilled in directing the mind in concentration—this one, among these four jhāna-attainers, is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk... and is the most excellent.”

8. Samādhimūlakasakkaccakārīsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Reverential Action Rooted in Concentration

669. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī. Idha [P 3.0268] pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

669. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four jhāna-attainers. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration, but does not act with reverence in concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer acts with reverence in concentration, but is not skilled in the constituents of concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is neither skilled in the constituents of concentration nor acts with reverence in concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in the constituents of concentration and also acts with reverence in concentration. Among these, bhikkhus, that jhāna-attainer who is skilled in the constituents of concentration and also acts with reverence in concentration—this one, among these four jhāna-attainers, is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk... and is the most excellent.”

9. Samādhimūlakasātaccakārīsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Persistence Rooted in Concentration

670. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha pana[V 2.0266], bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva [T 3.0332] samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Navamaṃ.

670. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in concentration but does not practice it persistently. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator practices concentration persistently but is not skilled in concentration. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is neither skilled in concentration nor practices it persistently. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is both skilled in concentration and practices it persistently. Among these four meditators, bhikkhus, the one who is both skilled in concentration and practices it persistently is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk… and is the most excellent.” The ninth.

10. Samādhimūlakasappāyakārīsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Conducive Practice Rooted in Concentration

671. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0228]. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī. Idha [P 3.0269] pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Dasamaṃ. (Samādhimūlakaṃ.)

671. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in concentration, but does not practice what is conducive to it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator practices what is conducive to concentration, but is not skilled in it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is neither skilled in concentration nor practices what is conducive to it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is both skilled in concentration and practices what is conducive to it. Among these four meditators, bhikkhus, the one who is both skilled in concentration and practices what is conducive to it is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk… and is the most excellent.” The tenth. (The Section Rooted in Concentration.)

11. Samāpattimūlakaṭhitisuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on Stability Rooted in Attainment

672. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco [T 3.0333] jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

672. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration, but not skilled in maintaining it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in maintaining concentration, but not skilled in attaining it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled neither in attaining concentration nor in maintaining it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled both in attaining concentration and in maintaining it. Among these four meditators, bhikkhus, the one who is skilled both in attaining concentration and in maintaining it is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk… and is the most excellent.” The eleventh.

12. Samāpattimūlakavuṭṭhānasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on Emerging, Rooted in Attainment

673. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0267]. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na ca [M 2.0229] samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo [P 3.0270] ca hoti, samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī …pe… pavaro cā”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

673. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration, but not skilled in emerging from it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in emerging from concentration, but not skilled in attaining it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled neither in attaining concentration nor in emerging from it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled both in attaining concentration and in emerging from it. Among these four meditators, bhikkhus, the one who is skilled both in attaining concentration and in emerging from it… is the most excellent.” The twelfth.

13. Samāpattimūlakakallitasuttaṃ

13. The Discourse on Readiness, Rooted in Attainment

674. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo [T 3.0334] ca hoti, samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo ca. Tatra…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Terasamaṃ.

674. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration, but not skilled in the readiness of concentration. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in the readiness of concentration, but not skilled in attaining it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled neither in attaining concentration nor in the readiness of concentration. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled both in attaining concentration and in the readiness of concentration. Among these… is the most excellent.” The thirteenth.

14. Samāpattimūlakaārammaṇasuttaṃ

14. The Discourse on the Object, Rooted in Attainment

675. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo ca. Tatra…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Cuddasamaṃ.

675. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration but not skilled in its object. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in the object of concentration but not skilled in attaining it. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled neither in attaining concentration nor in its object. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled both in attaining concentration and in its object. Among these… is the most excellent.” The fourteenth.

15. Samāpattimūlakagocarasuttaṃ

15. The Discourse on the Range, Rooted in Attainment

676. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0268]. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo [P 3.0271] hoti, na samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo [M 2.0230] ca hoti, samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo ca. Tatra…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Pannarasamaṃ.

676. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration but is not skilled in the meditation subject of concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in the meditation subject of concentration but is not skilled in attaining concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is neither skilled in attaining concentration nor skilled in the meditation subject of concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration and is also skilled in the meditation subject of concentration. Among these… is the most excellent.” Fifteenth.

16. Samāpattimūlakaabhinīhārasuttaṃ

16. The Discourse on Application, Rooted in Attainment

677. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ [T 3.0335] abhinīhārakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo ca. Tatra…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Soḷasamaṃ.

677. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration but is not skilled in applying it. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in applying concentration but is not skilled in attaining it. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is neither skilled in attaining concentration nor skilled in applying it. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration and is also skilled in applying it. Among these… is the most excellent.” Sixteenth.

17. Samāpattimūlakasakkaccasuttaṃ

17. The Discourse on Reverence, Rooted in Attainment

678. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī ca. Tatra…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Sattarasamaṃ.

678. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration but does not practice concentration with reverence. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator practices concentration with reverence but is not skilled in attaining concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is neither skilled in attaining concentration nor practices concentration with reverence. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration and also practices concentration with reverence. Among these… is the most excellent.” Seventeenth.

18. Samāpattimūlakasātaccasuttaṃ

18. The Discourse on Sustained Practice, Rooted in Attainment

679. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0269]. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo [T 3.0336] ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī ca. Tatra…pe… pavaro cā”ti. Aṭṭhārasamaṃ.

679. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration but is not constant in concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is constant in concentration but is not skilled in attaining concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is neither skilled in attaining concentration nor constant in concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration and is also constant in concentration. Among these… is the most excellent.” Eighteenth.

19. Samāpattimūlakasappāyakārīsuttaṃ

19. The Discourse on Suitable Actions, Rooted in Attainment

680. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0231]. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha[P 3.0272], bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṃ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo tatra aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Ekūnavīsatimaṃ. (Samāpattimūlakaṃ.)

680. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in attaining concentration but not in what is conducive to concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in what is conducive to concentration but not in attaining concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled neither in attaining concentration nor in what is conducive to concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled both in attaining concentration and in what is conducive to concentration. Among these, bhikkhus, that meditator who is skilled both in attaining concentration and in what is conducive to concentration is, of these four meditators, the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk; from milk, curd; from curd, fresh butter; from fresh butter, ghee; and from ghee, the cream of ghee—among these, the cream of ghee is said to be the foremost; even so, bhikkhus, that meditator who is skilled both in attaining concentration and in what is conducive to concentration is, of these four meditators, the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent.” Nineteenth. (Rooted in Attainment.)

20-27. Ṭhitimūlakavuṭṭhānasuttādiaṭṭhakaṃ

20-27. The Octad Beginning with the Sutta on Emergence Rooted in Stability

681-688. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave[V 2.0270], ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco [T 3.0337] jhāyī samādhismiṃ ṭhitikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī…pe… uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Vīsatimaṃ. (Purimamūlakāni viya yāva sattavīsatimā ṭhitimūlakasappāyakārīsuttā aṭṭha suttāni pūretabbāni. Ṭhitimūlakaṃ[P 3.0273].)

At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of meditators. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in stability in concentration but not skilled in emerging from concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in emerging from concentration but not skilled in stability in concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is neither skilled in stability in concentration nor skilled in emerging from concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain meditator is skilled in stability in concentration and is also skilled in emerging from concentration. Among these, bhikkhus, that meditator… is supreme and preeminent.” Twentieth. (Like the preceding roots, the eight suttas up to the twenty-seventh, the Sutta on Doing What is Suitable Rooted in Stability, should be completed. The Stability Root.)

28-34. Vuṭṭhānamūlakakallitasuttādisattakaṃ

28-34. The Heptad Beginning with the Sutta on Suitability Rooted in Emergence

689-695. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo hoti, na [M 2.0232] samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo… samādhismiṃ [P 3.0274] kallitakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo… neva samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo… samādhismiṃ vuṭṭhānakusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī…pe… uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Aṭṭhavīsatimaṃ. (Purimamūlakāni viya yāva catuttiṃsatimā vuṭṭhānamūlakasappāyakārīsuttā satta suttāni pūretabbāni. Vuṭṭhānamūlakaṃ.)

At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of jhana-attainers. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhana-attainer is skilled in emerging from concentration, but not skilled in adapting concentration... is skilled in adapting concentration, but not skilled in emerging from concentration... is neither skilled in emerging from concentration nor skilled in adapting concentration... is skilled in emerging from concentration and is also skilled in adapting concentration. Among these, bhikkhus, that jhana-attainer... is supreme and preeminent.' The twenty-eighth. (Like the preceding root sections, the seven suttas up to the thirty-fourth, the Sutta on Doing What is Suitable Rooted in Emergence, should be completed. The Emergence Root.)

35-40. Kallitamūlakaārammaṇasuttādichakkaṃ

35-40. The Hexad Beginning with the Sutta on the Object, Rooted in Adapting.

696-701. Sāvatthinidānaṃ [P 3.0275]… “samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo… samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo… neva samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo… samādhismiṃ kallitakusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī…pe… uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Pañcatiṃsatimaṃ. (Purimamūlakāni viya yāva cattālīsamā kallitamūlakasappāyakārīsuttā cha suttāni pūretabbāni. Kallitamūlakaṃ.)

At Sāvatthī... 'One is skilled in adapting concentration, but not skilled in the object of concentration... One is skilled in the object of concentration, but not skilled in adapting concentration... One is neither skilled in adapting concentration nor skilled in the object of concentration... One is both skilled in adapting concentration and skilled in the object of concentration. Among these, bhikkhus, that jhana-attainer... is supreme and preeminent.' The thirty-fifth. (Like the preceding root sections, the six suttas up to the fortieth, the Sutta on Doing What is Suitable Rooted in Adapting, should be completed. The Adapting Root.)

41-45. Ārammaṇamūlakagocarasuttādipañcakaṃ

41-45. The Pentad Beginning with the Sutta on Range, Rooted in the Object.

702-706. Sāvatthinidānaṃ [V 2.0271]… “samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo… samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo… neva samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ [T 3.0338] gocarakusalo… samādhismiṃ ārammaṇakusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī…pe… uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Ekacattālīsamaṃ. (Purimamūlakāni viya yāva pañcacattālīsamā ārammaṇamūlakasappāyakārīsuttā pañca suttāni pūretabbāni. Ārammaṇamūlakaṃ[P 3.0276].)

At Sāvatthī... 'One is skilled in the object of concentration, but not skilled in the range of concentration... One is skilled in the range of concentration, but not skilled in the object of concentration... One is neither skilled in the object of concentration nor skilled in the range of concentration... One is both skilled in the object of concentration and skilled in the range of concentration. Among these, bhikkhus, that jhana-attainer... is supreme and preeminent.' The forty-first. (Like the preceding root sections, the five suttas up to the forty-fifth, the Sutta on Doing What is Suitable Rooted in the Object, should be completed. The Object Root.)

46-49. Gocaramūlakaabhinīhārasuttādicatukkaṃ

46-49. The Tetrad Beginning with the Sutta on Application, Rooted in Range.

707. Sāvatthinidānaṃ… “samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo… samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo hoti[M 2.0233], na samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo… neva samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo… samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo ca… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṃ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo tatra aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo ca hoti samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ…pe… uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Chacattālīsamaṃ.

707. At Sāvatthī... 'One is skilled in the range of concentration, but not skilled in the application of concentration... one is skilled in the application of concentration, but not skilled in the range of concentration... one is neither skilled in the range of concentration nor skilled in the application of concentration... one is both skilled in the range of concentration and skilled in the application of concentration. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk; from milk, curds; from curds, fresh butter; from fresh butter, ghee; and from ghee, the cream of ghee, which is said to be the best; so too, bhikkhus, that jhana-attainer who is skilled in the range of concentration and also skilled in the application of concentration is the supreme and preeminent among these four jhana-attainers.' The forty-sixth.

708. Samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī…pe…. Vitthāretabbaṃ. Sattacattālīsamaṃ.

708. 'One is skilled in the range of concentration, but not conscientious in concentration... (This should be elaborated in full.)' The forty-seventh.

709. Samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī…pe…. Aṭṭhacattālīsamaṃ.

709. 'One is skilled in the range of concentration, but not constant in concentration...' The forty-eighth.

710. Samādhismiṃ gocarakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī…pe…. Ekūnapaññāsamaṃ. (Gocaramūlakaṃ.)

710. 'One is skilled in the range of concentration, but does not act suitably in concentration...' The forty-ninth. (The Range Root.)

50-52. Abhinīhāramūlakasakkaccasuttāditikaṃ

50-52. The Triad Beginning with the Sutta on Conscientiousness, Rooted in Application.

711. Sāvatthinidānaṃ [V 2.0272]… “samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo hoti, na [P 3.0277] samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī… samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo… neva samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī… samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī…pe… uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Paññāsamaṃ.

711. At Sāvatthī... 'One is skilled in the application of concentration, but not conscientious in concentration... one is conscientious in concentration, but not skilled in the application of concentration... one is neither skilled in the application of concentration nor conscientious in concentration... one is both skilled in the application of concentration and conscientious in concentration. Among these, bhikkhus, that jhana-attainer... is supreme and preeminent.' The fiftieth.

712. Samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī…pe…. Ekapaññāsamaṃ.

712. 'One is skilled in the application of concentration, but not constant in concentration...' The fifty-first.

713. Samādhismiṃ abhinīhārakusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī…pe…. Dvepaññāsamaṃ. (Abhinīhāramūlakaṃ.)

713. 'One is skilled in the application of concentration, but does not act suitably in concentration...' The fifty-second. (The Application Root.)

53-54. Sakkaccamūlakasātaccakārīsuttādidukaṃ

53-54. The Dyad Beginning with the Sutta on Constancy, Rooted in Conscientiousness.

714. Sāvatthinidānaṃ [M 2.0234]… “samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī… samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī [T 3.0339]… neva samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī… samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ…pe… uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Tepaññāsamaṃ.

714. At Sāvatthī... 'One is conscientious in concentration, but not constant in concentration... one is constant in concentration, but not conscientious in concentration... one is neither conscientious in concentration nor constant in concentration... one is both conscientious in concentration and constant in concentration. Among these, bhikkhus, that jhana-attainer... is supreme and preeminent.' The fifty-third.

715. Samādhismiṃ sakkaccakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī…pe…. Catupaññāsamaṃ.

715. 'One is conscientious in concentration, but does not act suitably in concentration...' The fifty-fourth.

55. Sātaccamūlakasappāyakārīsuttaṃ

55. The Sutta on Suitable Action, Rooted in Constancy.

716. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Catārome, bhikkhave, jhāyī. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave[V 2.0273], ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī hoti, na samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī. Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī hoti, na ca samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī. Idha [P 3.0278] pana, bhikkhave, ekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī ca. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī ca hoti samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī ca ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṃ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṃ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo tatra aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ jhāyī samādhismiṃ sātaccakārī ca hoti, samādhismiṃ sappāyakārī ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti. Pañcapaññāsamaṃ. (Yathā pañcapaññāsaṃ veyyākaraṇāni honti tathā vitthāretabbāni.)

716. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, there are these four jhāna-attainers. Which four? Here, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in persistence regarding concentration but not skilled in what is suitable for concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is skilled in what is suitable for concentration but not skilled in persistence regarding concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is neither skilled in persistence regarding concentration nor skilled in what is suitable for concentration. Again, bhikkhus, a certain jhāna-attainer is both skilled in persistence regarding concentration and skilled in what is suitable for concentration. Bhikkhus, among these four jhāna-attainers, the one who is both skilled in persistence regarding concentration and skilled in what is suitable for concentration is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent. Just as, bhikkhus, from a cow comes milk, from milk curds, from curds fresh butter, from fresh butter ghee, and from ghee the cream of ghee, which is said to be the foremost among them; even so, bhikkhus, that jhāna-attainer who is both skilled in persistence regarding concentration and skilled in what is suitable for concentration is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent among these four jhāna-attainers.' The Blessed One said this. Those bhikkhus, being satisfied, delighted in the Blessed One’s words. The fifty-fifth. (The prose discourses should be elaborated in the same way as the fifty-five.)

Jhānasaṃyuttaṃ samādhisaṃyuttaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) samattaṃ.

The Saṃyutta on Jhāna is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Samādhi [T 3.0340][M 2.0235] samāpatti ṭhiti ca, vuṭṭhānaṃ kallitārammaṇena ca;

Gocarā abhinīhāro sakkacca, sātacca athopi sappāyanti.

Concentration, Attainment, and Steadiness, Emergence, Malleability, and with Object; Range, Application, Conscientiousness, Persistence, and also Suitability.

Khandhavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter: The Division on the Aggregates.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Khandha rādhasaṃyuttañca, diṭṭhiokkanta okkanti (sabbattha) uppādā;

Kilesa sāriputtā ca, nāgā supaṇṇa gandhabbā;

Valāha vacchajhānanti[P 3.0279], khandhavaggamhi terasāti.

The Aggregates, the Connected Discourses with Rādhā, Views, Entering, Arising, Defilements, Sāriputta, Nāgas, Supaṇṇas, Gandhabba, Clouds, Vacchas, and Jhāna—thirteen in the Division on the Aggregates.

Khandhavaggasaṃyuttapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāḷi of the Connected Discourses of the Division on the Aggregates is concluded.
